body.text:
A Pramāṇavārttikaṭīkā
r1 /// .. daḥ ayaṃ ca vikalpabuddhyāropitatvād asamīkṣitatatvārthḥ / anapekṣitas tatvārtho vastvartho yeneti vigrahaḥ / yathā loke buddhyārūḍho 'py adhyavasitatadbhāvatayā pratīyate / taṃ dharmādivibhāgaṃ tatheti lokapratītivat* / sādhyasādhanasaṃsthitir vidvadbhir avakalpyata iti saṃbandhaḥ / kim arthaṃ para ///
body.translated_text:
A. <s>Pramāṇavārttikaṭīkā</s>
[Folio r1] /// ...and this, because it is superimposed by <s>vikalpa</s> (conceptual cognition), has its real nature unexamined. The analysis is: 'by whom the true nature of reality, the object as it is, is disregarded.' Just as in the world, even what is grasped by cognition is cognized as being determined to be that very thing — that division into <s>dharma</s> (property) and so forth is accepted as such, like worldly cognition. The establishment of <s>sādhya</s> (what is to be proved) and <s>sādhana</s> (the means of proof) was devised by the learned — such is the connection. For what purpose does the opponent... ///

body.text: 2 /// .. ya / kiṃ punaḥ kāraṇam ekatvādivyavahārasya vastuny asaṃbhava ity ata āha / saṃsṛjyanta ityādi pāramārthikāḥ arthāḥ svato na saṃsṛyante tato na sāmānyavyavahāro vastuni / na bhidyante kṛtakatvādibhir dharmaiḥ pratyekaṃ tasya vastuno 'nekatvāyogāt* ataś ca teṣv artheṣu bahuṣu rūpam ekaṃ / ekasmin vārthe 'nekaṃ rūpaṃ yad adhyavasīyate tad buddher vika ///
body.translated_text: [Folio 2] /// ...moreover, what is the reason that the convention of unity and so forth is impossible in reality? To this he says: 'They do not combine,' and so forth. Ultimate objects do not combine of themselves; therefore, the convention of universality does not apply to reality. Nor are they differentiated by properties such as being produced, since it is impossible for each individual real thing to be many. And thus, among those multiple objects, a single form, or in a single object, multiple forms — whatever is determined is a <s>vikalpa</s> (construction) of cognition... ///

body.text: 3 /// .. nte / na bhidyante pāramārthikā arthās tataḥ kāraṇāt* / sāmānyam idaṃ bahūnāṃ / tathā dharmāṇāṃ dharmiṇāṃ ca bheda ity api yo 'yaṃ bhedo nānātvavyavahāraḥ / sa bauddhe 'rthe na bāhye svalakṣaṇe buddhipratibhāsasyālīkatvāt kathaṃ tatra kṛtakatvādidharmabheda iti ced āha / tasyaiva cetyādi / buddhipratibhāsasyaiva etad uktaṃ bhavati bāhyenaikatvādhyavasāyā ///
body.translated_text: [Folio 3] /// ...they are not differentiated — ultimate objects are not differentiated. For that reason: 'this is a universal of many things.' Likewise, the differentiation of <s>dharmas</s> (properties) and <s>dharmins</s> (property-bearers) — this differentiation, this convention of plurality — pertains to the object as understood by <s>buddhi</s> (cognition), not to the external <s>svalakṣaṇa</s> (particular), since the appearance in cognition is false. If one objects: 'How then can there be differentiation of properties such as being produced?' — he answers: 'Of that very...' and so forth. This means: it is of the appearance in cognition itself. Through the external, the determination of unity... ///

body.text: 4 /// thā taddarśanāyāto 'pi vikalpapratibhāso 'dhyavasīyata iti / ata evāha prakalpyata iti / yathā pratyakṣeṇa vastusvalakṣaṇam eva gṛhyate tathā sādhanānumitenānityatvādinā sādhyadharmeṇa viśiṣṭaṃ svalakṣaṇam eva kasmān na gṛhyata ity āha sādhyetyādi / idaṃ sādhyam idaṃ sādhanam ity asmin saṃkalpe vastudarśanahānitaḥ kutaḥ sva ///
body.translated_text: [Folio 4] /// ...thus, the appearance of <s>vikalpa</s> (conceptual construction) that comes for perceiving that is also determined. Therefore he says: 'It is constructed.' Just as in <s>pratyakṣa</s> (perception), only the <s>svalakṣaṇa</s> (particular) of the real thing is grasped, so too why is not the <s>svalakṣaṇa</s> qualified by the <s>sādhya</s>-property such as impermanence, which is established through the <s>sādhana</s>-inference, grasped in the same way? He answers: 'The <s>sādhya</s>...' and so forth. In this conception that 'this is the <s>sādhya</s>, this is the <s>sādhana</s>' — because of the loss of seeing the real thing — whence the particular... ///

body.text: 5 /// .. nyāpohaviśiṣṭo bhedo gṛhyata ity abhidhānād ācāryadiṅnāgaprabhṛtiḥ svalakṣaṇasya sāmānyasaṃsṛṣṭasya grahaṇaṃ / pratijñātam ity āśaṅkām apanayann āha bheda ityādi / bhedaḥ sāmānyasaṃsṛṣṭaḥ pratīyata ity atrāpi vacane grāhyaṃ na svalakṣaṇaṃ svalakṣaṇam eva nirdiṣṭam iti naivaṃ boddhavyam ity arthaḥ / .. .. .. ddhisanniceśina eva bhe ///
body.translated_text: [Folio 5] /// ...because it has been stated that differentiation qualified by <s>anyāpoha</s> (exclusion of the other) is grasped, the master <s>Dignāga</s> and others have asserted the apprehension of the <s>svalakṣaṇa</s> (particular) as mixed with the <s>sāmānya</s> (universal). Dispelling this apprehension, he says: 'Differentiation...' and so forth. Even in this statement that 'differentiation mixed with universality is cognized,' what is grasped is not the <s>svalakṣaṇa</s>. One should not understand it as: 'the <s>svalakṣaṇa</s> itself has been indicated.' This is the meaning... cognition's settling on the very differentiation... ///

body.text: v1 /// ṣṭā gṛhyanta iti tatrāpi boddhavyaṃ / anye tu bhedaḥ sāmānyaṃ saṃsṛṣṭo grāhya iti pulliṅgena paṭhanti / tatrāyam artho bhedaḥ / sāmānyasaṃsṛṣṭo grāhya ity atrāpi vacane na svalakṣaṇaṃ boddhavyaṃ iti / kiṃ punaḥ kāraṇaṃ tatraivaṃ boddhavyam iti ced āha samānetyādi / anekasminn ekatvā ///
body.translated_text: [Folio v1] /// ...those qualified are grasped — thus it should be understood there also. Others, however, read with the masculine form: 'differentiation, mixed with universality, is the graspable.' In that case, the meaning is: differentiation, mixed with the universal, is the graspable — even in this statement, one should not understand it as the <s>svalakṣaṇa</s>. If one asks what the reason is that it should be understood thus there, he answers: 'Of the same...' and so forth. In many things, of unity... ///

body.text: 2 /// .. sminn upādhibahutvaṃ bhinnākāraḥ ādiśabdād dharmadharmyākāraparigrahaḥ / na tat svalakṣaṇagrāhyaṃ kathaṃcana kiṃ kāraṇaṃ tatraikasmiṃ svalakṣaṇe kṛtakatvānityatvādirūpeṇa bahubhedānān dharmāṇāṃ kiṃ viśiṣṭānāṃ bhedānāṃ vasturūpāṇāṃ tatraikasmin svalakṣaṇe 'yogāt* / na hy ekasmin vastuni vasturūpāṇi bahūni yujyante niraṃśatvāt* svalakṣaṇa ///
body.translated_text: [Folio 2] /// ...in a single thing, the plurality of conditions — 'of different aspects,' and by the word 'and so forth' (ādi), the inclusion of the aspects of <s>dharma</s> (property) and <s>dharmin</s> (property-bearer). That is not graspable as a <s>svalakṣaṇa</s> (particular) in any way. For what reason? Because in that single <s>svalakṣaṇa</s>, the many differentiations of properties such as being produced, being impermanent, and so forth — these differentiations which are of the nature of real things — are impossible in that single <s>svalakṣaṇa</s>. For many real forms in a single real thing are impossible, due to the partless nature of the <s>svalakṣaṇa</s>... ///

body.text: 3 /// .. .. .. .. tatprātipādikā śrutir iti asādhāraṇena rūpeṇa tasya svalakṣaṇasya pratipādakaḥ śabdo nāsti kalpanā vāsti nety prakṛtaṃ / asādhāraṇena rūpeṇa svalakṣaṇasya grāhako vikalpāpi nāstīty arthaḥ / kiṃ kāraṇaṃ sāmānyenaiva śabdasya kalpanāyāś ca vṛttitaḥ tatpratipādikā na śrutir astīti bruvatā svalakṣaṇe ///
body.translated_text: [Folio 3] /// ...the verbal expression whose basis is that — thus there is no word that designates that <s>svalakṣaṇa</s> by its unique form, nor is there <s>kalpanā</s> (conceptual construction), or there is not — this is the topic. There is no <s>vikalpa</s> (conceptual cognition) either that grasps the <s>svalakṣaṇa</s> by its unique form. This is the meaning. For what reason? Because words and conceptual construction operate only through the <s>sāmānya</s> (universal) — by saying that there is no verbal expression that designates the <s>svalakṣaṇa</s> [by its unique form], regarding the <s>svalakṣaṇa</s>... ///

body.text: 4 /// punar ityādi / na tu sāmānyenaiva vṛttita ity anantaram uktatvād ayuktaṃ codyaṃ / satyam etad adhikaṃ tu parihāram abhidhātum upanyāsaḥ saṃketenaa viṣayīkṛtaḥ saṃketitas tam āhuḥ śabdāḥ vyavahārāya sa smṛta iti saṃketaḥ / yasmin svalakṣaṇe saṃketaḥ kriyata itīṣyate / tata svalakṣaṇaṃ tadā vyavahārakāle nāsti na hi saṃketa ///
body.translated_text: [Folio 4] /// ...'Moreover,' and so forth. But since it has just been stated that they operate only through the universal, the objection is unfounded. True, but in order to state an additional response, the introduction [continues]: <s>saṃketa</s> (linguistic convention) — 'that which has been made the object of convention, the conventionally designated — words convey it for the purpose of communication; that is remembered.' The <s>saṃketa</s> (convention) — on whichever <s>svalakṣaṇa</s> (particular) the convention is established, it is accepted. But that <s>svalakṣaṇa</s> does not exist at the time of verbal usage. For indeed the convention... ///

body.text: 5 /// .. .. / .. .. .. pasya vyaktyantare saṃbhavābhāvāt* yāpy ekā vyaktiḥ saṃketaviṣayatvenābhimatā tasyā api kṣaṇikatvāt* / kālāntare tenaiva rūpeṇānugamo nāsti kim uta deśakālabhinne vyaktyantare / tena kāraṇena tatra svalakṣaṇe saṃketo na kriyata ity adhyāhāraḥ na hītyādinā vyācaṣṭe / prāg iti saṃketakāle kṛ ///
body.translated_text: [Folio 5] /// ...because of the impossibility of its occurrence in another instance. Even the single instance which is accepted as the object of convention, due to its <s>kṣaṇikatva</s> (momentariness), its continuity in the same form at another time does not exist — how much less so in another instance differing in place and time. For that reason, convention is not established in that <s>svalakṣaṇa</s> — this is to be supplied. He explains with 'For not...' and so forth. 'Previously' means at the time of convention... ///

body.text:
B Pramāṇavārttikaṭīkā
r1 /// .. .. kiñcid vastu .. .. .. .. .. anyatreti yatra vyaktibhede tayā āskantavyaṃ / etac cānyatra sata iti vastubhūtasya sāmānyasya na saṃbhavatīti saṃbandhaḥ / kiṃ kāraṇam āśrayād ananyatrve 'bhyupagamyamāne 'nvayābhāvān na hy ekasmād avyatiriktas tadātmabhūto .. .. .. .. ///
body.translated_text:
B. <s>Pramāṇavārttikaṭīkā</s>
[Folio r1] /// ...some real thing... elsewhere, meaning where there is a difference of instances, it should be applied. And this 'existing elsewhere' is not possible for a universal that is real — such is the connection. For what reason? Because when non-difference from the substratum is accepted, there is an absence of continuity; for what is non-different from a single [substratum], being of its very nature... ///

body.text: 2 /// .āśrayabhāvasya niṣiddhatvāt* / yadi vyatiriktasya sāmānyasyāsaṃbandhān na vyaktyantare svākārajñānajananam evaṃ tarhy ādyāyām api vyaktau tattulyam iti kim ucyate vyaktiṣv apūrvāsv iti / vyaktiṣv ity eva vaktavyaṃ / tathā ekatra dṛṣṭasyānyatra darśanāsaṃbhavād ity api na vaktavyam ekatrāpi vyaktibhede .. ///
body.translated_text: [Folio 2] /// ...because the existence of the substratum has been refuted. If, due to the non-relation of the distinct universal, there is no production of cognition bearing its own form in another instance — then the same applies even in the first instance; so why is it said 'in novel instances'? It should be stated simply 'in instances.' Likewise, the statement 'because what is seen in one cannot be seen elsewhere' need not be made, since even in one [substratum] there is a difference of instances... ///

body.text: 3 /// .. .. sāmānyasyānyatra darśanaṃ na saṃbhav. .. .. va tatvānyatvābhyām anyaḥ prakāraḥ saṃbhavatīty āha svabhāvo hītyādi svabhāvāt tatvam anyatvaṃ vā na laṃghayatīti saṃbandhaḥ / kasmād rūpasya svabhāvasyātadbhūtasyātadrūpasyānyatvāvyatikramāt* / tato 'nyatvād ity arthaḥ / astv atadrūpatvam anyatvaṃ tu kasmād i .. .. .. ///
body.translated_text: [Folio 3] /// ...the seeing of the universal elsewhere is not possible. If one proposes a mode other than identity and difference, he answers: 'For the nature...' and so forth. The nature does not transgress identity or difference — such is the connection. Why? Because the nature of form, being of a non-identical nature, does not transgress otherness. Therefore, from otherness — this is the meaning. Granted that it has a non-identical nature, but why otherness?... ///

body.text: 4 /// d. vānyatvalakṣaṇam ity arthaḥ / ākārāntaravat* / ṣaṣṭhyarthe vatiḥ / tathā hi sukhād duḥkhasyāpi anyatvam asukharūpam* duḥkham ity eva kṛtvā iyatā tadrūpasyānyatvalakṣaṇena vyāptir uktā / asya cānyatvalakṣaṇasyāviśeṣād abhimate 'pi sāmānye etena dharma uktaḥ / prayogas tu yad vastutve saty atadrūpaṃ tasya tato 'nyatvaṃ yathā sukhād. ///
body.translated_text: [Folio 4] /// ...the defining characteristic of otherness — this is the meaning. Like another aspect. The suffix 'vat' is in the sense of the sixth case (genitive). For example, the otherness of pain from pleasure is [understood] precisely by saying 'pain is of a not-pleasure nature' — to this extent the pervasion of the defining characteristic of otherness with that nature is stated. And since this defining characteristic of otherness is without distinction, it is expressed as a property even of the accepted universal. The argument is: whatever, being real, has a non-identical form, has otherness from that — like pain from pleasure... ///

body.text: 5 /// .. .. tvenānyatvavyavahārasya sādhyatvāt svahāvahetuḥ evaṃ tāvad atadrūpatve sāmānyasyānyatvam āpatitaṃ / athānyatvaṃ neṣyate tadā tatvaṃ prāpnotīty āha tac cetyādi / vyakter ananyat tadā tad eva vyaktirūpam eva tat sāmānyaṃ bhavati / atatva ity avyaktirūpatve vastvantaravad anyatvaprasaṃgād etac cānantaraṃ evoktaṃ astv ananyatvaṃ sāmānya .. .. .. .i .. .. ///
body.translated_text: [Folio 5] /// ...because the convention of otherness through [non-identical] nature is what is to be proved, it is a <s>svabhāvahetu</s> (nature-based reason). Thus, first the otherness of the universal follows from its being of a non-identical nature. Now if otherness is not accepted, then identity follows — to this he says: 'And that...' and so forth. If non-different from the instance, then the universal becomes that very instance-form. If it is of a non-instance nature, then otherness follows, as with any other real thing. And this was said immediately [before]: 'Granted non-identity, the universal... ///

body.text: 6 /// di / ekavyaktisvabhāvasya vyaktyantarānvāveśo 'nugamo vyaktyantarasvabhāvatvam iti yāvat* kasmāt tasmād ananugamyamānasyāvyaktyantaratvaprasaṃgāt* / yadi śābaleyātmakaṃ sāmānyaṃ bāhuleyasyātmabhūtaṃ bhavet* / tadā bāhuleyaḥ śābaleya eva jātaḥ / śābaleyātmakāt sāmānyād avyatirekāc chābaleyavad iti kuto 'sya vyaktyantaratvaṃ tata iti .. .. .. .. ///
body.translated_text: [Folio 6] /// ...and so forth. Of [the universal] having the nature of a single instance, entry into — continuity with — another instance, meaning becoming of the nature of another instance. Why? Because if it does not so continue, the undesirable consequence follows that there is no other-instance-ness. If the universal having the nature of <s>Śābaleya</s> (a spotted cow) were to be of the nature of <s>Bāhuleya</s> (another cow), then <s>Bāhuleya</s> would simply be born as <s>Śābaleya</s> — because of non-difference from the universal having the nature of <s>Śābaleya</s>, just like <s>Śābaleya</s> itself. Whence then its being another instance? Therefore... ///

body.text: 7 /// mānyāt sakāśād anvayinīty anugāminī nāpi vyatirekiṇaḥ / sāmānyād anvayinī buddhir iti prakṛtaṃ kasmāt tasya vyatiriktasya sāmānyasya kvacid vyaktibhede anāśrayād avṛtteḥ saṃbandham antareṇa vṛttyayogāt* / vṛttir ādheyatā vyaktir iti tasminn na yujyata ityādinā ca vyaṃgyavyaṃjakasyādhārādheyabhāvasaṃbandhasya ca .i ///
body.translated_text: [Folio 7] /// ...from the universal, the cognition that follows — meaning one that accompanies — is not even of one that differentiates. That cognition following from the universal is the topic. Why? Because that distinct universal, in some instance-difference, having no substratum and thus no occurrence — since occurrence is impossible without a relation. Occurrence means being contained; the instance — in that [the universal] is not established. And with the statement 'It is not fitting,' and so forth, the relation of expressed-expressor (<s>vyaṅgya-vyañjaka</s>) and container-contained (<s>ādhāra-ādheya</s>)... ///

body.text: 8 /// rhi sāmānyatadvatoḥ saṃbandho bhaviṣyatīti ced āhānyasyāpītyādi / vyaṃgyavyaṃjakabhāvāder iti pañcamī ādiśabdād ādhārādheyabhāvaparigrahaḥ / etasmāt pūrvaniṣiddhāt saṃbandhadvayād anyasyāpi yasya ///
body.translated_text: [Folio 8] /// ...if one says: 'There will be a relation between the universal and its possessor' — he answers: 'Of another also,' and so forth. 'From the relation of expressed-expressor and so forth' — the fifth case [ablative]. By the word 'and so forth,' the inclusion of the container-contained relation. From this — from these two relations previously refuted — even of another, whichever... ///

body.text: v1 /// yasya kasyacit saṃbandhasya vyaktiṃ prati sāmānyasyābhāvāt kiṃ kāraṇaṃ nityatvāt kenacid vyaktibhedanānupakāryasya sāmānyasyāpratibandhena na hy apratibandhasya kaścit saṃbandho 'stīty uktam* / etena cānyatve 'napāśrayād iti ślokabhāgo vyākhyātaḥ / asaṃbandham apisāmānyaṃ vyaktiṣu sāmānyānukāriṇī pratītiṃ janayatīti ced āhāsaṃbandhād ityādi ///
body.translated_text: v1 /// [There is] the absence of a <s>sāmānya</s> (universal) with respect to a particular, [because] of any relation whatsoever — what is the reason? Because, being eternal, the universal, which is not affected by any difference among particulars, is unrestricted; and there is no relation for what is unrestricted — thus it has been stated. And by this, the verse portion 'because of having no basis when there is otherness' is explained. If [the opponent says that] the universal, even without relation, generates in the particulars a cognition that follows the universal — [in response, he] says 'because of no relation' and so forth ///

body.text: 2 /// .. d ity arthaḥ / tad iti tasmāt* / ayam iti sāmānyāvādī / ekasya sāmānyasya darśanena hetunā ekasmin śābaleye vyaktibhede vṛttir yasya pratyayasya tasyānyatra vyaktyantare vṛttim avicchan* / vastutveneṣṭasya sāmānyasya vyakteḥ sakāśād ye tatvānyatve te nātikrāmati vastuno gatyantarābhāvāt* tatra cokto doṣa ity ayuktam etat* / vastubhūtāt sāmānyād anuyā ///
body.translated_text: 2 /// ...is the meaning. 'That' means 'therefore.' 'This one' refers to the proponent of universals. By the reason of perceiving one universal in one particular — a piebald [cow] — [he has] the operation of a cognition that does not desire its operation in another particular. The two [possibilities of] sameness and difference of the universal — desired as a real entity — from the particular: he does not transgress [either], because there is no alternative for a real thing. And the stated fault applies there — so this is unreasonable. From a universal that is a real entity, the follow- ///

body.text: 3 /// .. .ākārā pratītiḥ bhrāntir eva bhinneṣv abhedādhyāropeṇa vṛtteḥ kutas tarhi sā utpannety āha vikalpetyādi / vijātīyavyāvṛttipadārthānubhavena yā tathābhūtavikalpasya prakṛtyā janikā vāsanā āhitā tataḥ samutthitāḥ etac ca prāg evoktam ity āha bhāvabheda ityādi bhāvānāṃ tatkāryāṇām atatkāryebhyo bhedaḥ tathābhūtānāṃ cā ///
body.translated_text: 3 /// ...the cognition having such a form is indeed an error, because it operates by superimposing non-difference upon what is different. Whence then does it arise? [In response] he says 'through conceptual construction' and so forth. The <s>vāsanā</s> (latent impression), which by its nature generates such a conceptual construction, has been deposited through the experience of objects that are excluded from what is of a different class — from that [vāsanā] they have arisen. And this has already been stated previously; hence he says 'the differentiation of things' and so forth — the differentiation of things, i.e., those effects, from what are not such effects, and of those that are of such a nature ///

body.text: 4 /// ti nirloṭhitam etat prāk* tatra bhāvabhedaḥ pāraṃparyeṇa kāraṇaṃ vāsanāprakṛtiḥ sākṣād iti dvayaṃ upanyastaṃ / yady anyāpoha eva śabdavācyaḥ / kathaṃ tarhīdānīm ityādi / pradhāneśvarādikāryaśabdā iti pradhānakāryam īśvarakāryaṃ jagad iti ādiśabdāt* śabdabrahmapariṇāma ityādiśabdānāṃ saṃgrahaḥ / bhāveṣv ādhyātmābāhyeṣu atadbhūto 'pra ///
body.translated_text: 4 /// This has been examined previously. Therein, the differentiation of things is the indirect cause, and the nature of <s>vāsanā</s> (latent impressions) is the direct [cause] — these two have been presented. If <s>anyāpoha</s> (exclusion of the other) alone is what is denoted by words, then 'how is it now?' and so forth. 'Words [such as] effect of <s>pradhāna</s> (primal matter), [effect of] <s>Īśvara</s> (God)' — meaning: the world is the effect of <s>pradhāna</s>, the effect of <s>Īśvara</s>; and by the word 'and so forth,' words such as 'transformation of <s>śabdabrahman</s> (word-Brahman)' are included. In entities both internal and external, what is not of that nature, not ///

body.text: 5 /// .āt tadā bhavet pradhānādikāryātmako bhedaḥ / sa eva sa sarveṣām abhedaḥ / tenābhedena nimittena sarvatrā vartante / sa ca nāsti bhāvānām anyāpohavādino matenāpradhānādikāryātmakatvāt* / tataś ca katham evaṃbhūteṣv abhedena vartante / naivety abhiprāyaḥ / tathā cāvyāpiny anyāpohavyavastheti bhāvaḥ / te 'pītyādinā pariharati / te ///
body.translated_text: 5 /// ...then there would be a differentiation having the nature of being an effect of <s>pradhāna</s> and the like. That itself is the non-differentiation of all. By that non-differentiation as a reason, [those words] operate everywhere. But that does not exist according to the view of the proponent of <s>anyāpoha</s> (exclusion), because [things] do not have the nature of being effects of <s>pradhāna</s> and the like. And therefore, how do [those words] operate by non-differentiation in things of such a nature? They do not — this is the intent. Thus the <s>anyāpoha</s> formulation does not have universal applicability — this is the meaning. He responds with 'those too' and so forth. Those ///

body.text: 6 /// tetyādi / vastuny atathā .. .. .. .. .. .. .. .. .. .. .. .. .. .. .. .. .. .. .. .. .. .. .. .. .. .. .. .. .. .. .. .. .. .. .. .. .. .. .. .. .. .. .. .. .. .. .. .. .. pariṇāmenopaskṛtatvād vijñānasantateḥ sarveṣām bāhyādhyātmikānām arthānāṃ darśaneṣv anubhaveṣu / satsu apy anapekṣya tadbhedam apradhānakā .. ///
body.translated_text: 6 /// 'those' and so forth. In reality, not so... ... ... because the continuum of consciousness has been modified by transformation, regarding the perceptions — the experiences — of all objects, both external and internal, even when [such perceptions] exist, without regard to their differentiation, [what is] not an effect of the primary ///

body.text: 7 /// .. .. .. .. kṣyety arthaḥ / tathādhyavasāy. + + saṃketam apradhānakāryān api bhāvāt pradhānakāryatvenādhyavasāyāt* / atathābhūtaṃ kalpitapradhānakāryatvena kalpitaṃ caitanyaṃ / tasya vyavacchedena pradhānakāryābhāvā iti / yadvikalpavijñānaṃ tatpratibhāsiny arthe sa eva / vijātīyavikalpavyavacchedenānyāpoha iti ///
body.translated_text: 7 /// ...is the meaning. Likewise, in determining... through convention, even things that are not effects of the primary, because of [their being treated as] existing as effects of the primary through determination — [that which is] not of such a nature, [but] imagined as being an effect of the primary, [is] imagined consciousness. By its exclusion, [there is] the absence of being an effect of the primary. Whatever conceptual cognition — in the object that appears to it, that alone — by the exclusion of conceptual constructions of a different class, is <s>anyāpoha</s> (exclusion of the other) ///

body.text: 8 /// māt* prabhava utpādo yasya vikalpasya tasmāt samutthitā etad uktaṃ bhavati / yadi nāma vastuni tathābhūtabhedābhāvas tathāpi vikalpāropita evānyāpohaḥ śabdānāṃ pravṛtter aṅgaṃ tato nāsty avyāpitādoṣa iti / pradhānādikārya .. .. ///
body.translated_text: 8 /// From which [the <s>vāsanā</s>] is the origin — the arising — of the conceptual construction, from that it has arisen. What is stated is this: even if there is no such differentiation in the real thing, nevertheless, <s>anyāpoha</s> (exclusion), superimposed by conceptual construction alone, is the basis for the operation of words. Therefore there is no fault of non-pervasion. [The words] 'effect of the primary' and so forth ///

body.text:
C Pramāṇavārttikaṭīkā
r1 /// bhūteṣv apradhānakāryeṣu ubhayathāpi sāmānyasya niṣedhād iti bhāvaḥ / anyāpohavādinas tu na doṣa ity āha / tathetyādi pradhānādhikāryatvavikalpanayety arthaḥ / tadanyebhyo 'pradhānādikāryatvena kalpitebhyaḥ / pradhānādikāryatvenādhyāropitānāṃ bhedaḥ prati ///
body.translated_text:
C <s>Pramāṇavārttikaṭīkā</s>
r1 /// [there is] the negation of the universal in both ways regarding things that are not effects of the primary — this is the meaning. But for the proponent of <s>anyāpoha</s> (exclusion), there is no fault — he says 'thus' and so forth. 'By the conceptual construction of being an effect of the primary' — this is the meaning. From those others imagined as not being effects of the primary. Of those superimposed as being effects of the primary, the differentiation ///

body.text: 2 /// nuvṛttiḥ / pratyayanimittaṃ sāmānyaṃ kiṃ neti cet* naitad asti yasmāt tena sāmānyavādinā sāmānyaṃ kalpayatāpi avaśyaṃ tatra pradhānakāryābhimate vastuni / apradhānakāryābhimatād bhedo nāntarīyakatvād eṣṭavyaḥ / yadi hy apradhānakāryāt puruṣāt pradhānakāryasya na .. ///
body.translated_text: 2 /// ...following. [If one asks:] 'Is the universal the cause of cognition or not?' — this does not hold, because even the proponent of universals, in constructing a universal, must necessarily accept a differentiation from what is considered not an effect of the primary, in the thing considered an effect of the primary — because it is inevitable. For if from what is not an effect of the primary — namely, <s>puruṣa</s> (spirit) — the effect of the primary does not ///

body.text: 3 /// kārye ekaśabdapravṛttyādilakṣaṇe paryāptaḥ śaktaḥ / atathābhūtabhedeṣu yathā sāmānyabuddhir bhrāntā evaṃ tathābhūtabhedeṣv apīty aviśeṣeṇa darśayann āha / yadītyādi / yadiśabdaḥ svabhāvadyotanārthaḥ / yady asya sarvatra nirviṣayatvaṃ svabhāvas tatra kiṃbhūmau vayam iti / s. ///
body.translated_text: 3 /// ...is sufficient — capable — of [explaining] the operation of a single word and such features in the effect [of the primary]. Showing without distinction that just as the universal-cognition is erroneous regarding differentiations that are not of such a nature, so too regarding differentiations that are of such a nature — he says 'if' and so forth. The word 'if' is for revealing [its] inherent nature. If its inherent nature is to be objectless everywhere, then what is our position? ///

body.text: 4 /// .. gṛhītasyānityādirūpasya nityādikasya ca bāhyeṣv abhāvāt* / ataś cābhūtagrahāt* / viplava eva bhrāntir eveti kṛtvā nāsyāḥ sāmānyabuddher nirviṣayāyā viṣayanirūpaṇaṃ prati kaścid ādaraḥ / yadi sarvaiva sāmānyabuddhir bhrāntā kathaṃ tarhy anumānād vastusaṃvāda ity āha / ///
body.translated_text: 4 /// ...because what is grasped — the form of impermanence and the like — and likewise what is eternal and the like, are absent in external [things]. And therefore, because of apprehending what does not exist, it is nothing but error, nothing but delusion — considering this, there is no reason to care about determining an object for this universal-cognition that is objectless. If all universal-cognition is erroneous, then how is there correspondence with reality from inference? — he says ///

body.text: 5 /// ye paricchede nivedayiṣyāmo niveditaṃ ca prāk* / yatrāsti vastusaṃbandho yathoktānumitau yathetyādinā / na tathābhūtasya vastvātmakasya grāhyasya samāveśād grahaṇād anumānavikapasya vastusaṃvādaḥ / pratyakṣavat iti vaidharmyadṛṣṭāntaḥ / kiṃkāraṇam atathā ///
body.translated_text: 5 /// ...in [that] section we shall explain, and it has already been explained previously — 'where there is a connection with a real thing, as in the stated inference' and so forth. It is not because of the inclusion — the grasping — of something real, of such a nature, that is to be apprehended, that the inferential conceptual construction has correspondence with reality. 'Like perception' is a dissimilarity example. For what reason? Not of such a nature ///

body.text: 6 /// dhānāc ca sāmarthyam ity atrānatre / yadi sāmānyabuddhir nirviṣayā katham asyā anyāpohaviṣayatvam uktam ity ata āha netyādi / asyāḥ sāmānyabuddher bhinnapadārthadarśanabaleneti vijātīyavyāvṛttasvalakṣaṇānubhavasāmarthyenotpatter ity adhyāhāraḥ / bahulagrahaṇaṃ ///
body.translated_text: 6 /// ...and from capability — in this [passage] and elsewhere. If the universal-cognition is objectless, how has it been said to have <s>anyāpoha</s> (exclusion) as its object? — to this he says 'not' and so forth. [The implied completion is:] because this universal-cognition arises through the force of seeing differentiated objects — that is, through the power of experiencing <s>svalakṣaṇas</s> (unique particulars) that are excluded from what is of a different class. The word 'abundantly' ///

body.text: 7 /// vasāyāt* / teṣu bhinneṣu vastuṣu svapratibhāsyasya bhāvatvenādhyāropāt* / dṛśyavikalpyāv arthāv ekīkṛtya pravṛtter ity arthaḥ / etad uktaṃ bhavati yasmād bhinnavastudarśanabalenotpadyate utpannāt svapratibhāsaṃ bhinneṣu vastuṣv āropya vartate ///
body.translated_text: 7 /// ...through determination. In those differentiated real things, by superimposing the existence of what appears to it [the cognition]. Having unified the two objects — what is perceived and what is conceptualized — [the cognition] operates; this is the meaning. What is stated is this: because it arises through the force of perceiving differentiated real things, and having arisen, it operates by superimposing what appears to it upon differentiated real things ///

body.text: v1 /// tāvad eko upapattidvayaṃ kṛtvā vyācakṣate / anye tv ekaiveyaṃ dvayapratipattir iti pratipannā / bhinnapadārthadarśanabalena teṣu svapratibhāseṣu bhāvādhyavasāyāt* svapratibhāsa eva bhinno bhāva ity evam adhyavasāyād bhedaviṣayatvam ucyata it. ///
body.translated_text: v1 /// So far, one [commentator], having presented two explanations, explains [the verse]. But others maintain that this is a single understanding of two things. Through the force of seeing differentiated objects, by the determination of existence in those self-appearances — it is said to have differentiation as its object precisely because of this determination that the differentiated thing is nothing but the self-appearance ///

body.text: 2 /// .. nāsti śaśaviṣāṇādikalpanāsu tatra katham iti ced āha tathā bhāvetyādi / yathaiva bhinnavastusvabhāvagrāhyānubhavabalenotpa + + + + tyādibuddhayaḥ svapratibhāse bhinnabhāvādhyāropeṇa pravartante pradhānakāryatvanityādibuddhiṣv api tathābhāva .. ///
body.translated_text: 2 /// ...does not exist, as in the case of conceptual constructions such as a hare's horn — if [one asks] how then? — he says 'thus, things' and so forth. Just as cognitions such as [cognition of universals] — arisen through the force of experiencing what is to be grasped, having the nature of differentiated real things — ... operate regarding their self-appearances by superimposing differentiated existence, so too in cognitions such as 'being an effect of the primary,' 'being eternal,' the existence of such ///

body.text: 3 /// vṛtter bhedaviṣayatvam ucyate śaśaviṣāṇādivikalpeṣv api vikalpāntaravyavacchedena bhinnatvādhyāropād bhedaviṣayatvam astīti svāśrayamātragata vyaktideśa eva sthitaṃ na tu vyaktiśūnye deśe sarvagataṃ vā vyaktiśūnye 'pi deśe vidyamānatvāt* apūrvagha .. ///
body.translated_text: 3 /// ...because of operation, it is said to have differentiation as its object. Even in conceptual constructions such as a hare's horn, through the superimposition of differentiation by the exclusion of other conceptual constructions, there is [having] differentiation as object. [The universal] abides only in the particular-locus belonging to its own substrate alone, and is not omnipresent, nor [is it present] in a locus devoid of particulars — because it would exist even in a locus devoid of particulars ///

body.text: 4 /// bhavo naivety abhiprāyaḥ / bhavet saṃbhavo yadi tasmāt pūrvadravyāt tatsāmānyaṃ paścād utpadyamānaṃ dravyaṃ yāti tac ca nāstīty āha na hītyādi / anyadravyavṛtter ity utpitsudravyād bhinnadeśadravyavṛtter bhāvasya sāmānyākhyasya tataḥ pūrvakād āśrayād acalatas tadubhayā .. ///
body.translated_text: 4 /// ...existence is not [possible] at all — this is the intent. There would be the possibility if from that prior substance, that universal, going [to] a subsequently arising substance — but that does not exist; he says 'for not' and so forth. 'Having operation in another substance' means: of the entity called universal, having operation in a substance in a different location from the substance about to arise — from that prior substrate, without moving, both of those ///

body.text: 5 /// .. tu bhinnadeśenādarśena yogo 'stīti bruvānaḥ / kathaṃ nonmattaḥ syāt* / sāmagrībalād bhrāntaṃ jñānaṃ / pratibimbānugatādarśapratibhāsi tatra jāyate / yathoktaṃ viruddhapariṇāmeṣu vajradarśatalādiṣu parvatādisvabhāvānāṃ bhāvānāṃ nāsti saṃbhava iti / ye 'pi .. ///
body.translated_text: 5 /// ...but one who says there is a connection with a mirror in a different location — how would he not be mad? Through the force of the aggregate of conditions, there arises an erroneous cognition, appearing in the mirror as if following a reflection. As it has been said: 'In objects of contradictory transformation — such as the surface of a diamond — there is no possibility of entities having the nature of mountains and the like.' Those who also ... ///

body.text: 6 /// deśe āsīd vyaktiśūnye deśe tasya sthānānabhyupagamād asti paścāt tatsāmānyaṃ vyaktāv utpannāyāṃ sāmānyaśūnyāyā vyakter anabhyupagamāt* / na ca tatra deśo vyaktyā sahotpannaḥ / na ca kutaścit pūrvakād vyaktiviśeṣād āgataḥ / etac ca na yātī ///
body.translated_text: [6] ...in a location devoid of particulars, since the existence of the <s>sāmānya</s> (universal) in that location is not accepted. It exists later, when a particular has arisen, since a particular devoid of the universal is not accepted. And the location does not arise together with the particular, nor does it come from any prior particular. And this [universal] does not go...

body.text:
D Pramāṇavārttikaṭīkā
r1 /// mānyam iṣyata iti vyāghātaḥ / sa ca prājñānāṃ duḥsahatvād bhāraḥ / ata evāha / ka imam ityādi / prajño hi katham ayuktaṃ saheta / jaḍas tv ajñānād yuktāyuktavicāraṇe 'kṣamaḥ sahetāpi yad āhānyatra jāḍyād iti / bhavatu nāma sakriyaṃ sāmānyaṃ tathā ///
body.translated_text:
[D] <s>Pramāṇavārttikaṭīkā</s>
[r1] ...the universal is accepted'—this is a contradiction. And this is a burden intolerable for the wise. Therefore he says 'ka imam' and so forth. For how could a wise person tolerate what is unreasonable? But a dull person, being incapable of discriminating between what is reasonable and unreasonable due to ignorance, might tolerate it—as he says 'anyatra jāḍyāt' ('apart from dullness'). Granted that the <s>sāmānya</s> (universal) possesses activity; similarly...

body.text: 2 /// .. .. .. .. .. ṅśānta + + + tsudravyaṃ yāyāt* / anaṃśaṃ vā pūrvam ādhāraṃ hitvā / dvayam apy etan nāstīty āha / na cetyādi / pūrvam ādhāram iti sūtrabhāgam utpitsu deśād bhinnadeśam iti miśrakeṇa spaṣṭayati / tayoś ceti pūrvapaścādutpannayor dravyayoḥ bhinnetyādi ///
body.translated_text: [2] ...partless...would go to the substance. Or, being partless, having abandoned its prior substratum—he says 'na ca' etc. to state that neither of these two alternatives obtains. 'The prior substratum'—he clarifies the sūtra-portion 'in a location different from the location about to arise' in a combined manner. 'Of those two'—the two substances arisen earlier and later, 'different' and so forth...

body.text: 3 /// .. .. .. .. deśābhyāṃ dravyābhyāṃ sa + + t* / āloko hi sāvayavatvāt* anyenāvayavena ghaṭena saṃbadhyate 'nyena paṭādibhiḥ / evaṃ rajjuvaṃśadaṇḍāv api svasaṃbandhibhiḥ / na hītyādi asyaiva samarthanaṃ / kasmān na yukta ity āha / tasyetyādi / tasyānavayavasya vastuna ekena dravyeṇa sa .. ///
body.translated_text: [3] ...by two substances in [different] locations...For light, being composite, is connected by one part with the pot and by another part with the cloth, etc. Similarly, rope, bamboo, and stick also [are connected] with their respective associates. 'Na hi' etc. is the substantiation of precisely this. Why is it not reasonable? He says 'tasya' etc.—of that partless entity, with a single substance...

body.text: 4 /// .. tmanaś ca tasya sāmānyasya tatpradeśavarttisaṃbandhirūpatvād utpitsughaṭadeśāt pūrvadeśavartti yadghaṭādidravyaṃ tatsaṃbandhirūpatvān nāsti bhinnadeśena yugapadyogaḥ / a{nyathe ya ātmā tadvyatirekeṇa dvitīyātmābhāvād ekātmanaś ca tasya sāmānyasya tatpradeśavarttisaṃbandhirūpatvād utpitsu} anyatheti tatpradeśavarttirūpatvābhā ///
body.translated_text: [4] ...of itself, and of that <s>sāmānya</s> (universal), since it has the nature of a connection with what exists in that location, because it has the nature of a connection with the substance such as a pot that exists in a prior location relative to the location of the pot about to arise, there is no simultaneous connection with [a substance in] a different location. Otherwise, that self—since there is no second self apart from it, and since that <s>sāmānya</s>, having a single self, has the nature of a connection with what exists in that location—[the nature of existing in that location] is absent...

body.text: 5 /// ṇa saṃbandhāyogāt* tasmād ekavyaktinityatātmanaḥ sāmānyasya nāsti tasminn eva kāle bhinnadeśena dravyena saṃbandhaḥ / saṃbandhe vā pūrvavyaktiniyataikātmakatvena sāmānyasya pūrvavyaktau sthitis tasminn eva kāle bhinnadeśavyaktigamanenāsthitir etac ca viruddham ity āha ekasyādheyasyetyādi / tatra sthānam iti vyaktau / .. ///
body.translated_text: [5] ...because there is no possibility of a connection. Therefore, for the <s>sāmānya</s> (universal), which has a single self eternally bound to one particular, there is no connection with a substance in a different location at that very time. Or, if there were a connection, since the <s>sāmānya</s> has a single self determined by the prior particular, its stability would be in the prior particular; at that very time, its going to a particular in a different location would mean its instability—and this is contradictory. He says 'ekasyādheya' etc. 'Abiding there' means in the particular...

body.text: 6 /// bhyupagamāt* tatra pūrvavyaktāv eva tenaiva pūrvavyaktiniyatenaivātmanā tasya sāmānyasyāsthānam ity ayuktam etat kiṃkāraṇaṃ tasthitetyādi / tasyām eva pūrvavyaktau sthitāsthitātmanoḥ svabhāvayor ekasya yugapat sāmānyasya virodhāt* / sarvatra pūrvavyaktāv utpisudravye ca sarvadety utpitsudravyāt* prāg api aya .. ///
body.translated_text: [6] ...since this is accepted: in the prior particular alone, with that very self determined by the prior particular, the instability of that <s>sāmānya</s> (universal) is unreasonable. For what reason? 'Tasthite' etc.—because of the contradiction of the <s>sāmānya</s> having simultaneously two natures, stability and instability, in that very prior particular. 'Everywhere, in the prior particular and in the substance about to arise, always'—meaning even before the substance about to arise...

body.text: 7 /// .. deśe prāg evāsti sāmānyaṃ / tataś ca yad uktaṃ na ca tatrāsīd iti / tad asiddham iti / sarvākārasthitātmeti yenaivākāreṇa pūrvavyaktau sthitaṃ sāmānyaṃ tenaivotpitsudravye 'pi niraṃśatvāt sarvatra tulyākārāvṛttir ity arthaḥ / tatsvabhāvetyādinā pratiṣedhati / sāmānyasvabhāvasya darśanam āśrayo yasya sa sarvatra bhinnajātīye 'pi ///
body.translated_text: [7] ...in that location, the <s>sāmānya</s> (universal) exists already. And so what was said, 'it was not there'—that is unestablished. 'With a nature abiding in every aspect'—the <s>sāmānya</s>, by the very aspect by which it abides in the prior particular, [abides] also in the substance about to arise, because being partless, its occurrence in every [location] has an identical aspect—this is the meaning. With 'tatsvabhāva' etc. he refutes this. One whose perception, the apprehension of the nature of the <s>sāmānya</s>, is [its] basis, even in [entities of] different <s>jāti</s> (class) everywhere...

body.text: 8 /// .ādi / kiṃ kāraṇam ity āha / aśvetyādi / aśve sthita ātmā yasya dravyatvasyeti vigrahaḥ / gamakatvād vyadhikaraṇasyāpi bahubrīhiḥ / aśve sthita iti vā sādhanaṃ kṛteti samāsaḥ / paścād ātmaśabdena dvipado bahuvrīhiḥ / ///
body.translated_text: [8] ...etc. What is the reason? He says 'aśve' etc. The compound 'aśvasthitātmā yasya dravyatvasyeti' is analyzed as: 'that <s>dravyatva</s> (substanceness) whose self abides in the horse.' Because it serves as an indicator, the <s>bahuvrīhi</s> compound applies even to what is in a different locus. Or: 'aśve sthita' is the instrumental [clause], combined as 'kṛta'; then 'ātma'-word makes it a <s>bahuvrīhi</s> of two padas...

body.text: v1 /// ttyā ca / yathoktalakṣaṇasya dravyatvasya pratītyā tathety aśva iti / na tu dravyatvena saṃbandhāt* gaur dravyam ity evaṃpratyayaḥ syāt* / sa ca pareṇeṣṭa eva na tv aśva iti / na hi dravyatvanimitto 'śvapratyayaḥ / kiṃ tv aśvatvanimittaḥ / tac cāśvatvaṃ gavi nāsti / sajātīyāsv eva vyaktiṣu sarvadā sarvākārasthitātmatābhyupagamanāt* / ayam . .. .. ///
body.translated_text: [v1] ...and by the cognition of <s>dravyatva</s> (substanceness) having the aforementioned definition, thus 'horse'—but not because of a connection with <s>dravyatva</s> would there be a cognition 'a cow is a substance.' And that [cognition] is accepted by the opponent, but not 'horse.' For the cognition 'horse' is not caused by <s>dravyatva</s>, but rather by <s>aśvatva</s> (horseness). And that <s>aśvatva</s> does not exist in a cow. Because it is accepted that [the universal] has a single self abiding in every aspect always only in particulars of the same <s>jāti</s> (class)...

body.text: 2 /// viṣaye dravyatvaṃ vartata itīṣyate / tataś cāśvabuddhiviṣayadravyavṛttidharmakena tena bhāvyaṃ tac cāśvabuddhiviṣayadravyavṛttisvabhāvaṃ dravyatvaṃ yena svabhāvenāśve vartate tenaiva gavādāv api / tathā ca gor apy aśvabuddhiviṣayatā prāptānyathā dravyatvasyāśvabuddhiviṣayadravyavṛttitvaṃ svabhāvo na syāt* / na caikasya dvau svabhāvau yenāśve 'nya .. ///
body.translated_text: [2] ...<s>dravyatva</s> (substanceness) is held to operate in that domain. Therefore, it must have the nature of existing in substances that are objects of horse-cognition. And that <s>dravyatva</s>, whose nature is to exist in substances that are objects of horse-cognition—by the very nature by which it exists in a horse, by that same [nature] it exists in a cow etc. as well. And so a cow too would become an object of horse-cognition; otherwise, <s>dravyatva</s>'s nature of existing in substances that are objects of horse-cognition would not hold. And one entity cannot have two natures, so that in a horse it has one...

body.text: 3 /// .. .. .. .. vyatvamātraṃ dṛśyam aśvabuddhiviṣayadravyavṛttisvabhāvaṃ sad api na dṛśyate tato nāsti gor aśva iti pratītir ity ata āha / tasya ceti sāmānyasya ekasyety anaṃśasya gṛhītasyāpi bhrāntyānavadhāraṇam ity api mithyā niścayātmake parapratyakṣe vṛtter ayogād yathoktaṃ prāk* / tasmād ityādinopasaṃhāraḥ / anavayavaṃ sāmānyaṃ a .. ///
body.translated_text: [3] ...mere substanceness is perceivable, [yet] even though it has the nature of existing in substances that are objects of horse-cognition, it is not perceived—therefore there is no cognition 'a cow is a horse.' To this he says 'tasya ca'—'of the <s>sāmānya</s> (universal), of one [entity],' meaning of that which is partless—'even when apprehended, the non-ascertainment through error'—this too is false, since there is no possibility of occurrence in a <s>parapratyakṣa</s> (direct perception of another) that has the nature of erroneous determination, as stated previously. Therefore, with 'tasmāt' etc. he summarizes. A partless <s>sāmānya</s>...

body.text: 4 /// .. tāṃ na pratipadyate iyatā ca na cāṃśavad ity etad vyākhyātaṃ / jahāti pūrvaṃ nādhāram ity etat pūrvam ityādinā vyācaṣṭe / sa ceti pūrvādhāratyāgaḥ / sāmānyasya nābimataḥ / anyatreti pūrvavyaktau vartamānasya sāmānyasya svasmāt pūrvādhāradeśād acalatas tataḥ pūrvādhāradeśād anyatra sthāne janma yasya dravyasya tasmin vṛ .. ///
body.translated_text: [4] ...does not obtain. And with this much, 'na cāṃśavat' ('nor is it like [something] having parts') has been explained. 'It does not abandon its prior substratum'—he explains this with 'pūrvam iti' etc. 'Sa ca'—the abandonment of the prior substratum is not accepted as belonging to the <s>sāmānya</s>. 'Anyatra'—when the <s>sāmānya</s>, existing in the prior particular, without moving from its own prior substratum-location, [is said to exist] in a substance born in another place, from that prior substratum-location...

body.text: 5 /// .. pi sāmānyaṃ tato 'nyadeśaṃ dravyaṃ prāpnoti ced āha / yatretyādi / yatra deśe asau paścātkālabhāvī vartate tena deśena sāmānyaṃ na saṃbadhyate / pūrvasthānaparityāgānabhyupagamāt* / yatra deśe sāmānyaṃ na vartate taddeśinaṃ ca paścātkālabhāvinaṃ bhāvaṃ prāpnoti nyāyātikrāntatvāt kim apy etan mahādbhūtam iti prak. ///
body.translated_text: [5] ...even the <s>sāmānya</s> (universal) reaches a substance in another location—if so, he says 'yatra' etc.: the <s>sāmānya</s> is not connected with the location where that later-in-time [substance] exists, since the abandonment of the prior location is not accepted. And that [the universal] reaches a later-in-time entity in a location where the <s>sāmānya</s> does not exist—since this transgresses all reasoning, 'this is indeed a great wonder'...

body.text: 6 /// .. .. .. .. .. m adhyavasātum* / sarvagatatva .. panām api nirācikīrṣur āha / yasyetyādi / tasyāpi sarvagatasāmānyavādinaḥ sarvatragā yadi jātis tadā ekatra śābaleyādau yā tasya vyaktiḥ prakāśanā tayā vyaktā karaṇabhūtayā / sā jātiḥ sarvatra vyaktiśūnye deśe vijātīye ca vyaktibhede vyaktaiva prakā .i ///
body.translated_text: [6] ...to determine. Wishing to refute even the position of omnipresence, he says 'yasya' etc. For that advocate of an omnipresent <s>sāmānya</s> too: if the <s>jāti</s> (genus) is present everywhere, then the <s>vyakti</s> (manifestation) that is its disclosure in one [location], such as in a spotted dog—by that manifestation which serves as the instrument, that <s>jāti</s> is manifested everywhere, even in a location devoid of particulars, and in a different <s>jāti</s>, and in a different particular...

body.text: 7 /// .. kācid vyaktir iti niṣiddh. .. .. vṛttir ādheyatā / vyaktir iti / tasmin na yujyata ity itrānatare / yata evaṃ tasmāt sā jātir nityam anapekṣitaparopakārānādheyātiśayatvād evaṃbhūtā yadi svabhāvena svavijñānajananayogyā / tadā nityaṃ dṛśyeta vyakteḥ prāk* paścāc ca / atha na yogyā tadā na vā .. ///
body.translated_text: [7] ...a certain particular is refuted...existence, superimposition. 'Particular' means: in that, it is not possible—in this interval. Since this is so, therefore that <s>jāti</s> (genus), being eternal and having received no assistance from any external aid, being of an unsurpassable nature—if it is by its own nature capable of producing its own cognition, then it should always be perceived, before and after the particular. But if it is not capable, then neither...

body.text: 8 /// .. .. .. + + + vyaktyasannidhāne tatsannidhāne tu samarthā bhavati / tato na nityaṃ darśanam adarśanaṃ vā jāter ity ata āha / svabhāvetyādi / nityatvenānādheyātiśayatvād iti bhāvaḥ / yadi jāter nasti vyaktis tat kiṃ vyaktyaivaikatra sā vyakte
body.translated_text: [8] ...in the absence of the particular, [the jāti is inoperative], but in its presence, it becomes capable. Therefore, there is neither perpetual perception nor non-perception of the <s>jāti</s> (genus)—to this he says 'svabhāva' etc. The sense is: because of being eternal and therefore of an unsurpassable nature. If the <s>jāti</s> has no particular, then what—is it by the particular alone that in one [location] it is manifested?

body.text:
E Pramāṇavārttikaṭīkā
r1 /// .. .. .. .. .. .. .. .. .. .. bhāvād ekatvāj jāter vyaktaiva prakāśitaiva sarvatra vyaktiśūnye deśe vijātīye ca vyaktibhede vyaktiśūnyeṣv apīti apiśabdād vijātiye 'pi vyaktibhede sāmānyasya vyaṃjikayā vyaktis tayā sāmānyagrāhiṇaḥ / indriyasya yaḥ saṃbandhas tadapaekṣayā ///
body.translated_text:
[E] <s>Pramāṇavārttikaṭīkā</s>
[r1] ...because of unity, of the <s>jāti</s> (genus)—being manifested everywhere, even in a location devoid of particulars, and in a different <s>jāti</s>, and in a different particular—'even in [locations] devoid of particulars' means, by the force of the word 'api,' even in a different <s>jāti</s>—the manifestor of the <s>sāmānya</s> (universal) is the particular; through it, the sense organ that apprehends the <s>sāmānya</s> has a connection, in dependence upon that...

body.text: 2 /// .. .. vyakt. .. .. .. te na vyaṃjakas tato vyāpini na sarvatra darśanam ity ata āha / na cetyādi / caśābdenaitad āha / apekṣitāṃ nāma vyaktiṃ jātis tathāpi tasyāḥ sarvatra darśanaṃ syād eva tathā hi yatra tāvad vyaṃjikā vyaktisaṃnihitā tatra sā jātir dṛśyā saṃpannā tad eva ca rūpaṃ tasyāḥ sarvatreti / api ca / na ca sā jātir vyaktyapekṣiṇī ///
body.translated_text: [2] ...the particular...is not a manifestor; therefore, in the omnipresent [universal], perception is not everywhere—to this he says 'na ca' etc. By the word 'ca' he says this: granted that the <s>jāti</s> (genus) requires a particular; even so, it should be perceived everywhere. For wherever the manifesting particular is present, there the <s>jāti</s> is perceived in its full form—and that very form of it exists everywhere. Moreover, that <s>jāti</s>, which requires a particular...

body.text: 3 /// .. .. vakroktyā darśayati / yadi vyaktapekṣiṇī syāt* / yadi vyaṃjikā vyaktir jāter bhavatīti yāvat* / evaṃ ca jātivyaktyor yathākramaṃ vyaṅgyavyaṃjakabhāve 'bhyupagamyamāne yo nyāyo 'tra dṛṣṭaḥ so 'ṅgīkartavyaḥ / kaś cātra nyāya ity āha / vyaṃjakāpratipattāv ityādi sāmānyatadvatos tu vyaṅgyavyaṃjakayoḥ punar viparyayaḥ / kasmād iṣṭaḥ / tathā ///
body.translated_text: [Folio 3] /// ...he shows by an indirect expression. 'If it were dependent on the instance' — meaning: if the instance were the manifester (<s>vyañjikā</s>) of <s>jāti</s> (universal class). And thus, when the <s>vyaṅgya-vyañjaka</s> (expressed-expressor) relationship of <s>jāti</s> (universal) and <s>vyakti</s> (particular) is accepted in their respective order, the principle observed here must be accepted. And what is that principle? He says: 'When the manifester is not apprehended,' and so forth. But between the universal and its possessor, the expressed-expressor relationship is reversed. Why is this accepted? Thus... ///

body.text: 4 /// .. .. .. prāg eva sāmānyagrahaṇam iṣṭaṃ taddvāreṇa tu vyaktes tato vyaṃjikāyā vyakter grahaṇam antareṇāpi vyaṅgyābhimatasya sāmānyasya pratipattir iṣṭeti viparyayaḥ yo 'pi hītyādinā vyācaṣṭe / svāśrayo yatra samavetaṃ sāmānyaṃ tasya jāter grāhakam indriyaṃ tayoḥ saṃyogas tadapekṣā pratītir yasya sāmānyasya tattathoktaṃ / śabdaśrotrendriya .. ///
body.translated_text: [Folio 4] /// ...it is accepted that the <s>sāmānya</s> (universal) is grasped first, and through that the <s>vyakti</s> (particular) is grasped. Thus the reversal consists in this: even without the apprehension of the manifesting <s>vyakti</s>, the apprehension of the <s>sāmānya</s> (universal) which is considered to be the expressed is accepted. He explains with 'For whoever,' and so forth. The sense faculty which grasps the <s>jāti</s> (universal) inhering in its own substratum, their contact, the cognition dependent on that, of which universal — thus it is stated. The faculty of hearing, the word... ///

body.text: 5 .. saṃyogagrahaṇaṃ saṃbandhopalakṣaṇārthaṃ draṣṭavyaṃ / āśrayaśūnyāḥ pradeśā vijātīyavyaktyadhyāsitā vyaktiśūnyāś ca tatra na dṛśyate / yathoktasaṃyogābhāvāt* / tasyāpy evaṃvādinaḥ kvacid vyaktidarśane saty asty evāśrayeṇendriyasaṃyogo jāteḥ sarvatra sthitāyā upakāraka iti / tat āśrayendriyasaṃyogād dhetos taddarśī kvacid vyaktibheda jātidarśī yathā .. ///
body.translated_text: [Folio 5] ...the mention of 'contact' should be seen as indicative of relation in general. In places devoid of substratum, occupied by instances of a different kind, and devoid of [the relevant] instance — there it is not seen, due to the absence of the aforementioned contact. Even for one who holds this view, when some instance is seen, there does exist the contact of the sense faculty with the substratum that is beneficial to the <s>jāti</s> (universal) which abides everywhere. Therefore, from the reason of the sense faculty's contact with the substratum, one who sees a particular instance-difference somewhere sees the universal, just as... ///

body.text: v1 /// .ikā vyaktis tatraiva jāteḥ svarūpaṃ dṛśyaṃ nānyatreti ced āha / na hītyādi tasyā iti / jāteḥ kvacid vyaktau dṛśyamānāyāṃ tadīyam iti sāmānyasaṃbandhi ekasya dṛṣṭādṛṣṭatvanirodhāt* / evaṃ tāvad vyakter vyaṃjikātvam abhyupagamya caśabdopātto 'rtho vyākhyātaḥ / adhunā na ca sā vyaktyapekṣiṇītyādi vyākhyātum āha / vyaktivyaṃgyatvād ityādi ///
body.translated_text: [Folio v1] /// ...the instance — the own-form of the <s>jāti</s> (universal) is visible only there and not elsewhere. If this is objected, he answers: 'For not...' and so forth. 'Of that' means: of the <s>jāti</s>. When some instance is being seen, what belongs to it — related to the universal — is [also seen]; because the state of being seen and unseen of a single thing is not simultaneously possible. Thus, having accepted the instance as the manifester, the meaning implied by the word 'and' (ca) has been explained. Now, to explain 'And it is not dependent on the instance,' and so forth, he says: 'Because of being expressed by the instance,' and so forth... ///

body.text: 2 /// .. .. .. .. .. ṣṭādṛṣṭaṃ rūpam astīty ato 'pūrvapakṣa evāyaṃ kevalaṃ doṣāntarābhidhānārthaṃ / gajanimīlanaṃ kṛtvopanyastaḥ / tathābhūtasyeti nyāyyasya tatreti jātitadvator nyāyyam* vyaṅgyavyaṃjikabhāvasyetyādinā prāha / svarūpaśūnye deśe pradīpādirahite deśe / svavyaṅgyaṃ ghaṭādikaṃ / naivaṃ yathoktena nyāyena vyaktir vyaṃjikā ///
body.translated_text: [Folio 2] /// ...there exists a form both seen and unseen — therefore this is merely the prior position (pūrvapakṣa), presented under the guise of stating a different fault. Having made an elephant-eye-closing, it is presented. 'Of such a nature' means: of what is reasonable. 'There' means: of the <s>jāti</s> (universal) and its possessor. He states: 'Of the expressed-expressor relationship,' and so forth. 'In a place devoid of its own form' — in a place without a lamp and so forth. 'Its own expressed' — a pot and such. 'Not in this way' — by the stated reasoning, the instance is not the manifester... ///

body.text: 3 /// sāmānyam evādau gṛhyata itīṣyate pareṇa sāmānyagrahaṇadvāreṇaiva vyakter grahaṇābhyupagamāt* / ataś ca vyaṃjakāpratipattyāpi vyaṃgyasyas grahaṇād vyaṃjakadharmātikramo vyakteḥ / etad evāha / kathaṃ hītyadi / seti vyaktiḥ sāmānyasya vyaṃjikā ca syād iti saṃbandhaḥ / tatpratipattidvāreṇeti sāmānyapratipattidvāre ///
body.translated_text: [Folio 3] /// ...the opponent accepts that the <s>sāmānya</s> (universal) alone is grasped first, since the grasping of the <s>vyakti</s> (particular) is accepted only through the grasping of the universal. And therefore, even without the apprehension of the manifester (<s>vyañjaka</s>), the expressed is grasped — hence there is a transgression of the property of the manifester by the instance. This is what he states: 'For how,' and so forth. 'It' (sā) refers to the instance. The connection is: 'it would be the manifester of the universal.' 'Through the apprehension of that' means through the apprehension of the universal... ///

body.text: 4 mānyadarśanabalena vyakter darśane 'bhyupagamyamāne vyaṅgyā sā vyaktiḥ prasajyate sāmānyasyety adhyāhāraḥ / padīpena / ghaṭavad iti tṛtīyeti yogavibhāgāt samāsaḥ / supsupeti vā / yathā pradīpena ghaṭo vyaṅgyas tadvat* sāmānyena vyaktir vyaṅgyā prāptety arthaḥ / tatpratipattim antareṇa sāmānyapratipattiṃ vinā vyakter adṛśyarūpa ///
body.translated_text: [Folio 4] /// ...when it is accepted that the instance is seen by the force of seeing the universal, the consequence follows that the <s>vyakti</s> (particular) is the expressed of the <s>sāmānya</s> (universal) — this is to be supplied. 'By a lamp; like a pot' — the compound is formed by separation of case-relations from the third case (instrumental). Or by the rule 'sub-sub' (nominal compound). Just as a pot is expressed (made manifest) by a lamp, so too the particular is expressed by the universal — such is the consequence. Without the apprehension of that — without the apprehension of the universal — the form of the instance is invisible... ///

body.text: 5 .. vyaṃjakam ity etad upāttaṃ / tataḥ pradīpaghaṭābhyāṃ tulyam iti dvandvād eva vatir draṣṭavyaḥ / pūrvanipātalakṣaṇasya vyabhicāritvād ghaṭaśabdasyāpūrvanipātaḥ / pradīpavat sāmānyaṃ vyaṃjakaṃ ghaṭavac ca vyaktir vyaṅgyā / prasajyata iti vākyārthaḥ / aneneti sāmānyavādinā / sāmānyam vinā kim asaṃbhavat kāryam a ///
body.translated_text: [Folio 5] ...the manifester — this has been taken up. Therefore, 'like a lamp and a pot' — the suffix 'vat' should be understood as forming a dvandva compound. Due to the variability of the rule of prior placement, the word 'pot' is placed first. The sentence meaning is: the universal is the manifester like a lamp, and the particular is the expressed like a pot — this is the consequence. 'By this' — by the proponent of universals. Without the universal, what impossible effect... ///

body.text: 6 ktāv iti vahvāyāsaḥ / aśakyasādhanatayā bahuduḥkhahetuḥ / parasparetyādi paraḥ / bhedād vilakṣaṇatvād dhetor vyatirekiṇīṣv ananvayinīsu anvayina ekākārasya pratya ///
body.translated_text: [Folio 6] /// ...is great effort. Being a cause of much suffering due to the impossibility of proving it. 'Mutually,' and so forth. The opponent [objects]. Due to differentiation, due to being of different character — the reason being: in those that are dissimilar, that do not continue, the cognition of a single form that does continue... ///

body.text:
F Pramāṇavārttikaṭīkā
r1 /// .. .. .. ācāryaḥ / ye pācakādiśabdāḥ kriyānimittān icchanti tān praty etad ucyate / abhinnena sāmānyākhyenārthena vinā pācakādiṣu katham ekaḥ śabdo vācakaḥ / vācakagrahaṇena pratyayo 'py anvayī gṛhīta eva tena vinā śabdasyāpravṛtteḥ / ata eva vṛttau śabdapratyayānuvṛttir a ///
body.translated_text:
F. <s>Pramāṇavārttikaṭīkā</s>
[Folio r1] /// ...the <s>ācārya</s> (master) [says]: To those who hold that words such as 'pācaka' (cook) and so forth are based on action — to them this is said: Without an undifferentiated object called <s>sāmānya</s> (universal), how can a single word be the designator of 'cooks' and so forth? By the mention of 'designator,' the cognition that continues is also included, since without that, the word would not function. For this very reason, in usage, the continuation of word and cognition... ///

body.text: 2 /// te pācakādayo 'bhinnās santo 'pi tathety abhedena pratīyeran* jñānena upalakṣaṇam etat tathābhidhīyeran* pācakeṣv adhiśrayaṇādilakṣaṇaṃ pācakeṣv adhyayanātmakam evam anyeṣv api yathāyogaṃ karmaikapratyayādinimittam astīti cet* / sa ity anvayī pratyayagrahaṇam upalakṣaṇam eva śa .. ///
body.translated_text: [Folio 2] /// ...cooks and such, even though undifferentiated, would be cognized as such — that is, as non-different — by cognition. This is indicative: they would be so designated. Among cooks, the characteristic of placing [pots] on fire and so forth; among cooks, what has the nature of study; and likewise in other cases, as appropriate, there exists action, single cognition, and so forth as the basis — if this is objected. 'That' — the mention of 'cognition that continues' is merely indicative. The word... ///

body.text: 3 /// .ākyopanyāse / tat karmeti vā saṃbandhanīyaṃ / pratipācakaṃ karmaṇo bhedāt* / yenāparādhena tā vyaktayaḥ tathety abhinnapratyayahetutvena satyaṃ na kiñcid aparādhaḥ / kiṃtu tāsāṃ vyaktīnām ekarūpatvāt* / tathā hi dravyam ekarūpam anaṃśatvāt* / tad eva ced abhinapratyayanibandhanaṃ na tu tato vyatiriktaṃ dharma ///
body.translated_text: [Folio 3] /// ...in the presentation of the statement. It should be connected as 'that action.' Due to the difference of action in each cook. 'By what fault' — that those instances are thus the cause of non-different cognition — in truth there is no fault. But rather, because of the single form of those instances. For the substance is of one form, being partless. If that very [substance] is the basis of non-different cognition, and not a property distinct from it... ///

body.text: 4 /// kter ākāras tadākāras tasmād anyo 'bhedākāraḥ / sa eva viśeṣaḥ so 'sti yasyāṃ sā atadākāraviśeṣavatī dravyākārād anyākārety arthaḥ / etad uktaṃ bhavati / dravyebhyo eva pratyayo dravyam ity evamākāraḥ / tato 'nyenaivākāreṇa pācakapratyayaḥ / sa yadi dravyanimittam eva syāt tadā dravya ///
body.translated_text: [Folio 4] /// ...the aspect of the instance is its aspect; different from that is the aspect of non-differentiation. That very distinction — which is possessed by it — she possesses the distinction of a non-identical aspect, meaning an aspect other than the aspect of the substance. This has been said: From substances alone there is cognition in the form 'it is a substance.' By an aspect other than that is the cognition of 'cook.' If that too were based solely on the substance, then the substance... ///

body.text: 5 /// dravyasyābhāva iti pratiṣedhapratyayo 'py atadākāra iti śakyeta vyapadeṣṭuṃ / na cāsau vastvantaranibandhanaḥ pareṇeṣṭo viśeṣapratyayānām eva dharmāntaranibandhanatvāt* / viśeṣagrahaṇe ca kevalakriyamāne caitrapratyayo maitrāpekṣayā bhavati viśeṣavān* / na tv atadākāraḥ caitrādyabhidhā ///
body.translated_text: [Folio 5] /// ...the absence of the substance — thus the negating cognition too could be designated as being of a non-identical aspect. But that [negating cognition] is not accepted by the opponent as being based on another real thing, since only particular cognitions are based on another property. And if only the grasping of distinction is being considered, then the cognition of <s>Caitra</s> relative to <s>Maitra</s> is also one possessing distinction — but it is not of a non-identical aspect. The designation of <s>Caitra</s> and others... ///

body.text: 6 /// sparśād viśeṣavāṃs .. tasmāt tatra dravyavyatiriktena nimittāntareṇa bhāvyam iti / uktam ity ācāryaḥ / yathā vyatireko gor gotvaṃ pācakasya pākatvam ityādiko yathā ca viśeṣapratyayā anantaroktās tathoktam iti saṃbandhaḥ / katham uktam ity āha / yathāsvam ityādi arthāntaraviveko 'rthāntaravyavacchedaḥ ///
body.translated_text: [Folio 6] /// ...possessing distinction due to contact. Therefore, there must be a ground other than the substance that is distinct [from it] — thus it has been stated by the <s>ācārya</s> (master). Just as distinction — the cow-ness of a cow, the cook-ness of a cook, and so forth — and just as the particular cognitions as stated immediately above — 'thus it has been stated' — such is the connection. How has it been stated? He says: 'According to each,' and so forth. The discrimination from another object — the exclusion of another object... ///

body.text:
7 /// vacchedamātram apratikṣiptabhedāntaraṃ pratipādaṃ dharmivacanaḥ / pācakatvaśabdas tu tam eva vyavacchedaṃ
v1 /// pratikṣipta bhedāntaram āheti / dharmavacanaḥ tato dharmidharmabhedakalpanayā pācakasya pācakatvam iti / vyatirekavibhaktiḥ / prayujyate evaṃ dravyaśabdasyāpy adravyavyavacchedamā ///
body.translated_text:
[Folio 7] /// ...merely exclusion, without rejecting other differentiations, is the expression — the word for the <s>dharmin</s> (property-bearer). But the word 'cook-ness' (pācakatva) expresses that very exclusion
[Folio v1] /// ...with other differentiations rejected — thus it is the word for the <s>dharma</s> (property). Therefore, by the construction of the <s>dharmin</s>-<s>dharma</s> difference: 'the cook-ness of the cook' — this is a division of distinction. It is employed thus: even of the word 'substance,' merely the exclusion of non-substance... ///

body.text: 2 /// nukāriṇy eva buddhir ato yathāvyavacchedaṃ saṃketānusāreṇa viśeṣavatī buddhir ekatrāpy aviruddhā etac ca bhedāntarapratikṣepāpratikṣepau tayor dvayor ityādiṣu pradeśeṣu pratipāditaṃ / tasmād ityādinopasaṃhāraḥ yathā vyaktīnāṃ bhedas tadvat karmm. + –Insertion of line 7 /// yāni karmāṇi pākākhyāni teṣu karmasu yā karmajātiḥ samavetā saivābhedād dhetuḥ pācakābhedapratyayasya netyādinā pratiṣedhati na jātir hetur iti prakṛtaṃ / kiṃ kāraṇaṃ karmasaṃśrayāt* / karmaṇi samavatatvād arthāntarasaṃbandhinīti / dravyād arthāntaraṃ karmasaṃbandhinī arthāntara iti dravye / na hi .. ///
body.translated_text: [Folio 2] /// ...it is cognition that merely follows [exclusion]; therefore, in accordance with each exclusion, following convention, cognition possessing distinction is non-contradictory even in a single [thing]. And this non-rejection and rejection of other differentiations by those two has been established in passages such as 'of those two,' and so forth. The conclusion is stated with 'Therefore,' and so forth: just as there is differentiation of instances, so too of actions. + [Insertion of line 7:] /// the actions that are called 'cooking' — in those actions, the action-universal (<s>karmajāti</s>) that inheres is itself the cause of the non-different cognition of cooks, due to non-differentiation — he refutes this with 'Not,' and so forth. The <s>jāti</s> (universal) is not the cause — this is the topic. For what reason? Because it inheres in the action (<s>karma</s>). Being inherent in the action, it is related to something other — and 'other' here means relative to the substance. For not... ///

body.text: 3 /// tiḥ samavetā na ca tāni karmāṇīti pācakākhyāni śabdagrahaṇam upalakṣaṇaṃ tathā pācakapratyayena paricchidyante tasya pākākhyasya karmaṇa āśrayo dravyaṃ pācakaśabdenocyate / na ca tatra dravye karmajātiḥ / samavatā evaṃ tāvad arthāntarasaṃbandhitvaṃ karmajāter āśritya dravyaviṣayaṃ pācakā ///
body.translated_text: [Folio 3] /// ...the <s>jāti</s> (universal) does not inhere [in the substance], nor are those actions — the mention of the word 'named cook' is indicative — thus cognized by the cognition of 'cook.' The substratum of that action called 'cooking' is the substance, and it is denoted by the word 'cook' (pācaka). But the action-universal (<s>karmajāti</s>) is not inherent in that substance. Thus, having relied on the fact that the action-universal is related to something other [than the substance], with regard to the substance, 'cook'... ///

body.text: 4 /// ḥ śrutyantaraṃ śrutigrahaṇam upalakṣaṇam evaṃ jñānāntaranimittatvāt* / śrutyantaram evāha pāka ityādi / tata iti karmajāteḥ karmaviṣayābhidhānasya pratyayasya ca hetutvāt karmajāter ity abhiprāyaḥ / syān mataṃ na karmajātiḥ / pācakapratyayaṃ janayati kiṃtu karmajātisamāśrayāt karmai ///
body.translated_text: [Folio 4] /// ...(another) verbal suffix — the mention of 'verbal suffix' is indicative; likewise, because it is caused by another cognition. He states 'another verbal suffix' with 'cooking (<s>pāka</s>),' and so forth. 'From that' means: because the <s>karmajāti</s> (action-universal) is the cause of both the verbal suffix and the expression that designates the object of action — such is the intention. One might hold: the <s>karmajāti</s> (action-universal) does not generate the <s>pācaka</s>-cognition (the cognition 'cook'); rather, it is the action itself, by virtue of being the locus of the action-universal, that... ///

body.text: 5 /// ktivad bhedān na hetuḥ karmāsyetyādi / nanūktaṃ jātisamāśrayād bhinnam api karmābhinnapratyayahetur ity uktam idam ayuktaṃ tu jātisaṃbandhe 'pi karmaṇaḥ tathaiva bhinnatvāt* / kiṃcetyādinopacayahetum āha / –Insertion of line 6: kṣaṇikasya karmaṇaḥ sthityabhāvāc ca kāraṇān na karmanimittaḥ pācakādyabhedapratyayaḥ / na hītyādinā vyā /// tasya ca pācakādyabhedapratyayasya karmanimittatve 'bhyupagamyamāne niruddhe karmaṇi puru ///
body.translated_text: [Folio 5] /// ...(like an) agent (<s>kartṛ</s>) — distinctions (do) not (make it) a cause: 'The action is not its...' and so forth. Now it was said that even a differentiated action, by virtue of its dependence on the <s>jāti</s> (universal), causes an undifferentiated cognition — this was stated. But this is improper, for even when connected with the <s>jāti</s>, the action is just as differentiated. With 'Moreover' and so forth, he states the cause of the additional argument. —Insertion of line 6: Because the action is momentary (<s>kṣaṇika</s>) and has no persistence (<s>sthiti</s>), for that reason the undifferentiated cognition of 'cook' and so forth is not caused by the action. With 'For not' and so forth he explains /// ...if the undifferentiated cognition of 'cook' and so forth is accepted as caused by action, then when the action has ceased, a person... ///

body.text: 6 /// .. .. .. .. .. .. ṇo 'stitvād adoṣa iti ced aha / pacata evetyadi / yadi atītasya satvaṃ syāt* / vartamānavad upalabhyetopalabdhilakṣaṇaprāptaṃ ca kaemeṣyate syān mataṃ karma
body.translated_text: [Folio 6] /// ...because of the existence of... 'there is no fault' — if one argues thus, he replies with 'Of the very cooking (<s>pacata</s>)' and so forth. If the past were to have existence, it would be perceived like the present, and what is subject to the defining characteristic of perception would be accepted as... One might hold: the action... ///

body.text:
G Pramāṇavārttikaṭīkā
r1 /// dravyasaṃbandho 'syāsaṃbandhāt kāraṇān na sāmānyaṃ pācakādyabhidhānapratyayasya hetuḥ / asaṃbaddham api hetur iti ced āha / netyādi / ayuktam ity asaṃbaddhaḥ / śabdagrahaṇam upalakṣaṇaṃ / asaṃbaddhaṃ sāmānyaṃ na jñānaśabdakāraṇam ity arthaḥ / atiprasaṃgāt gotvaṃ apy aśvajñā ///
body.translated_text:
G. <s>Pramāṇavārttikaṭīkā</s>
[Folio r1] /// ...the <s>sāmānya</s> (universal) is not the cause of the designation-cognition 'cook' and so forth, because there is no relation of the substance (<s>dravya</s>) with it — because of the absence of connection. If one argues that even what is unconnected is a cause, he replies with 'No' and so forth. 'Improper' means: unconnected. The mention of 'word' (<s>śabda</s>) is indicative (of cognition as well). An unconnected universal is not the cause of cognition or words — such is the meaning. Because of overextension (<s>atiprasaṅga</s>): even <s>gotva</s> (cow-ness) would cause the cognition of a horse... ///

body.text: 2 /// .. .. ..t* / karmābhāvād eva na kartari / pācake pāraṃparyeṇāpi na samavetam ataḥ / saṃbaddhasaṃbandho 'py asya sāmānyasya dravyeṇa saha nāsti / anyatheti asaṃbaddhasyāpi jñānādihetutve sthityabhāvāc ca karmaṇa ityādi yad uktaṃ tatrātītetyādino 'ntaram āśaṃkate / atītaṃ vina ///
body.translated_text: [Folio 2] /// ...because of the very absence of action, it is not (established) in the agent (<s>kartṛ</s>). In the cook (<s>pācaka</s>), even indirectly, it is not inherent; therefore, there is no relation of the related with this universal and substance. 'Otherwise' means: if even what is unconnected were to be the cause of cognition and so forth — and because of the non-persistence of action as stated in 'because of the absence of persistence of action' and so forth — in between that, he raises an objection with 'The past, without...' and so forth. Without the past... ///

body.text: 3 /// tānāgatam asat* jñānābhidhānayor na nimittam iti saṃbandhaḥ / kiṃ kāraṇaṃ tayor ityādi / tayoḥ jñānābhidhānayoḥ asad dhītyādinā vyācaṣṭe / upākhyāyate / prakāśyate vastv anayety upākhyā 'rthakriyāśaktiḥ / sā nirgatā yasmād asatas tat tathoktaṃ / asad yasmād arthakriyāśaktivikalaṃ tad evaṃbhūtaṃ kathaṃ śabda .. ///
body.translated_text: [Folio 3] /// ...the future, being non-existent (<s>asat</s>), is not the cause of cognition or verbal designation — such is the connection. What is the reason for this? 'Of those two' and so forth. He explains 'of those two — cognition and verbal designation' with 'non-existent' and so forth. <s>Upākhyā</s> (designation) means: that by which a thing is designated, made known — namely, the capacity for causal efficacy (<s>arthakriyāśakti</s>). That which has departed from this — from the non-existent — is called such. The non-existent, being devoid of the capacity for causal efficacy, being of such a nature — how can a word... ///

body.text: 4 /// ṣyate tadā tasya vastutvam eva syān na .. + kiṃ kāraṇam ity āha / kāryetyādi lakṣaṇaśabdaḥ svabhāvavacanaḥ / tad iti tasmāt* atītaṃ pracyutarūpaṃ / anāgatam asaṃprāptarūpaṃ / karmaṇaḥ sakāśād anyac ca vyaktyādikaṃ jñānābhidhānayoḥ nimittatvena neṣṭaṃ sāmānyavādinā / vyaktiḥ karmāśrayo dravyaṃ ādiśabdāt saṃketavā .. ///
body.translated_text: [Folio 4] /// ...then it would have reality (<s>vasutva</s>) itself, not... What is the reason? He says with 'Effect' and so forth. The word 'defining characteristic' (<s>lakṣaṇa</s>) means 'of the nature of.' 'That' means: therefore. The past (<s>atīta</s>) is that whose form has passed away. The future (<s>anāgata</s>) is that whose form has not yet arrived. That which is other than the action — namely, the individual (<s>vyakti</s>) and so forth — is not accepted by the <s>sāmānyavādin</s> (universalist) as the cause of cognition and verbal designation. The individual (<s>vyakti</s>) is the substance (<s>dravya</s>) that is the locus of action; by the word 'and so forth' (<s>ādi</s>), convention (<s>saṃketa</s>) as well... ///

body.text: 5 /// thā ceti anvayinoḥ pācakādiśabdajñā .. + + nimittatve sati na jātisiddhiḥ caśabdān nityaṃ satvam asatvaṃ vā śabdajñānayoḥ syāt* / kasmān na jātisiddhir iti ced āha / tasyā ityādi / tasyā jāteḥ abhinnasya jñānasyābhidhānasya ca nimittatve neṣṭatvāt* yathā ca pācakādiviṣaye te animitte pravartate tathānyatrāpīti kena ni ///
body.translated_text: [Folio 5] /// ...thus, of the two that persist — the cognition and word 'cook' and so forth... if there is a cause, the establishment of <s>jāti</s> (universal) (does not follow); and by the word 'and' (<s>ca</s>), there would be either permanent existence or permanent non-existence for words and cognitions. Why does the establishment of <s>jāti</s> not follow? He says with 'Of that' and so forth. Because that <s>jāti</s> is not accepted as the cause of undifferentiated cognition and verbal designation. And just as in the case of 'cook' and so forth, they operate even without (the universal) as a cause — likewise elsewhere also, by what (ground is it established)... ///

body.text: 6 /// .. ṃkate / karmāśrayasya dravyasya śaktiḥ / śabdagrahaṇam upalakṣaṇaṃ pācakādijñānasyāpi śaktinimittaṃ / netyādinā pratiṣedhati na pācakādiśaktiḥ pācakādiśabdanimittaṃ / kiṃ kāraṇaṃ śakter dravyād avyatirekeṇa dravyavad evānanvayāt* / ananvayinaś cārthasyānvayijñānābhidhānaṃ prati nimittatvānabhyupagamād abhyupagame ///
body.translated_text: [Folio 6] /// ...he raises an objection. The capacity (<s>śakti</s>) of the substance (<s>dravya</s>) that is the substratum of action — the mention of 'word' (<s>śabda</s>) is indicative — even the cognition of 'cook' and so forth has capacity (<s>śakti</s>) as its cause. He refutes with 'No' and so forth: the capacity of cooking and so forth is not the cause of the words 'cook' and so forth. What is the reason? Because <s>śakti</s> (capacity), being non-different from substance (<s>dravya</s>), does not persist (<s>anvaya</s>) like the substance itself. And because it is not accepted that a non-persistent entity is the cause of persistent cognition and verbal designation — and if accepted... ///

body.text: 7 /// saṃgāt* bhinnaiva śaktir iti ced āha na hītyādi / yadi dravyād anyaiva śaktiḥ syāt tadā tasyā eva śakteḥ pākādyarthakriyāsūpayogena kāraneṇa dravyasya śaktyādhārasyānupayogitvaprasaṃgāt* / tasyāṃ pākādinivarttikāyāṃ śaktau tasya dravyasyopayogaḥ evam api pāraṃparyeṇa pākādau dravyam upayuktaṃ syād iti bhāvaḥ / kim ityādi siddhānta .. ///
body.translated_text: [Folio 7] /// ...if one argues that capacity (<s>śakti</s>) is indeed distinct (from substance), he replies with 'For not' and so forth. If capacity were something other than substance, then — because only that capacity has utility as a cause in causal activities such as cooking — the undesirable consequence follows that the substance, the support of capacity, would be without utility. In that capacity which accomplishes cooking and so forth, the substance has utility — even so, indirectly, the substance would be useful in cooking and so forth; such is the import. With 'Why' and so forth, the established position... ///

body.text: 8 /// tathā hi pākādinirvarttikāyāṃ prathamāyāṃ śaktau dravyaṃ yayā śāktyopayujyeta / sāpi śaktir yadi vyatiriktābhyupagamyeta tadā pākādinirvarttikāyāṃ śaktau dravyasyopayogāya śaktyantarasya dravyād vyatirekiṇo 'bhyupagame 'tiprasaṃgāt* / tasyām api śaktāv upayogāyāparā vyatiriktā śaktiḥ / kalpanī .. .. ///
body.translated_text: [Folio 8] /// ...for indeed, the substance is useful in the primary capacity that accomplishes cooking and so forth through whatever capacity. If that capacity too is accepted as distinct, then — since for the purpose of the substance being useful in the capacity that accomplishes cooking and so forth, another capacity distinct from substance must be accepted — there is an infinite regress (<s>atiprasaṅga</s>). For that capacity too, yet another distinct capacity would need to be postulated for its utility... ///

body.text: v1 /// vyatiriktāṃ śaktir dravyam eva prathamāyāṃ pākādinirvarttikāyāṃ śaktāv upayujyata iti vācyaṃ / evaṃ ca dravyasyopayoge śaktāviśeṣyamāṇe taddravyam arthakriyāyāṃ pākādilakṣaṇāyām evopayujyata iti kiṃ neṣyate / dravyasyārthakriyāyāś cāntarakāle kim anarthikayā śāktyā kalpitayā / yata evaṃ tasmāt pākādyarthakriyāśaktir ity anena dravyam evocyate / k. .. ///
body.translated_text: [Folio v1] /// ...if no distinct capacity (is accepted), then substance itself is useful in the primary capacity that accomplishes cooking and so forth — so it must be stated. And thus, when the substance's utility in that capacity is not differentiated, that substance is useful in the very causal activity characterized as cooking and so forth — why is this not accepted? Between substance and causal activity, what (need) for a purposeless capacity that is merely postulated? Since this is so, therefore, by the expression 'capacity for causal activity such as cooking,' substance itself is denoted... ///

body.text: 2 /// ntaraṃ nānvetīti kṛtvā tato dravyāt pācakaḥ pācaka ity anvayī śabdo na syāj jñānaṃ ca śabdagrahaṇaṃ tūpalakṣaṇaṃ / pācakādiṣu dravyeṣu pācakatvādi sāmānyam asti / tannibandhanam anvayiśabdajñānam iti ced āha / sāmānyam ityādi / sāmānyaṃ pācakatvādi yadīṣyate / tadā pākādikriyānirvarttanaśaktyavasthāyāḥ prāg eva dravyasyotpattisamakāla + + dravyasamave ///
