body.translated_text: [Folio 2] /// ...that which is other does not persist — having concluded this, therefore from that substance, the persistent word 'cook, cook' would not exist, nor cognition; the mention of 'word' is indicative. In the substances 'cook' and so forth, there exists a universal (<s>sāmānya</s>) such as 'cook-ness.' On its basis there is persistent word and cognition — if one argues thus, he replies with '<s>Sāmānya</s>' and so forth. If the universal such as 'cook-ness' is accepted, then — prior to the state of the capacity that accomplishes cooking and so forth — already at the time of the substance's arising... the substance's inherence... ///

body.text: 3 /// cakādijñānābhidhānaviṣayaḥ syād iti bh. .. .. .. .. .. .. vet tadā paścād api na bhavet* tasya dravyasyāviśeṣāt* / asty eva sarvakālaṃ dravye pācakatvādi kiṃtu prāg anabhivyaktam ato na śabdajñānayor nimittam ity ata āha / vyaktam iti prāg eva cāhivyaktaṃ bhaved ity arthaḥ / sattādivat* / yathā sattādravyatvādi yāvaddravyabhāvi / arthakriyāyā .. .. ///
body.translated_text: [Folio 3] /// ...the object of the cognition and verbal designation 'cook' and so forth would be — such is the import. ...if it were to inhere, then even afterwards it should not (apply), because of no distinction in that substance. The cook-ness and so forth always exists in the substance, but previously it was unmanifest, hence it is not the cause of words and cognitions — to this he says: 'Manifest' — meaning that it should have been manifest previously as well. Like existence (<s>sattā</s>) and so forth. Just as <s>sattā</s> (existence), <s>dravyatva</s> (substance-ness), and so forth persist as long as the substance persists, of causal activity... ///

body.text: 4 /// .. rthe jātyāśraye tatsamavāyasya sāmānya .. .. + + sya akādācitkatvāt sarvakālabhāvitvāt / etad eva draḍhayann āha / yāvanti hītyādi / arthe jātyāśraye samavāyadharmaṇi saṃbandhayogyāni / tāni sāmānyāni / asyārthasya ya utpādas tena saha samavayanti asmin sāmānyāśraya iti vibhaktivipariṇāmena saṃbandhaḥ / utpā .. .. kālam eva dravyeṇ. ///
body.translated_text: [Folio 4] /// ...in the object that is the locus of <s>jāti</s> (universal), the inherence (<s>samavāya</s>) of the universal... because it is not occasional, because it is present at all times. Confirming this very point, he says: 'As many as' and so forth. In the object, the locus of <s>jāti</s>, which has the property of <s>samavāya</s> (inherence) — those which are fit for connection — those are the universals. They inhere together with the arising of this object — in this locus of the universal — by transformation of the case-ending, the relation (is expressed). At the very time of arising, by the substance... ///

body.text: 5 /// .. / atha siddhāntam atikramya paścādbhāvitvaṃ sāmānyasya kalpyate / tadā tadvyatikrame siddhāntātikrame tasya sāmānyāśrayasya paścād apy aviśeṣāt+ / na tatsamavāyaḥ syāt* / tena sāmānyena samavāyo na syāt* / yathā phalasya ekasvabhāvasyāpi raktatā prāg na bhavati / paścāc ca bhavati / tadvat puruṣasya pācakatvasāmānyam ity ata / tatsaṃbandhītyādi / ta .. ///
body.translated_text: [Folio 5] /// ...now, transgressing the established position, if the posterior existence of the universal is postulated, then — upon the transgression of that (established position), the locus of the universal — because there is no distinction even afterwards — the inherence with that universal would not exist. The relation of <s>samavāya</s> (inherence) with that universal would not exist. Just as the redness of a fruit, even though of a single nature, does not exist previously but exists later — similarly, the universal of cook-ness in a person — to this he says: 'In relation to that' and so forth. That... ///

body.text: 6 /// .. .. .. .ai .. .. .. .. .. ti sāmānyasamavāyaḥ + syeti punsaḥ / na hy aviguṇe svabhāve sthitasya tatsaṃbandho na bhavet* / tatraiva ca sāmānyasamavāyaviguṇe svabhāve sthitasyāsya dravyasya paścāt sāmānyasamavāyo bhavatīti / duranvayaṃ durbodham etat* / phalasyāpy āmrādeḥ pūrvaṃ paścāc ca yady ekasvabhāvatā tatrāpi tulyaṃ codyaṃ / sāmānyasaṃbandham eva tadā dra ///
body.translated_text: [Folio 6] /// ...the inherence of the universal... would be — of the person. For when (the substance) abides in an unimpaired nature, that relation would not not-exist. And when (the substance) abides in that very nature impaired with respect to the inherence of the universal, the inherence of the universal occurs later for this substance — this is difficult to construe and difficult to understand. Even in a fruit such as a mango, if there is a single nature both before and after, the same objection applies equally. The relation with the universal — then the substance... ///

body.text: 7 /// .. kāretyādi / pākādilakṣaṇā kriyā tatkṛto ya upakāras tadapekṣasya dravyasya sāmānyaṃ prati vyaṃjakatve 'bhyupagamyamāne tasya dravyasyākṣaṇikatvād avikāriṇo nāpekṣā sahakāriṇaṃ prati / atha .. kriyeta tadāpy atiśāye 'sya dravyasya kṣaṇikatvam āpadyate / kṣaṇikatvāc cotpādānantaraṃ dhvaṃsi ///
body.translated_text: [Folio 7] /// ...'Activity' and so forth. The activity characterized by cooking and so forth — the benefit produced by it — if the manifestation of the universal with respect to the substance dependent on that benefit is accepted, then — because that substance is non-momentary (<s>akṣaṇika</s>) and non-changing — there is no dependence on an assisting condition. But if... were to be done, then even so, by the excess, momentariness (<s>kṣaṇikatva</s>) of this substance would follow. And from momentariness, it would perish immediately after arising. ///

body.text: 8 /// vyāpāraḥ karma tatkṛta upakāro 'tiśayas tam apekṣya sthirasvabhāvasya pūrvasvabhāvād acalataḥ anatiśāyāt svabhāvāntarānupādānāt* / aviśeṣādhāyini karmaṇi / kāpekṣā / naiva / atiśaye vā dravyasya kriyākṛte 'bhyupagamyamāne 'tiśayādhāyakasya karmaṇaḥ ///
body.translated_text: [Folio 8] /// <s>Vyāpāra</s> (operation) is <s>karma</s> (action); the benefit produced by it is <s>atiśaya</s> (transformation). With respect to that, for what is of stable nature — because it does not move from its prior nature, because there is no transformation, because no other nature is adopted — when the action does not bring about any distinction, what need is there [for it]? None at all. Or, if the transformation of the substance produced by action is accepted, then of the action that brings about transformation... ///

body.text:
H Pramāṇavārttikaṭīkā
r1 /// .. / yadi kriyākṛto 'tiśayo na svabhāvabhūto dravyasya tadarthāntarasya kāraṇād dravyaṃ naivopakṛtaṃ syāt* / tasmāt partikṣaṇaṃ svabhāvabhūtasyānyānyasyātiśayasyotpattes tad api dravyaṃ devadattādi kṣaṇikaṃ syāt* / tata iti kṣaṇikatvāt* svotpattisthānavinā .. .. .. ///
body.translated_text:
H. <s>Pramāṇavārttikaṭīkā</s>
[Folio r1] /// ...if the <s>atiśaya</s> (transformation) produced by action is not of the nature of the substance, then the substance would not be benefited at all by the cause of that other thing. Therefore, since at each moment a different <s>atiśaya</s> arises that is of the nature [of the substance], that substance too — such as <s>Devadatta</s> — would be <s>kṣaṇika</s> (momentary). From that, because of momentariness, without the locus of its own arising... ///

body.text: 2 /// nyasya vyaṃjakaṃ syāt* / tasmāt sthitam etad yathā vastubhūtā jātir nāstīti // atra paro brūte / kathaṃ tarhītyādi / yathetyādi siddhāntavādī / yathā pācakādiṣu / pācakatvādi / sāmānyaṃ nāsti / tathā prasādhitaṃ / atha ca tatra pravartete 'nvayinau jñānaśabdau / tathānyatrāpy antareṇ. ///
body.translated_text: [Folio 2] /// ...would be a manifestor of it. Therefore, this is established: that a <s>jāti</s> (universal) as a real thing does not exist. Here the opponent says: 'How then?' and so forth. The proponent responds with 'Just as,' and so forth: Just as in cooks and such, there is no real <s>sāmānya</s> (universal) of cookness and so forth — this has been demonstrated. And yet, the cognition and word that follow continuity operate there. Likewise, elsewhere too, even without... ///

body.text: 3 /// vṛttir iti / tato 'nvayijñānaśabdavṛtteḥ pācakādiṣv api / pācakatvādisāmānyam astīti / cintitam etad anantaraṃ yathā teṣu pācakatvādisāmānyaṃ na saṃbhavatīti / yady anvayirūpaṃ nāsti / tat kim idānīm animitte te śabdajñāne syātāṃ / netyādi / siddhāntavādī / asty eva tayor nimittaṃ yat tu pareṇ. ///
body.translated_text: [Folio 3] /// ...'occurrence' — therefore, because the operation of continuity-following cognition and word occurs even in cooks and such, [the opponent argues that] the <s>sāmānya</s> (universal) of cookness and so forth exists. This was examined immediately [after]: how the <s>sāmānya</s> of cookness and so forth is not possible in those [cases]. If there is no continuous form, then would those word and cognition be without a cause? The proponent says: 'No,' and so forth — there is indeed a cause for those two; but what the opponent... ///

body.text: 4 /// .. .. .. .. .. .. na bhavatu / kiṃ tarhi + + r nimittam ity āha / yathāsvam ityādi / yo ya ātmīyo vāsanāprabodhaḥ tasmād anvayino vikalpasyotpattiḥ / tato vikalpotpatteḥ sakāśād yathā vikalpaṃ śabdā bhavanti / na tu punar vikalpābhidhānayor vastusattā anvayipadārthasattā samāśraya ity uktaprāyam etat* / avaśyañ cai .. ///
body.translated_text: [Folio 4] /// ...let it not be so. What then is the cause? He says with 'according to each one's own,' and so forth: from whichever awakening of one's own <s>vāsanā</s> (latent impression), there arises the continuity-following <s>vikalpa</s> (conceptual cognition). From that arising of <s>vikalpa</s>, words come into being in accordance with the <s>vikalpa</s>. But the real existence of a continuous entity is not the basis for <s>vikalpa</s> and verbal designation — this has been essentially stated. And necessarily... ///

body.text: 5 /// .. jñānavāsa .. .. .. dhāt* / virodhirūpasamā .. .. na paraspararūpaviruddharūpādhyāropeṇa yathā pradhānakāryam īśvarakāryam ahetukaṃ saṃvṛtimātraṃ jagad ity evaṃ sarvabhede 'nvayinos tayor iti / jñānābhidhānayoḥ aparāparadarśane 'pīti / parasparabhinnānām arthānān darśane 'pi / na ca tatreti / pradhānādi .. + + + + .. ra .. .. ///
body.translated_text: [Folio 5] /// ...cognition, <s>vāsanā</s> (latent impression)... because of... not through the superimposition of mutually contradictory forms — just as [the claims that] the world is the product of <s>Pradhāna</s> (primordial matter), the product of <s>Īśvara</s> (the Lord), without a cause, or mere convention — thus, in all differentiation, those two which follow continuity, namely cognition and verbal designation — even in the perception of different and diverse objects, that is, even in the perception of mutually distinct objects — and not there, with respect to <s>Pradhāna</s> and so forth... ///

body.text: 6 /// . jñānaśabdayor nibandhanaṃ / kasmān nāstīty āha / .. + + + .i .. dhinor ityādi / aniyamenetyādi paraḥ sarvaṃ sarvatrānvayijñānam abhidhānaṃ ca syāt* / etad eva sādhayann āha / na hy animittam ityādi / nanu yathāsvaṃ vāsanāprabodhāt* / vikalpotpatter ityādi / tayor animittatvaṃ pratiṣiddham ity anavakāśa ///
body.translated_text: [Folio 6] /// ...the basis for cognition and word. As to why it does not exist, he says with '...' and so forth. The opponent [argues] with 'without restriction' and so forth: everything would be cognized and designated everywhere through continuity-following cognition and designation. Establishing just this, he says: 'For not without a cause,' and so forth. But [one might object:] from the awakening of one's own <s>vāsanā</s> (latent impression), from the arising of <s>vikalpa</s>, and so forth — since the causelessness of those two has been refuted, there is no scope [for the objection]. ///

body.text:
7 /// cid āsattiviprakarṣābhāvāt* / sarvatra sarvavikalpahetutvaṃ syād iti / na hy animittaṃ bhavad ity atra bāhyanimittābhāvād animittam iti draṣṭavyaṃ / nānimitta iti sāddhāntavādī / aviśiṣṭanimitte na bhavata ity arthaḥ / ata evāha / vāsanāviśeṣanimittatvād iti / yathābhūtadarśanadvārāyātā vāsanā /
8 /// ..ṃ / vikalpaṃ janayati na sarvatreti / samudāyārthaḥ tathābhūtam iti / anvayirūpaṃ na cāsati / tasminn anvayini bāhye nimitte iti siddhāntavādī
v1 /// ata evāha / vāsanāviśeṣanimittatvād iti / yathābhūtadarśanadvārāyātā / vāsanā / sā tatraivādhyavasitatadbhāvaṃ / vikalpaṃ janayati na sarvatreti / samudāyārthaḥ tathābhūtam iti / anvayirūpaṃ na cāsati / tasminn anvayini bāhye nimitte vikalpena na bhavitavyaṃ / bhavitavyam eva etad eva ///
body.translated_text:
[Folio 7] /// ...because of the absence of proximity and remoteness of consciousness, everything would be the cause of all <s>vikalpas</s> (conceptual cognitions) everywhere. Here, 'for it is not without a cause' should be understood as meaning 'without a cause' in the sense of the absence of an external cause. The proponent says: 'It is not without a cause' — the meaning is: it does not arise from an undifferentiated cause. For this very reason he says: 'because the cause is a specific <s>vāsanā</s>.' The <s>vāsanā</s> that has come through the gateway of perceiving things as they are —
[Folio 8] /// ...generates the <s>vikalpa</s> (conceptual cognition), not everywhere. The collective meaning of 'being of such a nature' is: the continuous form, even when it does not [really] exist — the proponent says: in that external continuity-following cause...
[Folio v1] /// For this very reason he says: 'because the cause is a specific <s>vāsanā</s>.' The <s>vāsanā</s> that has come through the gateway of perceiving things as they are — that <s>vāsanā</s>, in that very [object], determined as being of that nature, generates the <s>vikalpa</s>, not everywhere. The collective meaning of 'being of such a nature' is: the continuous form, even when it does not [really] exist — in that external continuity-following cause, there need not be a <s>vikalpa</s>; yet there must be one — this very [point]... ///

body.text: 2 /// gavādiṣu / keśamakṣikādiṣu ca yathākramaṃ / abhāveṣu śaśaviṣāṇādiṣu samayavāsanā yathāsvaṃ siddhāntaṃ saṃketavāsanā / tadbalenāropitarūpaviśeṣeṣu pradhānakāryatvādiṣu tathā vikalpotpatteḥ anvayino vikalpasyotpatteḥ na hy eteṣu yathokteṣu bāhyam anvayirūpam asti / svapnati ///
body.translated_text: [Folio 2] /// ...in cows and such; in hairs, flies, and such, respectively; in non-existents such as the hare's horn and so forth — doctrinal <s>vāsanā</s> (latent impressions) and conventional <s>vāsanā</s>, each according to its own principle. Through the force of those, in the particular forms that are superimposed — such as being the product of <s>Pradhāna</s> and so forth — likewise, from the arising of continuity-following <s>vikalpa</s> (conceptual cognition); for indeed in these as described, there is no external continuous form. In a dream... ///

body.text: 3 /// .i .. te / siddhāntasamāropitasya tu pa + spa .. + + + r yugapad ekatretyādinā pratipāditam evāsatvaṃ / na ca te vikalpāḥ svapnādyupalabdheṣv asatsu vastubhūtānvayirūpam antareṇāpy utpadyanta iti / sarvatrārth. sarvākārā bhavanty api tu pratiniyatā eva / niyamahetuṃ cāha / vibhāgenaivetyādi / tathopalabdhānām ///
body.translated_text: [Folio 3] /// ...and of what is superimposed according to a doctrinal system, its non-existence has been demonstrated through [the argument] 'simultaneously in one place' and so forth. And those <s>vikalpas</s> (conceptual cognitions) arise even without a real continuous form, in non-existent things perceived in dreams and such. They are not of all forms with respect to all objects everywhere; rather, they are strictly determined. And he states the cause of this restriction with 'by division alone,' and so forth — of those perceived in that manner... ///

body.text: 4 /// .. .. .. .. .. .. + + m arthānāṃ vibhāgenopalaṃbhaḥ siddhāntāropitānām api / yathāsvaṃ siddhāntaśravaṇakāle śaśaviṣāṇam ityādiṣv api / śaśaviṣāṇaṃ bandhyāsuta iti / vyavahāravyutpattikāle anāditvāc ca vyavahāravāsanāyāḥ / uktaṃ cātretyādi / ekapratyavamarṣākhyajñānādyekārthas. ///
body.translated_text: [Folio 4] /// ...the perception of objects by division — even of those superimposed by doctrinal systems, each according to its own [system], at the time of hearing the doctrine, even in cases such as 'hare's horn' and the like — 'hare's horn,' 'barren woman's son' — at the time of acquiring practical understanding; and because of the beginninglessness of practical <s>vāsanā</s> (conventional latent impressions). And as stated here with 'and so forth': the cognition having a single meaning, beginning with the cognition called <s>ekapratyavamarśa</s> (unitary reflective awareness)... ///

body.text: 5 /// tvaṃ / dhavādiṣv eva vartate / na gavādiṣv iti / pṛṣṭena pareṇaitad eva vācyam* / bhāvaśaktir eva sā / dhavādīnāṃ yena ta eva vṛkṣatvaṃ prati pratyāsannā na gavādaya iti / tadā tulye bhede yayā pratyāsatyā / bhāvaśaktilakṣaṇayā jātiḥ / kvacit svāśrayābhimate 'rtharāśau / prasarpati ///
body.translated_text: [Folio 5] /// ...[tree]-ness applies only to <s>dhava</s> (axle-wood) trees and such, not to cows and such. To the question posed by the opponent, precisely this must be said: that is nothing but the <s>bhāvaśakti</s> (power of being) — by which those <s>dhava</s> trees and such are proximate to tree-ness while cows and such are not. Then, given equal differentiation, that by which there is proximity — defined by the <s>bhāvaśakti</s> — is called <s>jāti</s> (universal). In some collection of objects accepted as its own locus, it extends... ///

body.text: 6 /// dhyavasāyavaśāt* bhāvānāṃ / an. yo na tu vastubhūta iti atra sāṃkhya āha / na nivṛttim ityādi / bhāvānvayo bhāvānām ekarūpatvaṃ / apara iti vastubhūtas tadā ekasya bījasya yat kāryaṃ / tadanyasya pṛthivyāder na syāt* / kasmāt* / tayor bījapṛthivyor atyantabhedataḥ / yady e ///
body.translated_text: [Folio 6] /// ...by the force of determination, of existing things — the continuity is not a real thing. Here the <s>Sāṃkhya</s> [philosopher] says: 'Not cessation,' and so forth. The continuity of existents means the oneness of form of existents. 'Another' — if it is a real thing, then the effect of a single seed would not belong to another thing such as earth and so forth. Why? Because of the absolute difference between those two — the seed and the earth. If... ///

body.text: 7 /// .ādhayati / yo hi tasya bījasyāṃkurajananasvabhāvo na hi so 'nyasya pṛthivyāder asti yo 'sti buddhyāropito vyāvṛttilakṣaṇo na sa janakaḥ / kasmād vyatirekasyānyavyāvṛttilakṣaṇasya niḥsvabhāvatvāt* / tasmād bījasvalakṣaṇam eva janakaṃ rūpaṃ t. .. .. .. ///
body.translated_text: [Folio 7] /// ...for that sprout-generating nature of the seed does not belong to another thing such as earth and so forth. What does exist [in common] is superimposed by cognition and characterized by <s>vyāvṛtti</s> (exclusion) — that is not the generator. Why? Because <s>vyatireka</s> (negative concomitance), characterized by exclusion from others, is without own-nature. Therefore, only the <s>svalakṣaṇa</s> (particular) of the seed is the generative form... ///

body.text:
I Pramāṇavārttikaṭīkā
r1 /// t. rekasyānyavyāvṛttilakṣaṇasya niḥsvabhāvatvāt* / tasmād bījasvalakṣaṇam eva janakaṃ rūpaṃ / tad eva vastu / tajjanakaṃ cety aṃkurajanakaṃ svalakṣaṇaṃ / anyatreti pṛthivyādau / aparaṃ pṛthivyādikaṃ /
2 /// + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + ḥ .. pṛthivyādis tenāṃkurajananena bījasvabhāvena / tato bījād abhinnaḥ syāt* yadītyādi siddhāntavādī / ātmaikatrāpīti / kāraṇakalāpasya yenābhinnenātmanā janakatvam iṣyate / sa ātmā teṣāṃ kāraṇānāṃ madhya ekatrāpi kāraṇe 'stīti / tenaikena kāryaṃ kṛtam iti .. ///
body.translated_text:
I. <s>Pramāṇavārttikaṭīkā</s>
[Folio r1] /// ...because <s>vyatireka</s> (negative concomitance), characterized by exclusion from others, is without own-nature. Therefore, only the <s>svalakṣaṇa</s> (particular) of the seed is the generative form. That alone is the real thing; and that is its generator — thus, the <s>svalakṣaṇa</s> that generates the sprout. 'Elsewhere' means in earth and so forth. 'Another' means earth and such.
[Folio 2] /// ...earth and such, through that sprout-generating nature of the seed — therefore it would be non-different from the seed. The proponent responds with 'if,' and so forth. 'The self even in one' — if the generative capacity of the causal aggregate is accepted as belonging to a non-different self, then that self exists even in a single one among those causes. Therefore the effect would be produced by that one alone... ///

body.text: 3 /// .. .. .. .. .. .. kāraṇāntaravaiyarthyam* / naitad asti samuditānāṃ antyāvasthāyām eva / teṣāṃ tādṛśaṃ sāmarthyam* / kṣaṇikānāṃ hetupratyayāyattasannidhitvāt* / parasya tu nityavādinaḥ sadā tadrūpam astīti bhavet kāraṇāntarāṇām ānarthakyaṃ / ata evoktam ekatrāpi so 'sti kāraṇānantaravika .. .. ///
body.translated_text: [Folio 3] /// ...the purposelessness of other causes. This is not so — only in the final state of those that have come together do they have such capacity. Because for <s>kṣaṇika</s> (momentary) things, their proximity is dependent on causes and conditions. But for the opponent who advocates permanence, since that form always exists, the other causes would be purposeless. For this very reason it was said: 'even in one [cause] it exists' — the immediate succession of causes... ///

body.text: 4 /// kasvabhāvatvād ekasya kāryasya kārako .. + + + sa teṣāṃ kāraṇābhimatānām arthānām abhinno janakaḥ svabhāva ekakāraṇasannidhāne 'py asti / tataś ca sarvasyām avasthāyāṃ avaikalyāt kāraṇasya yatra tatrāvasthitaḥ eko 'pi janakaḥ syāt* / etad eva draḍhayann āha / yasmād ityādi / ekasminn api bījādau sannihite nāpaity a .i ///
body.translated_text: [Folio 4] /// ...because of its being of one nature, the producer of a single effect... that non-different generative <s>svabhāva</s> (own-nature), which is accepted as the cause of those objects, exists even in the presence of a single cause. And therefore, because of the non-deficiency of the cause in every state, wherever it is situated, even one [cause] alone would be the generator. Confirming precisely this, he says: 'Since,' and so forth — even when a single seed and so forth is present, it does not depart... ///

body.text: 5 /// .. .. nnasya kāryajananasvabhāvasya bījād arthā + + pṛthivyādau / viśeṣo 'stīti / kiṃ kāraṇaṃ / viśeṣe saty abhedahāneḥ / sa hy abhinno janakābhimataḥ / svabhāvaḥ tatrāpi bīje 'pi kevale 'stīti / naikasya bījasya sthitāv api / tasyety abhinnasya rūpasya janakābhimatasy. ///
body.translated_text: 5 /// ...of what has the nature of producing an effect, from the seed, objects... in earth and the like — there is a particular. What is the reason? Because in the presence of a particular, non-difference is abandoned. For the undifferentiated [nature] is considered as the producer. The inherent nature exists there too, even in the seed alone. Even when one seed persists, of that — of the undifferentiated form considered as the producer ///

body.text: 6 /// .. .. vasthābhedaḥ / .. .. ṃ sahasthitiniyamābhāvāt .. + + .. .. etac cābhyupagamyoktam anyathā nityād avasthāntaravyatiriktānāṃ viśeṣāṇām api katham apāyaḥ / na ca te janakā iti viśeṣaḥ / kasmān neṣṭā ity āha / sahakāriṇām ityādi / tasmād ekasminn api bījādau sthite / janakasyātmanaḥ sthānāt* / asthāyina iti / viśeṣasya ekasthi ///
body.translated_text: 6 /// ...non-differentiation of states... because there is no restriction of co-existence... And this has been stated by way of concession; otherwise, how could there be the disappearance of particulars that are distinct from other states, when [the universal is] eternal? And those [universals] are not producers — this is the distinction. Why are [they] not accepted? — he says 'of the auxiliaries' and so forth. Therefore, even when one seed and the like persists, because the producer-self remains; 'not persisting' means: of a particular, in one state ///

body.text: 7 /// ḥ syān na ca bhavati kāryotpattis tataḥ sāmānye sthite 'pi saha .. .i .. .. .y. .. kasya viśeṣasyāpāye / phalābhāvād viśeṣebhyas tadudbhavas tasya kāryasyodbhavaḥ na sāmānyāt* / tatkāryam aṃkurādikaṃ / kiṃ bhūtam aneketyādi / anekasya sahakāriṇaḥ sādhāraṇaṃ / anekasahakārijanyam ity arthaḥ / ekaviśeṣāpāye 'pīti / sahakāriṇām anyatamabhedāpā .. ///
body.translated_text: 7 /// ...there would be — but the production of the effect does not occur — therefore, even when the universal persists, along with... when a particular disappears, because of the absence of the result, its arising — the arising of that effect — is from the particulars, not from the universal. That effect is the sprout and the like. Of what nature? 'Of many' and so forth: common to many auxiliaries — meaning: produced by many auxiliaries together. 'Even when one particular disappears': [meaning] the disappearance of any one among the auxiliaries ///

body.text: 8 /// śeṣeṣv evānvayavyatirekau kāryasya na tu sāmānye / tad āha / na tv avikala iti / ekaviśeṣasthitāv avikale 'pi abhinne rūpe tatkāryaṃ na bhavati / kāryaṃ hītyādinaitad eva vibhajate / kutaścid bhāva utpādaḥ / sa eva dharmaḥ sa yasyāsti / tat tadbhāvadharmi / kadācid yan na bhavati / tat tasya janakasya vaikalyāt* / na cābhinnasya rūpasya janakābhi .. .. .ya ///
body.translated_text: 8 /// ...positive and negative concomitance of the effect is with the particulars alone, not with the universal. To that he says: 'but not when complete.' Even when one particular persists and the undifferentiated form is complete, that effect does not occur. 'For the effect' and so forth — he analyzes precisely this. Arising from something is production. That very property — that which possesses it — that is the substrate possessing that property. When at some time it does not occur, that is because of the deficiency of that producer. And of an undifferentiated form, the producer-conception... ///

body.text:
9 /// m asti / avikale tasmin sāmānyarūpe kāryam abhavat* / tasya sāmānyasyājananātmatāṃ sūcayati tasmāt* / viśeṣāṇām eva bhāvābhāvābhyāṃ kāryasya bhāvābhāvau / yeṣāṃ ca viśeṣāṇāṃ sākalyavaikalyābhyāṃ kāryaṃ bhāvābhāvavat* /
v1 /// ḥ kāryasyotpattiḥ / tasmin sati bhavatīti / hetubhāvayogye viśeṣe sati bhavataḥ kāryasya tadanyasmād iti / viśeṣād anyasmāt sāmānyāt* / atiprasaṃgāt* / sarvaḥ sarvasya kāraṇaṃ syāt* / yata evaṃ tasmād viśeṣā eva janakāḥ / na sāmānyaṃ janakaḥ / tato 'janakatvāt ta eva viśeṣā vastu paramārthasanta ity arthaḥ / kiṃ kāraṇaṃ yasmāt* / sa pāramārthik. .. ///
body.translated_text:
9 /// ...exists. When that universal-form is complete, the effect did not occur — this indicates that the universal has the nature of non-production. Therefore, by the presence and absence of particulars alone, the presence and absence of the effect [are determined]. And of those particulars, by whose completeness and deficiency the effect has presence and absence —
v1 /// ...the production of the effect. 'When that exists, it occurs' — meaning: when the particular that is suitable for being a cause exists, the effect occurs; 'from something other than that' — from something other than the particular, namely from the universal — there would be overextension: everything would be the cause of everything. Since this is so, therefore the particulars alone are producers; the universal is not a producer. Since it is not a producer, those very particulars are real things, ultimately existent — this is the meaning. What is the reason? Because that ultimately ///

body.text: 2 /// .ītyādinā vyācaṣṭe –vyācakṣate?–– / arthakriyāyogyatā vastuno lakṣaṇaṃ ayogyatā tv avastuno lakṣaṇam iti saṃbandhaḥ / vakṣyāmaḥ arthakriyāsamarthaṃ yat tatra paramārthasad ityādinā / sarvārthakriyāyogyo 'rtho viśeṣātmako / nānveti / viśeṣasya vyaktyantānanuyāyitvāt* / yo 'nveti / sāmānyātmā / tasmāt sāmānyātmano na kāryasaṃbhavaḥ / tasmād i ///
body.translated_text: 2 /// ...he explains with 'and so forth.' Suitability for causal efficacy is the defining characteristic of a real thing; unsuitability is the defining characteristic of a non-thing — this is the connection. As we shall state: 'What is capable of causal efficacy — that is ultimately real' and so forth. The object that is capable of all causal efficacy has the nature of a particular. [The universal] does not follow — because the particular does not follow to other instances. What does follow has the nature of a universal. Therefore, from what has the nature of a universal, the production of an effect is not possible. Therefore ///

body.text: 3 /// d ity arthaḥ / tataḥ eveti / viśeṣād eva / .. .. + + .. .i .. niṣpatteḥ tad evaṃ paraiḥ kalpitasyānvayirūpasyājanakatvaṃ pratipāditam adhunā yat pareṇoktam ekasya kāryam anyasya na syād atyantabhedata iti / tat parihartuṃ tad eva codyam āvartayati / svabhāvānanvayāt tarhītyādinā / jvarādiśamane kaścit saha .. tyekam e ///
body.translated_text: 3 /// ...is the meaning. 'From that alone' — from the particular alone... because of production [from that alone]. Thus the non-productivity of the form that follows [universals], as constructed by opponents, has been established. Now, to refute what the opponent has said — 'since one thing's effect would not belong to another, due to absolute difference' — he repeats that very objection with 'therefore, because of the non-following of the inherent nature' and so forth. In curing fever and the like, some [substance], together... one ///

body.text: 4 /// saḥ / ekasya bījāder yajjanakaṃ rūpaṃ tadany + pṛthivyāder nāstīti kṛtvānyaḥ sahakārī ajanakaḥ syāt* / janakasvabhāvād bhinnasvabhāvasya janakatve vābhyupagamyamāne bhedāviśeṣāt sarvo yavabījādir api / śālyaṃkurasya janakaḥ syāt* / naitad ityādinā pariharati / śālibījasyaikasya / janakasya ///
body.translated_text: 4 /// ...that: the productive form of one [thing such as] a seed is not present in another [thing such as] earth — considering this, the other auxiliary would be non-productive. Or, if it is accepted that what has a nature different from the productive nature can be a producer, then without any distinction of difference, every barley seed and the like would also be a producer of a rice sprout. He responds with 'not so' and so forth. Of one rice seed, of the producer ///

body.text: 5 /// .iḥ / śālyaṃkurasya nāparo .. .. .ī .. ..ḥ / caśabda ślokapūraṇārthaḥ / evakārārtho vā / kiṃ kāraṇaṃ / svabhāvo 'yaṃ bhāvānāṃ ekasya yo janaka ātmā tasmād ātmanaḥ svabhāvād bhidyamānāḥ sarve samaṃ tulyaṃ janakāḥ prāpnuvanti / bhedāviśeṣāt* / na vā kaścij janaka iti / syād etac codyaṃ / yady eṣām ekasmā .. .. .. d ātmano ///
body.translated_text: 5 /// ...of a rice sprout, no other [is a producer]... The particle 'ca' is for completing the verse, or has the meaning of 'eva' (only). What is the reason? This is the nature of things: all that differ from the self — the producing nature — of one thing, equally become [non-]producers. Because there is no distinction of difference. Or else no one at all is a producer. This objection might arise: if from one of these... from the self ///

body.text: 6 /// .. .. ..ṃ .. .. d eva / tata iti / viśeṣasaṃ .. + + bhedāviśeṣe 'pi / kutaścid ātmātiśayād viśiṣṭakāryapratiniyatalakṣaṇāt* / kaścij janakaḥ pṛthivyādi / śālyaṃkurasya nāparo yavabījādi / kasmāt* / śālyaṃkurajananāviśeṣas tasya pṛthivyādeḥ / sahakāriṇaḥ svabhāvo nāparasya yavabījādeḥ / ayam eva vibhāgaḥ / kiṃ kṛ .. ///
body.translated_text: 6 /// ...that alone. 'From that' means: from the connection with the particular... even when there is no distinction of difference, due to the superiority of a certain self — defined by the restriction to a specific effect — something [such as] earth is the producer of a rice sprout, not another [such as] a barley seed. Why? Because that — earth — has the nature of an auxiliary [characterized by] non-distinction in producing a rice sprout, which another — a barley seed — does not have. This is precisely the distinction. What makes... ///

body.text: 7 /// .. .. .. yuktaṃ syāt* / kuto hetor ayaṃ yathoktaḥ svabhāva iti / avaśyaṃ hi svabhāvabhedasya hetunā bhāvyaṃ / yato nirhetukatve hetv anapekṣiṇo deśādiniyamābhāvenātiprasaṃgāt* / sarvatra sarvadā sarvātmanā bhāvaprasaṃgāt* / tasmāt svabhāvo 'sya kāraṇābhimatasya svahetoḥ sakāśād bhavatīty ucyate / tasya ///
body.translated_text: 7 /// ...would be reasonable. From what cause does this stated inherent nature arise? For the differentiation of inherent nature necessarily requires a cause, since if it were causeless — not depending on a cause — there would be overextension due to the absence of restriction by location and the like: there would be the absurd consequence of existence everywhere, at all times, in all ways. Therefore, the inherent nature of this [thing] considered as a cause arises from its own cause — this is what is said. Of that ///

body.text: 8 /// .. .. .. .. .. nādir hetuparaṃparā na bhinnānāṃ bhāvānāṃ hetupravibhāge bādhakaṃ pramāṇam asti / tad evāha bhinnetyādi / svabhāvād iti vastusthiteḥ ekatve tu bādhakam astīty āha / abhede tv ityādi / parasparam abhedād ekasya nāśe sarvasya yugapannāśa
body.translated_text: 8 /// ...the beginningless series of causes does not serve as a proof that invalidates the assignment of different causes to different things. He states this with 'different' and so forth. 'From the inherent nature' means: from the actual state of things. But with regard to oneness, there is an invalidating proof — he says 'but in non-difference' and so forth. Because of non-difference from each other, when one is destroyed, there would be the simultaneous destruction of all,

body.text:
J Pramāṇavārttikaṭīkā
r1 /// .. .. .. śeḥ / svabhāvenābhedāt* / vibhāgotpattītyādi / ekasyotpattir anyasyānutpattir ekasya sthitir anyasya nirodha ity evaṃ vibhāgenotpatyādayo na syuḥ / kiṃtu sakṛd eva syuḥ / svātmavad iti / yathaikasyāvasthāviśeṣasya na vibhāgenotpatyādayas tadvad i {.. nvayavyatirekas tadabhedasya lakṣaṇaṃ saty api bhā} ///
body.translated_text:
J <s>Pramāṇavārttikaṭīkā</s>
r1 /// ...because of non-difference by nature. 'Differentiated arising' and so forth: the arising of one and the non-arising of another, the persistence of one and the cessation of another — such arising and the rest differentiated [by individual items] would not be possible; rather, they would occur all at once. 'Like its own self' means: just as for one state-particular, there is no differentiated arising and the rest, so too {positive and negative concomitance is the defining characteristic of that non-difference, even when there exists} ///

body.text: 2 /// .. .y. .r. h. .. m ityādi / sūtre tu n. + .. dbhavagrahaṇam upalakṣaṇaṃ / tathā tenaivāvibhāgotpatyādinā upalakṣaṇān niścayād abhedasya anyathā bhedābhedau kena lakṣyete / ekākārasyāpīti tulyākārasyāpi vyatirekaḥ pṛthagutpatyādimatvaṃ tad bhedasya lakṣaṇaṃ / avibhāgotpatyādimatvam avyatirekas tad abhedasya lakṣaṇaṃ .. ///
body.translated_text: 2 /// ...'and so forth.' But in the <s>sūtra</s>, the mention of... is indicative. Likewise, by that very indication of non-differentiated arising and the rest, from the ascertainment of non-difference; otherwise, by what would difference and non-difference be characterized? 'Even of one having one form' — even of one having the same form, there is negative concomitance, i.e., having separate arising and the rest — that is the defining characteristic of difference. Having non-differentiated arising and the rest is non-negative-concomitance — that is the defining characteristic of non-difference ///

body.text: 3 /// r utpādānutpādaprabhṛtikayor yuga .. + tm. + virodhāt* / nābheda evārthānāṃ kiṃtu bhedo 'py asti / tena kāraṇena / naivaṃ / na sakṛdutpatyādiprasaṃga iti ced āha / netyādy asyaiva vyākhyānaṃ / na vai sarveṇākāreṇāvyatirekam abhedaṃ brūmo yenaivaṃ syāt* / sakṛnnāśotpādādi .y. t* / .. ///
body.translated_text: 3 /// ...because of the contradiction between the pair of arising and non-arising and the like... [there is] not only non-difference of things, but difference also exists. For that reason — [if one says] 'it is not so, there is no absurd consequence of simultaneous arising and the rest' — he says 'not' and so forth — this is the explanation of precisely that. We do not claim non-negative-concomitance, i.e., non-difference, in every aspect, so that this would follow — simultaneous destruction, arising, and the rest ///

body.text: 4 /// .. .. .. lakṣaṇo bhinno n. .y. traiguṇyātmakaḥ sukhaduḥkhamohātmatāyāḥ sarvatrāviśeṣāt / iti yathoktād avasthālakṣaṇād bhādāt* / evaṃ tarhi sāmānyasya nityatvāt* sarvatra sthānaṃ / viśeṣāṇān tu vināśa ity etad aṅgīkṛtaṃ tataś ca ekasmin viśeṣe vinaśyati sati / yas tiṣṭhati sāmānyātmā / na sa tasya viśeṣasya .. .. ..ḥ / vi .. .. .. ///
body.translated_text: 4 /// ...characterized as different, not... having the nature of the three <s>guṇas</s>, because of the universality of having the nature of pleasure, pain, and delusion everywhere — thus, because of contradiction with the stated state-characteristic. If so, then because of the eternality of the universal, it persists everywhere; but the particulars are destroyed — this is accepted. And therefore, when one particular is destroyed, what persists — having the nature of a universal — that is not [the cause] of that particular... ///

body.text: 5 /// .. nyathā sthānāsthānayor ekāśrayatve 'bhyupagamya .. + + .. + .. .. mmāv ekātmany aṅgīkṛtau / tataś ca ko 'nyo dharmo bhedako naiva kaścit* naiva viruddhau dharmāv ekatrāṅgikriyete / yasmād viśeṣāḥ pṛthagutpātyādinā sarvākāravivekinaḥ / sāmānyaṃ tu pṛthagutpatyādyabhāvāt sarvatrāvivekīty ata āha / sarvākāretyādi sarvākāravivekāviveki ///
body.translated_text: 5 /// ...otherwise, having accepted that persistence and non-persistence share a single substrate... both are accepted in one self. And then what other differentiating property [could there be]? None at all. Contradictory properties are not accepted in one [thing]. Because the particulars, through separate arising and the rest, are discriminated in every aspect, whereas the universal, through the absence of separate arising and the rest, is undiscriminated everywhere — therefore he says 'in every aspect' and so forth — discriminated-undiscriminated in every aspect ///

body.text: 6 /// .. .i .i / bhedasāmānye bhinne ity etadabhidhānamātraṃ neṣṭaṃ syāt* / na tu vastu neṣṭaṃ / vastu tu bhedasāmānyātmakaṃ parasparaṃ bhinnam iṣṭam eva / etac coktaṃ prāk* / nāmāntaraṃ vārtham abhyupagamya tathābhidhānād ityādinā / tad iti tasmāt* / ime bhāvā iti / viśeṣāḥ sāmānyaṃ vā / parasparaṃ bhinnā eva / kiṃbhū .ā naikayogakṣem. ///
body.translated_text: [6] ...in the case of difference-and-universal being different, only this verbal designation is not accepted—but the real entity is not rejected. Indeed, the real entity, having the nature of both difference and universal, is accepted as mutually distinct. And this was stated earlier with 'having accepted the meaning, or by a different name, because of such designation' and so forth. 'Tat' means 'therefore.' 'These entities'—whether particulars or the universal—are mutually different indeed. Of what nature? Having no common welfare...

body.text:
7 taḥ kāraṇāt* / na syāt sāmānyabhedadhīḥ / sāmānyaviśeṣayoḥ parasparasaṃbandhavatī buddhir na syād ity arthaḥ / buddhyabhāvāc ca vyapadeśo 'pi pratikṣipta eva /
v1 /// .. .. .. .. .y. .. .. .. .. .. .. .. .. padeśābhāvokto buddhyabhāvanāntarīyakatvāt* / tadabhāvasya buddhyabhāvo 'py arthāt kathita eveti / tad iti tasmād idaṃ sāmānyaṃ bhedebhyo 'rthāntaraṃ / bhedeṣv anāyattaṃ / kasmāt tair bhedais tasya sāmānyasyājanyatvāt* / dvitīyo 'rthas tad idaṃ bhedātmakaṃ vastu / sāmanyād arthāntaraṃ tasmin sāmānyo ///
body.translated_text:
[7] For this reason, there would be no cognition of universal-and-difference—that is, there would be no cognition relating the universal and the particular to each other. And since the cognition is absent, the verbal designation too is thereby refuted.
[v1] ...the absence of designation has been stated, because it necessarily follows from the absence of cognition. The absence of that [designation] has been stated implicitly through the absence of cognition. 'Tat' means 'therefore': this <s>sāmānya</s> (universal) is a different entity from the differences, not dependent on those differences. Why? Because the <s>sāmānya</s> is not produced by those differences. The second meaning: 'tat' means this entity of the nature of difference; it is a different entity from the universal. In that universal...

body.text: 2 /// .. .. bhedasyedaṃ sāmānyam iti vyapadeśaṃ .ār.. .i / bhedo vā asya sāmānyasyeti / anyāpohe 'pi sāmānye eṣa prasaṃga iti / sa ekasmin vinaśyati / tiṣṭhaty ātmetyādikaḥ / tathā hi dhave khadire vā vinaśyati / avṛkṣavyāvṛttis tiṣṭhaty eva vṛkṣāntare / netyādinā pariharati / ayam atrārthas trividho hy anyāpohaḥ / ekas tāva .y. ///
body.translated_text: [2] ...'this is the universal of this difference'—such a designation...or 'this is the difference of this universal.' [Objection:] 'This same problem applies even to the <s>anyāpoha</s> (exclusion) [theory of] universal'—namely, 'when one [particular] is destroyed, the self persists' and so forth. For example, when a <s>dhava</s> or <s>khadira</s> tree is destroyed, the exclusion-from-non-tree persists in another tree. He refutes this with 'na' etc. The meaning here is: <s>anyāpoha</s> is of three kinds. The first...

body.text: 3 /// .. ha / svabhāvaparabhāvābhyāṃ yasmād vyāvṛtt. + + + + + .. yaṃ ca śabdaliṅgāśrayasya vyavahārasyāśrayatvena vyavasthāpyate / na tu śabdavācyatayā / anyavyavacchedamātraṃ dvitīyaḥ / anyāpohanam anyāpoha iti kṛtvā / yaḥ sarvatrābhedena pūrvācāryaiḥ vyavsthāpyate / pratiṣedhamātrasya sarva .. .i .. .. ṣāt* / vikalpa ///
body.translated_text: [3] ...since it is distinguished from both its own nature and the nature of others...and this is established as the basis of the conventional usage that relies on words and inferential marks—but not as what is expressible by words. The second is mere exclusion of others. <s>Anyāpohanam</s> (exclusion of others) is <s>anyāpoha</s>—taking it thus, which is established by the earlier teachers as undifferentiated everywhere. Since mere negation is everywhere...

body.text: 4 ///.. .. kārasya śābdavācyatayābhimataḥ / ta .. ya .. + .āvṛttaṃ / svalakṣaṇam adhikṛtyocyate / tad ayuktaṃ / tadviṣayasyātmabhūtaṃ tasmin vinaśyati vinaśyaty evābhedāt* / yac ca tiṣṭhati svalakṣaṇāntaraṃ tat tasmād anyad iṣyata eva / yac ca pratiṣedhamātraṃ tasya niḥsvabhāvatvān naitac codyaṃ / tad āha / vyāvṛtter niḥsvabhāvatvād iti / na sthānāsth. .. ka .. ///
body.translated_text: [4] ...is intended as expressible by words...taking the <s>svalakṣaṇa</s> (particular) as the subject, it is said; that is unreasonable. That which is the essence of its object, when that [particular] is destroyed, is destroyed indeed, due to non-difference. And what persists is a different <s>svalakṣaṇa</s>—that is accepted as other than that. And since mere negation has no intrinsic nature, this objection does not apply...

body.text: 5 ///.. iti / iyaṃ sthānāsthānaka + + + + .. tasyety anyāpohasya svabhāvānuṣaṃgiṇyo vastvanupātinyaḥ yāpi vikalpabuddhyākāralakṣaṇānyavyāvṛttiḥ / sa upaplavaś ca vibhramaś ca / sāmānyadhiyo vikalpikāyā buddher ataḥ sāpi bahir nāsty eva yata evaṃ tenāpi viplavatvena kāraṇena sā .. vṛttir adūṣāṇā / .. ///
body.translated_text: [5] ...this [question of] abiding and non-abiding...of that <s>anyāpoha</s> (exclusion), the exclusion-from-others that has the character of a conceptual cognition's aspect, which follows the real entity and accompanies its own nature—that is a disturbance and an error. Of the conceptual cognition that has the universal as its object, therefore that too does not exist externally; since this is so, by that very reason of being erroneous, that...exclusion is not to be faulted...

body.text: 6 /// .. ..ṃ / .. .. .i .. .. .. mithyājñānam eva katham iti ced āha / yad ityādi yasmād ekatra ekākāraṃ tadviṣayasya vikalpavijñānaviṣayasya sāmānyasya na sthitir asthitir vā / kasmāt tasya mithyājñānaviṣayasyābhāvāt* / samānadoṣatām apanīya punaḥ prakārāntareṇa prakrāntaṃ codyaṃ / .. ///
body.translated_text: [6] ...how can this mere false cognition...? If so, he says 'yat' etc.: because in one [entity], of one aspect, there is neither abiding nor non-abiding of the <s>sāmānya</s> (universal) that is the object of the conceptual cognition that is its object. Why? Because of the non-existence of that which is the object of false cognition. Having removed the charge of equal fault, [the opponent] raises the objection again from a different angle...

body.text:
K Pramāṇavārttikaṭīkā
r1 /// .. .ya .v. bhāvaḥ yac ca tasya śālibījasya śālyaṃkurajanakaṃ rūpaṃ tato janakād rūpād anyaḥ pṛthivyādir janakaḥ katham iti / tatrety upanyāse tatra vā codye pratividhīyate / śālibījād anyasya pṛthivyādes tajjanakam aṃkurajanakaṃ rūpaṃ nāstīti na brūmaḥ / kiṃ tarhi yad ekasya ś. ///
body.translated_text:
[K] <s>Pramāṇavārttikaṭīkā</s>
[r1] ...existence, and the form of that rice-seed that generates the rice-sprout—how can another producer, such as earth, be different from that producing form? 'Tatra'—either in that instance, or as a reply to the objection: we do not say that the form of another [cause], such as earth, which generates the sprout, does not exist apart from the rice-seed. Rather, that which is one...

body.text: 2 /// .. rūpeṇeti na śālibījarūpeṇa kiṃ kāraṇam atatvād atatsvabhāvatvāt* / na cātra bādhakaṃ pramāṇam astīty āha / te yathāsvam ityādi te pṛthivyādayaḥ / yathāsvam iti yasya yatsvalakṣaṇaṃ tena bhinnāś ca parasparam ekasya kāryasya janakāś ca svabhāvena prakṛteti ko 'tra virodho / na kaścid bādhakapramāṇābhāvāt* / {svabhāvena vastusthitya} na tu śālyaṃkurajanakābhimatena śālibījarūpeṇa vikalasya pṛthivyādeḥ śālyāmkurakāryatvaviruddham ity atha āha / eka .. ///
body.translated_text: [2] ...'by that form'—not by the form of the rice-seed. Why? Because of not being that, because of not having that nature. And there is no defeating <s>pramāṇa</s> (means of valid cognition) here, he says 'te yathāsvam' etc. 'Te'—earth and the rest. 'Yathāsvam'—each according to its own <s>svalakṣaṇa</s> (particular characteristic); they are different from one another, yet are producers of a single effect by their nature—what contradiction is there here? No defeating...

body.text: 3 /// + + + + + .ibījasvabhāvo na syāt* + .. tkāryaḥ / kiṃtu tatkārya eva / sa śālyaṃkuraḥ kāryam asyeti vigrahaḥ / yadi tu bījasyaivāṃkurajanakatvaṃ syāt* syād virodhas tac ca nāsti / tad āha tenaivetyādi / tenaiveti śālibījenaiva / tatkāryam aṃkurākhyaṃ api cetyādinā pūrvoktaṃ smarayati / ekāpāye phalābhāvād viśeṣebhyas tadudbhava iti ///
body.translated_text: [3] ...the nature of the seed would not exist...having that as its effect. Rather, it has precisely that as its effect. 'That rice-sprout is his effect'—this is the analysis of the compound. If, however, it were the seed alone that had the power of producing the sprout, there would be a contradiction; but that is not the case. He says 'tenaiva' etc. 'Tenaiva'—by the rice-seed alone. 'That effect called the sprout'—with 'api ca' etc. he recalls what was stated earlier. By the removal of one...

body.text: 4 /// .. .. nakarūpeṇa / yad ekasya bījasya janakaṃ + + + nyasya pṛthivyādes tan nāsti na tāvateti / bījarūpavaikalyamātreṇājanakāḥ pṛthivyādayaḥ apy abheda ityādi / teṣu bhedeṣv abhedho 'py astīty arthaḥ / syād etad ityādinā vyācaṣṭe na punas teṣām iti viśeṣāṇāṃ tad evābhinnaṃ rūpam ekaśaktitayā yogāt* / tenety ācāryaḥ / tenābhinnena rūpeṇa te viśeṣā a ///
body.translated_text: [4] ...by the producing form. That which is the producer of one seed...of another [cause] such as earth—that does not exist. Not by the mere deficiency of the seed-form are earth and the rest non-producers. 'Api abheda' etc.—in those differences, there is also non-difference—this is the meaning. With 'syāt etat' etc. he explains: 'Na punas teṣām'—of those particulars, that very non-different form, by virtue of being a single power...

body.text: 5 /// .. .. viśeṣāḥ / tasya sāmānyarūpasya nitya + nānapāyāt* / (in the margin:) /// yarūpena tena sāmānyarūpeṇa te viśeṣā janakāḥ / kiṃ kāraṇaṃ tasya sāmānyarūpasya nityasyānapāyāt* / ekakāraṇasthitāv api kāryotpādaprasaṃgāt* etac ca nāpaity abhinnaṃ tadrūpaṃ viśeṣāḥ khalv apāyinaḥ / ityādinā prāg uktaṃ syātāṃ / nāśotpādau sakṛd ityādinā viruddhadharmādhyāsād bhedaṃ prasādhya pratibhāsabhedenāpi sādhayitum āha / kiñcetyādi / kiṃ viśiṣṭaḥ pratibhāsa ananyabhāk* prati .. ktibhinnaḥ ///
body.translated_text: [5] ...particulars. Of that universal-form, because of its permanence...because there is no departure. (In the margin:) ...by that form, by that universal-form, those particulars are producers. For what reason? Because of the non-departure of that permanent universal-form. Even when only one cause remains, there would be the absurd consequence of the effect arising. And this [universal-form] does not depart, being non-different; but the particulars indeed are departing. With this, as stated before...

body.text: 6 /// .. .. muccīyate / tasyety abhedavādinaḥ buddhipratibhāsabhedaḥ / buddher ākārabhedaḥ vi .. .. + + + .. ś ceti / pṛthagutpattivināśādikaḥ / sati vā tasmiṃ pratibhāsādibhede bhāvānāṃ abhede 'bhyupagamymāne na kvacid bhedakaḥ syāt* / sukhaduḥkhamohacaitanyeṣv api / tathā cety abhede sati ayaṃ pravibhāga iti pratibhāsādipravibhāgaḥ ekātmavat* yathaikasmin sukh. ni na pra .. ///
body.translated_text: [6] ...is released. 'Tasya'—of the advocate of non-difference: the difference in the appearance of cognition, the difference in the aspects of cognition...such as separate arising and destruction, etc. Or, when that difference of appearances etc. exists, if the non-difference of entities is accepted, then there would be no distinguishing factor anywhere—even among pleasure, pain, delusion, and consciousness. 'Tathā ca'—when there is non-difference, this...

body.text:
7 /// .ādhyātmiko bhedo viśeṣa eva parasparavilakṣaṇa eva / kiṃbhūto bhinnapratibhāsādiḥ / bhinnaḥ / pratibhāsādir yasyeti vigrahaḥ / abhinno 'py atra pratibhāso 'sti / tenābhedo 'pīti ced āha / na cātretyādi / atreti bhedeṣu
v1 /// .. tīyaṃ yadbalenābhinnapratibhāsabalena / ato viśeṣa eva bheda eva / na tv abhedo 'pi / sa eva viśeṣo 'rtho vastu / ye tv apare sāmānyadharmā vṛkṣatvādayas tasyaiva vyāvṛttayaḥ kalpitāḥ / tatkāryam ityādi / kāryādi yad asamānādhikaraṇyān napunsakaṃ / anyathā viśeṣasya prakrāntatvāt* sa iti syāt* / tad eva viśeṣarūpaṃ kāryaṃ kāraṇaṃ coktaṃ tad eva svalakṣaṇam ucyate tattyāgāptiphalā iti tasyaiva viśeṣasya / heyasyopā ///
body.translated_text:
[7] ...this internal difference is nothing but a particular—it is mutually distinct indeed. Of what nature? Having distinct appearances etc. 'Different'—whose appearances etc. are different—this is the analysis. [Objection:] There is also a non-different appearance here; therefore non-difference too [is established]. To this he says 'na cātra' etc. 'Atra' means among the differences.
[v1] ...the second, by the force of which—by the force of the non-different appearance—therefore the particular alone, the difference alone...

body.text: 2 /// .. phalaṃ yāsāṃ pravṛttīnāṃ tās tathoktāḥ sa cārthakriyākārī viśeṣa .. .. .. syaiveti viśeṣasyāparasmād vijātīyād bhedo vyāvṛttimātraṃ na tu vastubhūtaṃ kiñcit sāmānyaṃ nāma yadi syāt tadupalabdhilakṣaṇaprāptam* / bhedavyatirekeṇopalabhyeta / yasmān na hi tasya sāmānyasyārthatve vastutve sati dṛśyasya sataḥ rūpānupalakṣaṇaṃ svarūpāgra .. ..ṃ .. .. ///
body.translated_text: [2] ...the result of which activities—those activities are so called. And that which effects purposeful action is the particular...of the particular, the difference from another, from a thing of different class, is mere exclusion—not some real entity called 'universal.' If there were such [a universal], it would satisfy the conditions for being perceived. It would be perceived apart from the differences. Since, when the <s>sāmānya</s> (universal) has real existence...

body.text: 3 /// .. .. deṣv abhedapratyayasya na hi svayam agṛhītapara + nahetuḥ yathā sāṃkhyasyābhedāviśeṣe 'pi na sarvaṃ sarvasādhanaṃ tathā bauddhasya bhedāviśeṣe 'pi kasya punaś codyasyāyaṃ samādhir ity āha / yad uktam ityādi / tajjananasvabhāvād iti / śālyaṃkurajananasvabhāvāt* / bhinnaḥ pṛthivyādi / asyety aṃkurasya kathaṃ janakaḥ syāt* janakatve vā .. .. .. .yamāne bheda .. ///
body.translated_text: [Folio 3] /// ...in those [cases] the cognition of non-difference — for indeed, [something] not itself grasped as other + is not a cause. Just as for the <s>Sāṃkhya</s>, even though there is no distinction in non-difference, not everything is the means of accomplishing everything, so too for the Buddhist, even though there is no distinction in difference. To which objection is this the resolution? He says: 'What was said,' and so forth. 'Because of having the intrinsic nature of generating that' — because of having the intrinsic nature of generating rice sprouts. 'Different' refers to earth and so forth. 'Of this' — how could it be the generator of the sprout? Or if it is accepted as a generator... ... the difference being ascertained... ///

body.text: 4 /// .. .. m idaṃ tu dvitīyam ucyate kiṃ puna .. .. m i .. ha / yadītyādi / tulye 'pi bhede yadi .. .. sya bheda pratiniyatakāryajanakājanakatvalakṣaṇo viśeṣo na syāt* / syād etac codyam iti / yathetyādinā ślokārtham āha / tathā viśeṣe 'pi bhaviṣyati na sarvaḥ sarvasya janaka iti saṃbandhaḥ / vastudharmatayeti vastuśaktyā bhāvānāṃ abhede tv abhyupagamyamāne tasya .. r.. .. ///
body.translated_text: [Folio 4] /// ...but this second [point] is stated: what further... ... He says: 'If,' and so forth. Even though difference is equal, if... the difference characterized by the distinction of being a generator or non-generator of a determinate effect were not to exist. 'This objection would arise' — thus with 'Just as,' and so forth, he states the meaning of the verse: likewise, even in [the case of] difference, not everything will be the generator of everything — such is the connection. 'By the nature of things' (<s>vastudharmatā</s>) — by the power of things; when the non-difference of entities is being accepted, of that... ///

body.text: 5 /// .. tretyādinā vyācaṣṭe / hetur upādānakā + + / pratyayāḥ sahakāriṇaḥ sve hetupratyayāḥ svahetupratyayās tair niyamito viśiṣṭakāryanirvartanasamarthaḥ kṛtaḥ svabhāvo yeṣāṃ te tathoktās tadbhāvas tasmāt* nānya ity akārakābhimatād anye na kārakās syuḥ kiṃ kāraṇaṃ atatsvabhāvatvāt* / atatkāryajananasvabhāvatvāt* / tasyety ekasya traiguṇyasya tatraivety ekasminn eva kārye tatheti .. naivābhinnena .. ///
body.translated_text: [Folio 5] /// ...he explains with 'tretyādinā' and so forth. The cause (<s>hetu</s>) is the material cause + +. The conditions (<s>pratyaya</s>) are the auxiliary causes. 'Their own causes and conditions' — those whose <s>svabhāva</s> (intrinsic nature) has been determined by their own causes and conditions, rendered capable of producing a specific effect, are called such; the state of being that — therefore 'not others,' meaning those other than what is considered a non-agent would not be agents. For what reason? Because of not having that <s>svabhāva</s> — because of not having the intrinsic nature of generating that effect. 'Of that' — of the single <s>traiguṇya</s> (triad of guṇas). 'In that very' — in a single effect. 'Thus' — ...indeed by the undifferentiated... ///

body.text: 6 /// .. .. b. j. yaś ca śālibījasyā .. .. eva + .. bījasyety ekatraikasya kriyākriye prasajyete / tariguṇyasya tena tena sanniveśe .. bhedo 'py asti / ato bhedāt kasyacid akriyā cet* netyādi prativa .. .. .. / bhedaś ced akriyāhetur na kuryaḥ sahakāriṇaḥ teṣām api parasparaṃ bhedāt* / netyādinā vyācaṣṭe sarvākārāvivekaṃ sarvathaikyaṃ kasmād bhedasyāpi ///
body.translated_text: [Folio 6] /// ... and of the rice seed... ...of a single seed — both action and non-action would follow for one and the same. Of the <s>traiguṇya</s> (triad of guṇas), through this or that configuration, ...there is also difference. Therefore, if due to difference there is non-action of something — 'Not,' and so forth, in response... . 'If difference is the cause of non-action, then the auxiliary causes too would not act,' since there is mutual difference among them as well. He explains with 'Not,' and so forth: complete non-discrimination of all aspects — total unity in every respect — why, even though there is difference... ///

body.text: 7 /// .itād avasthābhedāt* / anyathā tatvavādinaḥ sāṃkhyasyābhedo 'pi durlabhaḥ /
body.translated_text: [Folio 7] /// ...because of difference of states. Otherwise, even non-difference would be difficult to obtain for the <s>Sāṃkhya</s>, who asserts that [things are] real.

body.text:
L Pramāṇavārttikaṭīkā
r1 /// .. .. .. .. .. .. .. .. sarvasyopayogād akārakatvam eva nāstīty ata āha / paryāyeṇeti / sa paryāyaḥ kiṃ tasyaivaikasya vastuno naivety arthaḥ / bhedādhiṣṭhānatvāt paryāyasyeti bhāvaḥ / athetyādinā vyācaṣṭe / sarveṣāṃ bhedānāṃ sarvatra kārye paryāyeṇa krameṇa upayogāt* / etac ca yadā pradhānaśakt. .. ///
body.translated_text:
[E] <s>Pramāṇavārttikaṭīkā</s>
[Folio r1] /// ...since everything would be useful, there would be no non-agency at all — therefore he says: 'By turns' (<s>paryāyeṇa</s>). That alternation — is it not of that very single entity? — this is the meaning. Because alternation is grounded in difference — this is the purport. He explains with 'Now,' and so forth: because of the usefulness of all differences in every effect, by turns, in sequence. And this [is the case] when the power of <s>pradhāna</s> (primal matter)... ///

body.text: 2 /// .. .. .. .. .. .. .. + + .. pradhānaśaktir eva vastu satī saivārthakriyāyām upayujyate / bhedāḥ kevalaṃ vyavasthāmātrahetuvaḥ paramārthatas tv asanta eva / tadedam ucyate / śakter vetyādi / traiguṇyalakṣaṇāyāḥ tanniveśinyāḥ pūrvam akārakābhimatapadārthaniveśinyāḥ paścād rūpāntareṇa kārakābhimatarūpeṇa vipariṇatayā ///
body.translated_text: [Folio 2] /// ...the very power of <s>pradhāna</s> (primal matter) is the real entity, and it alone is useful in causal efficacy (<s>arthakriyā</s>). The differences are merely the cause of conventional designation; in ultimate reality, they are entirely non-existent. This is what is stated: 'Of the power,' and so forth. Of that which is characterized by the <s>traiguṇya</s> (triad of guṇas), which inheres in what was previously considered a non-agent, [and] which subsequently, through a different form — in the form considered an agent — has undergone transformation... ///

body.text: 3 /// .. .. .. yasya sat tathoktaḥ ekasya .. .. sya kathaṃ naiva / etena sa kiṃ tasyaiva vastuna ity etad vivṛtaṃ / śakter veti yaduktaṃ / tatrāha vipariṇāmo veti / pūrvasmād avasthābhedād avyatirekiṇyāḥ śākteḥ parimāṇo 'vasthāntaraprāptir vā kathaṃ // atheṣyate pūrvāvasthāyāḥ paścād viśeṣaḥ traiguṇyasya tato viśeṣe vā .. .. ci .. .. .u .. ///
body.translated_text: [Folio 3] /// ...of that which exists, it is called such. Of a single... how indeed not? By this, 'Is that alternation not of that very entity?' — this has been elaborated. 'Of the power' — what was stated regarding that, he responds: 'Transformation,' and so forth. Of the power that is non-different from the prior state — how can there be transformation, i.e., attainment of another state? Now, if it is accepted that there is a distinction of the <s>traiguṇya</s> (triad of guṇas) subsequent to the prior state, then with regard to that distinction... ///

body.text: 4 /// .. .eṣyate / bhedasāmānyayoś ca paraspar. + + da evaṃ ca sati tadvati sāmānyaviśeṣavati vastuni atyantaṃ bhedābhedau syātāṃ / viśeṣebhyaḥ sāmānyasyāvyatirekāt* bhinnaṃ rūpam ity antabhedaḥ sāmānyasyābhāvāt* / sāmānyād viśeṣāṇām avyatirekād aikyam ity antābhedaḥ / sarvathā viśeṣāṇām abhāvāt / ekaṃ bhedasāmā ///
body.translated_text: [Folio 4] /// ...is accepted. And of difference and <s>sāmānya</s> (universal), mutually + + thus, this being the case, in the entity possessing both <s>sāmānya</s> (universal) and <s>viśeṣa</s> (particular), there would be absolute difference and non-difference. Because the <s>sāmānya</s> is non-different from the <s>viśeṣas</s> (particulars), its form is different — this is internal difference, due to the absence of <s>sāmānya</s> [as separate]. Because the <s>viśeṣas</s> are non-different from <s>sāmānya</s>, there is unity — this is internal non-difference, due to the absence of <s>viśeṣas</s> in every respect. A single difference-<s>sāmānya</s>... ///

body.text: 5 /// / sadṛśāsadṛśātmanoḥ sāmānyaviśeṣayo .. .. vāś ced bhedina iti saṃbandhaḥ / abhinnenātmanā pradhānākhyena teṣām eva bhedānāṃ sātmabhūtena tadvantaḥ / syur abhinnasvabhāvavantaḥ syuḥ // abhinnaḥ svabhāvaḥ pradhānākhya ātmā rūpaṃ yasya bhedasya sa tadabhinnasvabhāvātmā tadbhāvas tasmād bhedasyāpi kutaḥ / parasparaṃ bhedo naiva anenā ///
body.translated_text: [Folio 5] /// ...of the similar and dissimilar selves — of <s>sāmānya</s> (universal) and <s>viśeṣa</s> (particular)... ...if they are different — the connection is: 'the differents.' By the undifferentiated self called <s>pradhāna</s> (primal matter), which is the very self of those differences, they are possessed of that — they would have an undifferentiated <s>svabhāva</s> (intrinsic nature). The undifferentiated <s>svabhāva</s> — the self called <s>pradhāna</s> — is the nature of that difference; the state of being that — therefore whence could there be mutual difference even of differences? By this... ///

body.text: 6 /// ..ḥ ātmā na bhavati .. dasyānekātmakatvāt* / .. .. s. .. .. dātmanā bhedātmanā tenāpi sāmānyapadārthena / tatheti sāmānyātmanā bhavituṃ na yuktaṃ bhedād avyatiriktatvāt sāmānyasya samānatā nāstīty arthaḥ / etenātyantabhedo vyākhyātaḥ tathābhāve hīti / sāmānyātmakatve pradhānasyeṣyamāṇe pradhānātmātaddharmā bhedadharmā na syāt* / avya ///
body.translated_text: [Folio 6] /// ...the self does not exist... because of having many selves. ...by the self of difference, by that <s>sāmānya</s> (universal) as well. 'Thus' — it is not proper for it to exist as having the nature of <s>sāmānya</s>, because <s>sāmānya</s> is non-different from difference — there is no sameness — this is the meaning. By this, absolute difference has been explained. 'If such were not the case' — if the <s>sāmānya</s>-nature of <s>pradhāna</s> (primal matter) were accepted, then the self of <s>pradhāna</s> would not have the property of difference — the <s>dharma</s> (property) of difference would not exist. Non-dif... ///

body.text: 7 /// .ān na syād ity arthaḥ / avasthātadvatoḥ parasparaṃ bhedaḥ syād iti yāvat* / tam eva sādhayann āha / na hy ayam ityādi / ayam ekasvabhāvaḥ / pravṛttinivṛttimān na yukta iti saṃbandhaḥ / sthānaṃ pravṛttiḥ / vigamo nivṛttiḥ / tathā hi sthitāyāṃ śaktau avasthānāṃ nivṛttir iṣyate / etenānyonyaṃ vā tayor bheda ityādi vyākhyātam* / netyādinā parābhiprāyam āśaṃkate sāmā ///
body.translated_text: [Folio 7] /// ...would not exist — this is the meaning. There would be mutual difference between state and the possessor of state — this much [is intended]. Establishing precisely that, he says: 'For this,' and so forth. 'This' — having a single <s>svabhāva</s> (intrinsic nature). The connection is: it is not proper [for it to have] engagement and withdrawal. 'Remaining' is engagement. 'Departure' is withdrawal. For thus, when the power remains, the cessation of states is accepted. By this, 'Or the mutual difference of those two,' and so forth, has been explained. With 'Not,' and so forth, he raises the opponent's intended [objection] regarding <s>sāmānya</s> (universal)... ///

body.text: 8 /// .. .. kiṃtu tayor api bhedasāmānyayor bhedo bhaved yadi / kvacid bhede sāmānye vā asya sāṃkhyasya bhedo 'bhedo vā aikāntiko na hīti saṃbandhaḥ / ekatvavāditvāt parasya bheda aikāntiko nāstīti gamyata evābhedas tu katham aikāntiko nety atra kāraṇam āha / vivekenetyādi / sāmānyaṃ śaktiḥ vyaktayo viśeṣā ity evaṃ bhedena vyavasthānāt* / yenetyādy ā .. .. ///
body.translated_text: [Folio 8] /// ...but if there were also difference between those two — difference and <s>sāmānya</s> (universal) — then with regard to either difference or <s>sāmānya</s>, for this <s>Sāṃkhya</s>, neither difference nor non-difference would be absolute — such is the connection. Since the opponent holds the doctrine of oneness, it is understood that difference is not absolute; but how is non-difference also not absolute? — for this reason he states the cause: 'By distinction,' and so forth. <s>Sāmānya</s> is the power (<s>śakti</s>), and the <s>vyaktis</s> (manifestations) are the <s>viśeṣas</s> (particulars) — thus by such differentiation there is conventional determination. 'By which,' and so forth... ///

body.text: v1 1 /// .. .. .. sāmānyam ity etad yenātmanā vyavasthāpyate yadi .. .. tmanā sāmānyaviśeṣayor bhedās tadā bheda evātyantaṃ yadītyādinā vyācaṣṭe / yam ātmānam iti śaktivyaktyātmakaṃ / tenātmanā sāmānyaviśeṣayor yadi bheda iti saṃbandhaḥ / etad eva sphuṭayann āha yasmād ityādi / tau hi bhedavyasthāpakāv ātmānau tayor iti sāmāny. ///
body.translated_text: [Folio v1, 1] /// ...'<s>sāmānya</s> (universal)' — that by which self it is determined, if... by that self, if there is difference of <s>sāmānya</s> and <s>viśeṣa</s>, then there is absolute difference only. He explains with 'If,' and so forth. 'That self' — having the nature of <s>śakti</s> (power) and <s>vyakti</s> (manifestation). The connection is: if by that self there is difference of <s>sāmānya</s> and <s>viśeṣa</s>. Making this very point clearer, he says: 'Because,' and so forth. For those two — the selves that establish difference — of those two, the <s>sāmānya</s>... ///

body.text: 2 /// bhūtau tau ced vyatirekiṇau parasparabhinnau tadā vyatireka e + + bheda eva / kiṃ kāraṇaṃ svabhāvabhedāt* / syāt matam avasthāvasthātror bhedavyavasthāpako bhāva eva bhidyate na svabhāva ity āha / svabhāvo hītyādi / svabhāva eva bhāva ity arthaḥ / tathā ceti bhedasāmānyayo{r iti sāmānyaviśeṣayoḥ svātmanau svabhāvabhūtau tau ced vyatirekiṇau paraspa ///
body.translated_text: [Folio 2] /// ...being such, if those two are separable — mutually distinct — then there is separateness only + + difference only. For what reason? Because of difference of <s>svabhāva</s> (intrinsic nature). One might think: of states and their possessor, the entity that establishes the differentiation is itself differentiated, not the <s>svabhāva</s> — to this he says: 'For <s>svabhāva</s>,' and so forth. <s>Svabhāva</s> indeed is the entity — this is the meaning. 'And thus' — of difference and <s>sāmānya</s> {that is, of <s>sāmānya</s> and <s>viśeṣa</s> — their own selves, being of the nature of <s>svabhāva</s>, if those two are separable, mutually... ///

body.text: 3 /// bheda eva kiṃ kāraṇaṃ svabhāvabhedāt* / syāt matam avasthātror bhedavyavasthāpako bhāva eva bhidyate na svabhāva ity āha} r atyantabhede sati bhedasya niḥsāmānyatā sāmānyasya nirviśeṣatā syād iti saṃbandhaḥ / sāmānyasya bhedavatvaṃ bhedānāṃ ca sāmānyavatvaṃ na syād asaṃbhavād iti yāvat* / yadvadghaṭādīnāṃ bhedānāṃ saṃbandhābhāvāt parasparaṃ tadvattā nāsti .. ///
body.translated_text: [Folio 3] /// ...difference only. For what reason? Because of difference of <s>svabhāva</s>. One might think: of states and their possessor, the entity that establishes the differentiation is itself differentiated, not the <s>svabhāva</s> — to this he says:} When there is absolute difference, the connection is: difference would be without <s>sāmānya</s> (universal), and <s>sāmānya</s> would be without <s>viśeṣa</s> (particular). The possession of difference by <s>sāmānya</s>, and the possession of <s>sāmānya</s> by differences, would not exist — due to impossibility, this much [is meant]. Just as among pots and such differences, due to the absence of relation, there is no mutual possession of one by the other... ///

body.text: 4 /// .. nakatvena saṃbandhābhāvāt* uktam iti na syāt sāmānyabhedadhīr ity atrāntare / atha vā asthāne 'yaṃ yatnaḥ kriyate paraiḥ / kalpitaṃ sāmānyaṃ svalakṣaṇād bhinnaṃ / kiṃ vā neti tad dhi nityam iṣyate / parais tataś cānarthakriyākāritvāc chaśaviṣāṇaprakhyaṃ / tatrārthakriyārthinaḥ .. .. bhedābhedacinta ///
body.translated_text: [Folio 4] /// ...due to the absence of relation as cause — it has been stated — thus the cognition of difference-in-<s>sāmānya</s> would not arise, in this interval. Alternatively, this effort is made by the opponents in the wrong place. The <s>sāmānya</s> (universal) is a conceptual construction (<s>vikalpa</s>), different from the <s>svalakṣaṇa</s> (particular). Or is it not? — for that [universal] is held to be permanent. By the opponents, and consequently, since it has no causal efficacy (<s>arthakriyā</s>), it is like a hare's horn. In that case, for one who seeks causal efficacy... ...the investigation of difference and non-difference... ///

body.text: 5 /// .. .. m anyatra yathā parikalpitāyā vyāvṛ .. ty etad darśayitum āhāpi cetyādi / yam ātmānam arthakriyāyogyaṃ puraskṛtyālaṃbanīkṛtya tatsādhyaphalavāñchāvān* tenātmanā yatsādhyaṃ phalaṃ tadabhilāṣavān* / ayaṃ puruṣaḥ pravartate / tadāśrayau tadadhiṣṭhānau bhedābhedau cintyete / tasya cārthakriyāyogyasya svā .. ///
body.translated_text: [Folio 5] /// ...elsewhere, just as the imagined exclusion (<s>vyāvṛtti</s>) ... — to show this, he says 'api ca' and so forth. The self (<s>ātman</s>) that is capable of <s>arthakriyā</s> (causal efficacy) — having placed it before, having taken it as an object — one who desires the result to be accomplished by it, one who has the wish for the result to be accomplished by that self — this person engages in activity. The two, difference and non-difference, which are based on it, which have it as their substratum, are considered. And of that which is capable of <s>arthakriyā</s> (causal efficacy), its own ... ///

body.text: 6 /// .. lpabuddhipratibhāsānurodhinyā kṛtavya .. .. .. samānatā asty evādhyavasitatadbhāvā iyataivārthakriyārthino bhedābhedacintā / samāptā tato 'narthakriyākāriṇaḥ sāmānyasya kiṃ svalakṣaṇena / bhedābhedacintayeti / vastv eva sāmānyam astu kiṃ parikalpitayā vyāvṛtyety āha / vastu nānvetīti svalakṣaṇānāṃ parasparaṃ .. ///
body.translated_text: [Folio 6] /// ...in conformity with the appearance in <s>vikalpa</s> (conceptual construction), what must be done ... ... sameness indeed exists as having the nature of what is determined — to this extent alone is the consideration of difference and non-difference for one who desires <s>arthakriyā</s> (causal efficacy) completed. Then, of <s>sāmānya</s> (the universal) which does not produce <s>arthakriyā</s> (causal efficacy), what [connection] with the <s>svalakṣaṇa</s> (particular)? — in the consideration of difference and non-difference. Let the real thing itself be the <s>sāmānya</s> (universal); what need is there for an imagined <s>vyāvṛtti</s> (exclusion)? — to this he says: 'The real thing does not follow,' meaning the <s>svalakṣaṇas</s> (particulars) mutually ... ///

body.text: 7 /// .. .. r.. ta / tad āha pravṛtyādītyādi / ādiśabdāt tulyotpattinirodhādiprasaṃgataḥ / sarva evetyādinā vyācaṣṭe / viśeṣam evārthakriyāyogyaṃ / svabhāvākhyam ātmabhūtam ity arthaḥ / kasya bhāvasya vastuno 'dhikṛtya pravartate / sa eva hīty arthakriyākārī viśeṣaḥ / tatheti gaur ityādiśabdaiḥ arthakriyārthī hi svalakṣa ///
body.translated_text: [Folio 7] /// ... He says 'pravṛtti' and so forth. From the word 'ādi' (and so forth), because of the consequence of equal origination, cessation, and so forth. He explains with 'sarva eva' (all indeed) and so forth. The particular alone is capable of <s>arthakriyā</s> (causal efficacy), called <s>svabhāva</s> (intrinsic nature), meaning: constituting the essence. With regard to what entity, what real thing, does one engage in activity? For it is indeed he — the particular — that performs <s>arthakriyā</s> (causal efficacy). 'Thus' — by words such as 'cow' and so forth, one who desires <s>arthakriyā</s> (causal efficacy) indeed [acts toward] the <s>svalakṣaṇa</s> (particular) ... ///

body.text: 8 /// .. .. .i .. .aiva prati + + + tato vyavahartṛṇām adhyavasāyavaśāt* / śabdavyāpārāpekṣayā etad uktaṃ / śābde tu jñāne svalakṣaṇapratibhāso nāstīti svalakṣaṇam avācyam uktam ity avirodhaḥ / dravyatvādayas tu tatreti gaur ityādiśabdair gavādicodanāyāṃ / kasmād yathāsvaṃ dravyatvādiśabdais teṣāṃ dravyāt pṛthagabhidhān. ///
body.translated_text: [Folio 8] /// ... toward that very ... therefore, due to the <s>adhyavasāya</s> (determination) of those who engage in practical activity. This is said with regard to the operation of words. But in verbal cognition, since there is no appearance of the <s>svalakṣaṇa</s> (particular), the <s>svalakṣaṇa</s> has been said to be inexpressible — thus there is no contradiction. 'Substancehood and so forth, however, in that' — by words such as 'cow' and so forth, in the injunction regarding cows and such. Why? By the respective words 'substancehood' and so forth, their designation as separate from the substance ... ///

body.text:
M Pramāṇavārttikaṭīkā
r1 /// .. tyādi / arthasya gavādes tena gotvādinā sāmānyenāvyabhicārāt* / tato 'rthād gatiḥ sāmānyānāṃ syān na tu viśeṣaśabdaḥ sāmānye vyāpriyate nirloṭhitaṃ caitad ācāryadiṅnāgena sāmānyaparīkṣādau yathā viśeṣaśabdānāṃ na sāmānye vṛttir iti / atra codyate .. .. .u ..ḥ sāmānya .. ///
body.translated_text:
M. <s>Pramāṇavārttikaṭīkā</s>
[Folio r1] /// ...and so forth. Because of the invariable concomitance of the object — cow and such — with that <s>sāmānya</s> (universal) such as cow-ness. Therefore, the cognition of the <s>sāmānyas</s> (universals) would be from the object [itself], but the particular-word does not operate upon the <s>sāmānya</s> (universal). And this has been thoroughly examined by <s>ācārya</s> <s>Dignāga</s> in the investigation of universals (<s>Sāmānyaparīkṣā</s>), namely that particular-words do not function with regard to the universal. Here an objection is raised ... ... the <s>sāmānya</s> (universal) ... ///

body.text: 2 /// tad api .. d eva / tathā vikalpabuddhipratibhāsasya na bāhyena dravyeṇāvyabhicārā sti tasya svatantratvāt* / ucyate svalakṣaṇam eva sajātīyavyāvṛttaṃ viśeṣas tad eva vijātīyavyāvṛttim apekṣyābhedenopāttaṃ sāmānyam ity ucyate / tataḥ sāmānyaviśeṣayor vastuta ekatvāt kṛ ///
body.translated_text: [Folio 2] /// ...that too ... indeed. Thus, the appearance in <s>vikalpa</s> (conceptual cognition) has no invariable concomitance with an external substance, due to its being autonomous. It is replied: the <s>svalakṣaṇa</s> (particular) itself, being excluded from those of the same class, is the <s>viśeṣa</s> (particular); that very same [particular], when apprehended non-differently with reference to exclusion from those of a different class, is called <s>sāmānya</s> (universal). Therefore, since <s>sāmānya</s> and <s>viśeṣa</s> are in reality one ... ///

body.text: 3 /// .. bhedāt tu kevalaṃ kvacic chābdī pratipatti / kvacid ārthīty ucyate / tad iti tasmād ayaṃ puruṣaḥ / gavādipratyupasthāpitaṃ gavādiśabdasaṃnipātitam arthakriyāśrayaṃ / arthāntarasya sāmānyasyopanyāsena / bhedasāmānyākāratayā dvimukhā buddhir yasya sa tathoktaḥ / yo 'sya gavāder ātmā svabhāvaḥ ananyabhāgasādhāraṇaḥ ///
body.translated_text: [Folio 3] /// ...but due to [conceptual] differentiation alone, in some cases there is verbal cognition, in some cases object-based cognition — so it is said. 'That' — therefore this person; what is presented through [the word] 'cow' and so forth, what is brought about by the word 'cow' and so forth — the substratum of <s>arthakriyā</s> (causal efficacy). By the introduction of another thing, namely <s>sāmānya</s> (the universal), the cognition that is two-faced, having the aspects of both difference and universality — he who has such [cognition] is so described. That which is the self, the <s>svabhāva</s> (intrinsic nature) of the cow and so forth, not shared with any other aspect ... ///

body.text: 4 /// yam arthaṃ .. .. .. mantaṃ puraskṛtyety ālaṃba + / kṛtya viśiṣṭārthakriyārthī tām evāha yathetyādi / yathā gor vāhadohādāv arthī gām eva puraskṛtya pravartate / anyasaṃbhavina iti gor anyasminn aśve saṃbhavino 'rthasyārthī gāṃ puraskṛtya na pravartata iti vākyārthaḥ / samarthanīyaḥ ko 'rtho 'nyasaṃbhavīty āha / yathā yuddha .. vesa iti .. ///
body.translated_text: [Folio 4] /// ...this object ... having placed before, meaning: having taken as object ... desiring a specific <s>arthakriyā</s> (causal efficacy), he states that very [point] with 'yathā' and so forth. Just as one who desires the cow for draft-work, milking, and so forth engages in activity having placed the cow before. 'Of what occurs in another' — one who desires a purpose that occurs in another, namely a horse, [but] having placed the cow before, does not engage — this is the meaning of the sentence. What is the meaning of 'occurring in another' that needs to be explained? He says: 'Just as in battle ... ves' thus ... ///

body.text:
5 /// ..ṃ .. ditam iti .. .. pariṇāmena sa .. .. + .. .c. danayā gavādīnāṃ bhedā .. gavādiśabdaiś codanayā tadety arthaḥ / kriyārthinaḥ pravṛttikāle prāptum anabhipretatvāt* dravyādisāmānyasyeti vibhaktivipariṇāmena saṃbandhaḥ / satyaṃ gavādayo viśeṣāś codyante 'rthakriyārthibhis te tu bhedā dravya
v1 /// .. .. .. ity ata āha / gavādisamāveśād iti / avyatirekavādinaḥ sāṃkhyasya gavādiṣu bhedeṣu sāmānyatāṃ samāveśāt tādātmyenānupraveśād gavādisvabhāvatvād iti yāvat* / bhedasvabhāvatvaṃ sāmānyānām iṣṭam eveti ced ity āha tadātmabhūtānāṃ ceti / gavādisvabhāvānāṃ sāmānyānāṃ / gavādiva .. .. ///
body.translated_text:
[Folio 5] /// ... ... by transformation ... by the injunction of cows and such, the differences of cows and so forth ... by words such as 'cow' and so forth, by that injunction — this is the meaning. At the time of engagement by one who desires action, because of the unintendedness of attaining the universal of substancehood and so forth — the connection is through case-ending transformation. Truly, the particulars such as cow and so forth are enjoined by those who desire <s>arthakriyā</s> (causal efficacy); but those differences are substance —
[Folio v1] /// ... therefore he says 'gavādisamāveśāt' (because of the inclusion in cows and such). For the <s>Sāṃkhya</s>, who holds the doctrine of non-difference, because of the inclusion, i.e., entry through identity, into the differences such as cow and so forth — meaning: because of having the nature of cow and so forth — this much. If it is said that it is accepted that <s>sāmānyas</s> (universals) have the nature of differences, he says 'tadātmabhūtānāṃ ca' — of <s>sāmānyas</s> (universals) that have the nature of cow and so forth. The cow and so forth ... ... ///

body.text: 2 /// .. .. mānya .. śeṣa rūpatvād eveti + vat* / tataś ca viśeṣa eva codyate tad evāha tam evetyādi / tam eva cānanyasādhāraṇaṃ bhāvam ayam arthakriyārthī puruṣo bhedābhedaprakāraiḥ paryanuyuṃkute / anyāpohavādinā 'pi vyāvṛttilakṣaṇo dravyatvādyabhedaḥ svalakṣaṇād iṣṭas tato 'tyantabhedo viśeṣāṇāṃ viruddha ///
body.translated_text: [Folio 2] /// ...universal ... particular — precisely because of having the form ... thus. And therefore it is the particular alone that is enjoined — he states this very point with 'tam eva' and so forth. That very entity which is not shared with anything else — this person who desires <s>arthakriyā</s> (causal efficacy) investigates it through the modes of difference and non-difference.
