Even for the proponent of <s>anyāpoha</s> (exclusion of the other), the non-difference of substancehood and such, characterized by <s>vyāvṛtti</s> (exclusion), is accepted as [belonging to] the <s>svalakṣaṇa</s> (particular); therefore the absolute difference of particulars is contradicted ... ///

body.text: 3 /// .. .. vyatvādyabhedo 'sya .. syābādhaka eva tasya kalpitatvāt* tasmāt pāramārthiko bhedaḥ svalakṣaṇānām upakalpitam ekatvam anena ca prakāreṇa bhedābhedāv iṣṭāv asmābhis tad eva darśayann āha / sarvatretyādi / sāmānyasya ca vyāvṛttilakṣaṇasyābhyupagamād iti saṃbandhaḥ / na vyāvṛttirūpeṇa sāmānye ///
body.translated_text: [Folio 3] /// ...the non-difference of substancehood and such ... is merely a non-obstructor of it, due to its being constructed. Therefore the difference of <s>svalakṣaṇas</s> (particulars) is ultimately real; their unity is superimposed. And in this manner, both difference and non-difference are accepted by us — showing this very point, he says 'sarvatra' and so forth. Because the <s>sāmānya</s> (universal) characterized by <s>vyāvṛtti</s> (exclusion) is acknowledged — this is the connection. Not in the form of exclusion, in the <s>sāmānya</s> (universal) ... ///

body.text: 4 /// uktam iti sāmānyād avyatirekād bhedānām aikyaṃ bhedavad eva vā / sāmānyasyāpy anekatvam ity uktaṃ prāṅ na sāmānyam aṅgīkṛtya bhedānām aikyam ucyate / kiṃtu yo 'sau viśeṣas tenaivābheda ity āha / svātmanaivetyādi / svenaiva viśeṣarūpeṇa gavāśvādīnām abhede tad. .. dravyaṃ ni ///
body.translated_text: [Folio 4] /// ...has been said: 'Due to non-difference from the universal, either the unity of the differences is like the difference itself, or the universal too would be manifold' — thus it was said previously. It is not that unity of the differences is asserted by accepting a [real] <s>sāmānya</s> (universal). Rather, the non-difference is by that very <s>viśeṣa</s> (particular) itself — he says 'svātmanaiva' (by its own self) and so forth. By its own particular form, the non-difference of cow, horse, and so forth — that ... substance is determined ... ///

body.text: 5 /// vaḥ / dvayor iti gavi cāśve ca / yasmād eko 'pi hi kāraṇatvenābhimato gopadārthaḥ tatāṃ arthakriyāṃ vāhaodhasvabhāvāṃ tatsvabhāvatvāt* / tadarthakriyākaraṇasvabhāvatvād eva karoti / tadanyasyāpi tasmād godravyād anyasyāpi aśvasya tad vāhadoha .. .. ra .. .. ///
body.translated_text: [Folio 5] /// ... 'Of two' — in the cow and in the horse. Since even a single entity accepted as a cause — the object denoted by the word 'cow' — performs that <s>arthakriyā</s> (causal efficacy), which has the nature of draft-work, milking, and so forth, precisely because of having that nature, precisely because of having the nature of performing that <s>arthakriyā</s>. Of another too — of another [entity] besides that cow-substance, of the horse as well, that [capacity for] draft-work, milking ... ... ///

body.text:
N Pramāṇavārttikaṭīkā
r1 /// .. .. .. v. t. s. v. + .. sya bheda .. .. .. na ahrīkā nagnatayā / nirlajjaḥ kṣapalakāḥ ayuktābhidhānasya kusmitatvāt kim apīty āha / aślīlaṃ grāmyaṃ / sarvaḥ sarvasvabhāvo na ca sarvasvabhāva iti yat pralapanti pratikṣiptaṃ tad api / kasmād ekāntasaṃbhāvād ekasyaivāntasyātyantabhedaprakārasya saṃbhavāt syād uṣṭro dadhisvalakṣaṇasyaikyāt syān na dadhi avasthābhedād aślīlam ity asya vyākhyānam ayuktam i /// aślīlam ity asya grāmyaparyāyatvāt / aheyopādeyam iti / atyājyām agrāhyaṃ ca / kasmād apariniṣṭhānāt* / yadi hi kiṃcit sukhasādhana .. .. .iścitam anyac ca duḥ .. ///
body.translated_text:
N. <s>Pramāṇavārttikaṭīkā</s>
[Folio r1] /// ... ... the difference of that ... without shame, due to nakedness — the shameless <s>kṣapalakas</s> (mendicants). Because of the impropriety of the statement, why does he say this? He says: '<s>aślīla</s>' (vulgar). What they babble — 'everything has every nature and yet does not have every nature' — that too has been refuted. Why? Because of the occurrence of an absolute [consequence] — because of the occurrence of only one extreme, the mode of absolute difference: a camel, due to the identity of the <s>svalakṣaṇa</s> (particular) of curd, would become curd; and curd, due to difference of states, would not be [curd] — the explanation of '<s>aślīla</s>' (vulgar) as such is improper ... /// '<s>aślīla</s>' (vulgar), being a synonym of '<s>grāmya</s>' (crude). 'Neither to be rejected nor to be adopted' — meaning: neither to be abandoned nor to be grasped. Why? Because of non-finality. For if something were ascertained as a means to happiness ... ... and another as [a means to] suffering ... ///

body.text: 2 /// .. svabhāvatvān na ca sarvasvabhāvatvāt* / ataś cākulam ekasyāntasya grahītum aśakyatvāt* / tadanvaye vā tasya svabhāvabhedasya paraparam anvaye vā sarvasyobhayarūpatvaṃ ubhayagrahaṇam anekatvopalakṣaṇaṃ tasmin sati / tadviśeṣasya uṣṭra uṣṭra eva na dadhi / dadhi dadhy eva noṣṭra ity evaṃlakṣaṇasya nirākṛteḥ dadhi khādety e .. ///
body.translated_text: [Folio 2] /// ...because of not having every nature, and yet not because of having every nature. And therefore it is confused — because one extreme cannot be grasped. In the case of the entailment of that — of that difference of nature — the mutual entailment, or the duality of form of everything, the grasping of both (which is indicative of multiplicity) — when that obtains, the refutation of the distinction of that — a camel is a camel alone and not curd, curd is curd alone and not a camel — of this nature. 'Eat the curd,' and ... ///

body.text: 3 /// .. kāreṇa syād dadhi / nāpi sa evoṣṭra evoṣṭra ity ekāntavādaḥ / yenānyo 'pi dadhyādikaḥ syād uṣṭraḥ tathā dadhy api syād uṣṭraḥ nāpi tad eva dadhy eva yenānyad apy uṣṭrādikaṃ syād dadhi etena sarvasyobhayarūpatvaṃ vyākhyātaṃ / tadviśeṣanirākṛter ity etat tad anayor ityādinā vyācaṣṭe / ubhayathā hi da .u .. .. .. viśeṣaḥ syā ///
body.translated_text: [Folio 3] /// ...in this manner, it would be curd. Nor is the absolutist position that it is a camel and a camel alone [tenable] — by which another thing such as curd would also be a camel, and likewise curd too would be a camel. Nor is it that very thing as curd alone — by which another thing such as a camel would also be curd. By this, the statement 'everything has a dual form' has been explained. 'Because of the refutation of the distinction of that' — he explains this with 'tad anayor' (of these two) and so forth. For in both ways, curd ... ... the distinction would be ... ///

body.text: 4 /// .. dy uṣṭrasvarūpa eva niyataṃ syāt* / evaṃ dadhno 'pi vācyaṃ / ādyasya tāvad asaṃbhavas tad ityādinā kathyate tad evam anayor dadhyuṣṭrayor na kaścid viśeṣa iti saṃbandhaḥ / ekasyāpīty dadhna uṣṭrasya vā kasyacit tadrūpābhāvasya uṣṭrarūpābhāvasya dadhirūpabhāvasya cābhāvāt* / dvitīyasyāpi prakārasyābhāvam āha svarūpasyetyādi / a .. .. .. ///
body.translated_text: [Folio 4] /// ...curd would necessarily be of the very nature of a camel. The same is to be said of curd as well. The impossibility of the first [option] is stated with 'tad' and so forth — thus of these two, curd and camel, there is no distinction whatsoever — this is the connection. 'Even of one' — of curd or of the camel, of whichever — because of the absence of the absence of that form, the absence of the camel-form, and the absence of the curd-form. He states the impossibility of the second mode as well, with 'svarūpasya' (of the own-form) and so forth ... ... ///

body.text: 5 /// yatasya uṣṭrasvabhāvaniyatasya dadhisvabhāvaniyatasya cābhāvāt* / athāsti dadhyuṣṭrayor atiśayaḥ kaścid yenātiśayena dadhi khādeti coditaḥ puruṣo bhedena vartate / uṣṭraparihāreṇa dadhy eva pravartate / sa evātiśāyo dadhi sa cānyatroṣṭro nāsti anubhayaṃ vibhaktasvarūpaṃ sarvaṃ vastu .. .. .. paramārthaḥ ekatvaṃ tu ///
body.translated_text: [Folio 5] /// ...because of the absence of that which is determined to have the <s>svabhāva</s> (intrinsic nature) of a camel and that which is determined to have the <s>svabhāva</s> of curd. Now, if there is some distinguishing feature (<s>atiśaya</s>) of curd and camel, by which distinguishing feature a person instructed 'eat curd' acts differentially — avoiding the camel, he engages with curd alone — that very distinguishing feature is curd, and that which is other, the camel, does not exist [as curd]. Everything that is not both, having a distinct own-form, is every entity... the ultimate reality; oneness, however, /// [is merely constructed]

body.text: 6 /// .. .. .. .. .. .. .. vyākhye .. + + + + + . iti dadhikṣīrayoḥ tathā codita iti dadhi khādeti coditaḥ puruṣo bhedena vartate / uṣṭraparihāreṇa dadhy eva pravartate / sa evātiśayo dadhi sa sānyatroṣṭre nāstīti anubhayaṃ vibhaktasvarūpaṃ sarvaṃ vastu tad eva paramārthaḥ ekatvaṃ tu kalpitaṃ / dadhnaivāparam uṣṭrādikam anubhavarūpam itiy vyākhyeyam* / .. .. ///
body.translated_text: [Folio 6] /// ...... to be explained... thus of curd and milk, likewise: 'instructed' means a person instructed 'eat curd' acts differentially — avoiding the camel, he engages with curd alone. That very distinguishing feature is curd, and that which is other, in the camel, does not exist — thus everything that is not both, having a distinct own-form, is every entity; that alone is the ultimate reality (<s>paramārtha</s>); oneness, however, is constructed (<s>kalpita</s>). This should be explained as: by curd alone, the other — camel and such — is of the nature of experience... ///

body.text: 7 /// codita iti dadhi khādeti coditaḥ / kṣīravikāro dadhi nānyatrety uṣṭre / sa evātiśayo dadhi kiṃbhūta arthakriyārthipravṛttiviṣayaḥ dadhisādhyārthakriyā .. tayā yo 'rthī puruṣas tasya pravṛttiviṣayaḥ kiṃ kāraṇaṃ tatphaletyādi / dadhnaiva sādhyatvāt phalaviśeṣaḥ saivāsau viśeṣaś ceti vigrahaḥ / tasyopādānabhāvo hetubhāvas tena lakṣitaḥ svabhāvo yasya vastunas tad e .. .. .i .i ///
body.translated_text: [Folio 7] /// ...'instructed' means a person instructed 'eat curd.' Curd is a transformation of milk, not elsewhere — i.e., not in the camel. That very distinguishing feature is curd — of what character? It is the object of engagement of one who desires <s>arthakriyā</s> (causal efficacy): the <s>arthakriyā</s> accomplishable by curd... the person who desires that, it is the object of his engagement. What is the reason? 'Its result,' and so forth. Because it is accomplishable only by curd, the particular result — that alone is the particular, and thus is the analysis. Its being the material cause is its being the cause; the <s>svabhāva</s> characterized by that, of which entity, that... ///

body.text: 8 /// dadhisvabhāvaḥ / anyatrety uṣṭre / kasmāt* / dadhyarthinas tatroṣṭre pravṛtyabhāvāt* / bhinnau niyatārthau / dhīdhvanī jñānaṃ śabdaś ca / tadabhāvāt* bhinnabuddhiśabdabhāvāt* / bhedānāṃ saṃhāravādasya / ekīkaraṇavādasyāsaṃbhavaḥ / bhedena gṛhītayoḥ śrutayor vā ekatvenopasaṃharo nirdeśaḥ syād uṣṭro dadhītyādi / so 'yam ityādinā vyācaṣṭe / kva ///
body.translated_text: [Folio 8] /// ...has the <s>svabhāva</s> of curd. 'Elsewhere' means in the camel. Why? Because of the absence of engagement of one who desires curd there, in the camel. The two are distinct and have determined objects. 'Cognition and sound' (<s>dhīdhvanī</s>) means <s>jñāna</s> (cognition) and <s>śabda</s> (word). 'Because of the absence of that' means because of the existence of distinct cognitions and words. The impossibility of the doctrine of unification (<s>saṃhāravāda</s>) of distinctions — i.e., the impossibility of the doctrine of making into one (<s>ekīkaraṇavāda</s>). There would be a statement of subsumption (<s>upasaṃhāra</s>) as one of things apprehended or heard as distinct — such as 'the camel is curd,' and so forth. He explains with 'that very one,' and so forth. Where /// [does this apply?]

body.text:
9 /// .. m ākāram apaśyan* kathaṃ buddhyādhimucyetārthān iti saṃbandhaḥ / kiṃ viśiṣṭayā buddhyety āhāsaṃsṛṣṭetyādi /
v1 /// ro yasminn arthe sa tathoktaḥ / sa yasyā buddher asti sā asaṃsṛṣṭānyākāravatī vibhaktārthagrāhiṇyeti yāvat* / abhilaped vā kathaṃ pratiniyatasaṃketena dhvaninety ākūtaṃ / kasmān nādhimucyetety āha / vibhāgābhāvād bhāvānām iti tatsaṃhāravāda iti / bhedasaṃhāravādo na syāt syād uṣṭra ityādikaḥ / atha punar asaṃsṛṣṭau dadhyuṣṭrau pratipadya saṃh. ///
body.translated_text:
[Folio 9] /// ...not seeing the form, the connection is: how would one be convinced of objects by cognition? What kind of cognition? He says 'not commingled,' and so forth.
[Folio v1] /// ...that in which the object [is present], it is so called. That cognition which possesses this is called 'not commingled' (<s>asaṃsṛṣṭa</s>) — having a distinct form, grasping objects separately — this is the meaning. Or how would one designate with a conventionally determined sound? The intention is: why would one not be convinced? He says: 'Because of the absence of division among entities' — this is the doctrine of unification (<s>saṃhāravāda</s>). There would be no unification of distinctions — 'it is a camel,' and so forth [would be meaningless]. Now, if, without commingling, curd and camel are apprehended, the unification... ///

body.text: 2 /// .. sarginyā uṣṭrarūpeṇaiva dadhirūpeṇaiva vā saṃsargiṇyā buddher asaṃsṛṣṭākāragrāhiṇyā kvacid uṣṭre dadhini ca yat pratiniyamāt* / tatpratibhāsabhedakṛta eva buddhipratibhāsabhedakṛta eva eva tayor dadhyuṣṭrarūpayoḥ svabhāvabhedo 'pi / kasmāt* / ekāneketyādi pratibhāsabhedasyānekavyavasthitir viṣaya ekavyavasthitiḥ pratibhāsābhedasyeti yojyaṃ / bhinnapratibhāsa .i ///
body.translated_text: [Folio 2] /// ...by a cognition that is commingled — grasping only the camel-form or only the curd-form — by a cognition that grasps an uncommingled form, the determination in some cases to the camel, in some to curd: the difference of <s>svabhāva</s> (intrinsic nature) of those two — curd-form and camel-form — is produced precisely by the difference in cognitive appearance (<s>pratibhāsa</s>), produced precisely by the difference in cognitive appearance. Why? 'One and many,' and so forth: the many-fold establishment of the object is [due to] the difference in appearance; the single establishment is [due to] the non-difference in appearance — this is how it should be construed. Of distinct appearances... ///

body.text: 3 /// .. ti naika uṣṭro dadhi vā tadubhayarūpaḥ dadhyuṣṭrātmakarūpaṃ yasyeti vigrahaḥ / mithyāvāda eva syādvādaḥ / bhedalakṣaṇam iti vyāvṛttilakṣaṇaṃ prakṛtyā sva .. .. .. / ā .. .. .. .. .. .. .. .. .. .. .. .. .. .. .. .. .. .. .. .. .. .. .. .. .. vānāṃ vastūnāṃ svabhāvabhedaḥ / svabhāvenaivānyasmād vyāvṛttiḥ / tatreti nirūpākhyeṣu ///
body.translated_text: [Folio 3] /// ...thus, not one — neither camel nor curd nor one having the form of both, i.e., one whose form is constituted by both curd and camel — this is the analysis. The <s>syādvāda</s> [of the Jains] would be mere false doctrine (<s>mithyāvāda</s>). 'The mark of distinction' means the mark of exclusion (<s>vyāvṛtti</s>), by nature its own... /// ...of entities, the difference of <s>svabhāva</s>. The exclusion from another is by <s>svabhāva</s> alone. 'There' means in those that are without positive characterization (<s>nirūpākhya</s>) ///

body.text: 4 /// .. .. cānyāpohavādinā śakyaṃ vaktum* / naiva nirupākhyeṣu śabdānāṃ pravṛttir iti yatas teṣv apy avaśyaṃ śabdapravṛttyā bhāvyaṃ kasmāt* kathaṃcit* / jñānaśabdaviṣayatvenāvyavasthāpiteṣu nirūpākhyeṣu sarvatrārthe vidhipratiṣedhāyogāt* / yadi kvacid asata ākārasya niṣedhena jñānābhidhāne syātāṃ tadā niṣiddhākāraparihṛte 'rthe .. ///
body.translated_text: [Folio 4] /// ...can be stated by the proponent of <s>anyāpoha</s> (exclusion of the other). Words do not at all apply to those that are without positive characterization (<s>nirūpākhya</s>) — yet in those too, word-application must necessarily occur somehow. Why? Because when things are not established through being the objects of cognition and words as without positive characterization, in every object there would be the impossibility of both positive injunction (<s>vidhi</s>) and prohibition (<s>pratiṣedha</s>). If cognition and designation were possible through the negation of a non-existent form in some cases, then in the object from which the negated form has been excluded... ///

body.text: 5 /// .i .. kau vidhipratiṣedhau / āśrayo yasya vyavahārasya sa tathoktaḥ / tam eva vyavahārābhāvam uṣṭretyādināha / uṣṇasvabhāvo 'gnir ity anvayāśrayo vyavahāraḥ / nānuṣṇa iti vyatirekāśrayaḥ ayam apy atiprasiddho lokavyavahāro na syād ity apiśabdenāha / uṣṇavyavasthā hy anuṣṇavyavacchedena / tasya cānuṣṇasyoṣṇābhā ///
body.translated_text: [Folio 5] /// ...positive injunction and prohibition. 'The basis of which usage' — that is so called. He states that very absence of usage with 'camel,' and so forth. 'Fire has the <s>svabhāva</s> of being hot (<s>uṣṇa</s>)' — this is usage based on positive concomitance (<s>anvaya</s>). 'Not non-hot (<s>anuṣṇa</s>)' — this is usage based on negative concomitance (<s>vyatireka</s>). This too is an extremely well-known common usage — he says this with the word 'also' (<s>api</s>): the establishment of hotness is through the exclusion of non-hotness. And that non-hotness, [being the absence of] hotness... ///

body.text: 6 /// .. .. .. pyeta tad āha svabhāvāntaretyādi / uṣṇābhāva evoṣṇasvabhāvād antaraṃ vilakṣaṇaṃ tadviraharūpeṇeti svabhāvāntaram uktaṃ / ata evāsata ity etad ghaṭate / na tu svabhāvaviśeṣas svabhāvāntaraṃ / kathaṃcid api vikalpabuddheḥ śabdasya ca viṣayatvenā .. vasthāpanāt* ///
body.translated_text: [Folio 6] /// ...one might object; he states this with '<s>svabhāvāntara</s>,' and so forth. The absence of hotness (<s>uṣṇābhāva</s>) alone is what is called '<s>svabhāvāntara</s>' — something different from the <s>svabhāva</s> of hotness, characterized by the absence of that — thus it is called 'another <s>svabhāva</s>.' For this very reason, 'of the non-existent' is fitting. But a particular <s>svabhāva</s> is not another <s>svabhāva</s> [in the same sense]. Because somehow, through being the object of <s>vikalpa</s> (conceptual construction) and of words, [things] are established... ///

body.text: 7 /// .. pratipattir yathāgnisvabhāvasyaivaṃ sarvasya padārthasya tato vyāmūḍham aniścitarūpaṃ jagat syāt* / syād etan na tatra vahnyādau kasyacid asato niṣedho yenābhāve 'py avaśyaṃ śabdapravṛtyā bhāvyam iti / codyate kiṃtv anuṣṇaṃ sparśākhyaṃ sad eva vastv eva agneś cārthāntaraṃ niṣidhyata iti / uṣṇo 'gni nānuṣṇaḥ / agnāv anuṣṇasparśo nāstīty evaṃ niṣedhāt katham ityādi co .. /// sad eveti vacanāt satva .i ///
body.translated_text: [Folio 7] /// ...the cognition that, just as of the <s>svabhāva</s> of fire, so of every object — from that, the world would be confused, of undetermined form. One might say: it is not that in fire and such there is negation of anything non-existent, such that even in the absence [of a real universal], word-application must necessarily occur. It is objected: however, the non-hot (<s>anuṣṇa</s>), called touch, is a real existent entity, and what is negated is something other than fire. 'Hot is fire, not non-hot.' Because the negation is thus: 'in fire, the touch of non-hotness does not exist' — how then, and so forth, the objection... /// 'real existent' — by the statement of reality... ///

body.text: 8 /// .iharati / agnāv anuṣṇaṃ nāstīty anena sarvatroṣṇam asad iti na brūmaḥ / evaṃ hy ucyamāne satvaṃ pratijñāya punaḥ sarvatra satvaniṣedhe sadasatvam ekatra pratijñātaṃ bhavet* / kevalaṃ tatra tv agnaur anuṣṇaṃ nāstīti brūmaḥ / tataś cānyatra sato 'nyatrāsatvam aviruddhaṃ / ayam eva ca nyāya ity āha / deśetyādiḥ iha nā .. ///
body.translated_text: [Folio 8] /// ...he refutes. By saying 'non-hotness does not exist in fire,' we do not say that hotness is non-existent everywhere. For if, having asserted reality and then negating reality everywhere, the reality and non-reality would be asserted of one and the same thing. Rather, we merely say: in fire, non-hotness does not exist. And from that, the non-reality of what is real elsewhere is not contradictory. This very reasoning he states with '<s>deśa</s> (place),' and so forth: here it is not... ///

body.text:
O Pramāṇavārttikaṭīkā
r1 /// .. sya nadharmiṇo niṣedhaḥ kasmāt tanniṣedhe dharmiṇoniṣedhe tadviṣayasya śabdasya nirviṣayatayā pravṛtyabhāvāt* tataś ca dharmiśabdāpravṛtter anirdiṣṭo viṣayo yasya nañas! tasyāprayogāt* / idam iha nāstīty avaśyam idam ādipadair viṣayaḥ pratiṣedhasyopasthāpyo 'nyathā kiṃviṣayo 'yaṃ pratiṣedha ity evaṃ na jñāyeta ///
body.translated_text:
O <s>Pramāṇavārttikaṭīkā</s>
[Folio r1] /// ...the negation of what does not possess the property (<s>dharmin</s>): why? Because when that is negated — when the property-bearer is negated — the word pertaining to that object, being objectless, would have no application. And thus, due to the non-application of the <s>dharmin</s>-word, the negation particle (<s>nañ</s>), whose object is unspecified, would also not be employed. In the statement 'this does not exist here,' the object of negation must necessarily be presented by the words 'this' and so forth; otherwise, 'what is the object of this negation?' — this would not be known ///

body.text: 2 /// trāpīti deśakāladharmaniṣedhena deśādīnām ādiśabdāt kālasya parigrahaḥ / vyaktibhedāt tu bahuvacanaṃ nārthasyeti dharmasya na tv arthaśabdena dharmiṇo nirdeśaḥ / pareṇāpi dharminiṣedhasyoniṣṭatvāt* / na dharmi śaśaviṣāṇādiḥ / pratiṣidhyate nāpi deśādiḥ / kiṃtu śaśaviṣāṇaṃ nāstīti śaśasya viṣāṇena saha .. + + +ḥ sa .. ///
body.translated_text: [Folio 2] /// ...'not here' — by the negation of place, time, and property: the word '<s>ādi</s>' (and so forth) after '<s>deśa</s>' (place) includes time (<s>kāla</s>). The plural is due to the difference of instances, not of the object — thus of the property (<s>dharma</s>); but by the word 'object' (<s>artha</s>), there is not a reference to the property-bearer (<s>dharmin</s>). Because even according to the opponent, the negation of the <s>dharmin</s> is not established. The <s>dharmin</s> — the moon's horn and such — is not negated, nor is place and so forth negated. Rather, 'the horn of the moon does not exist' — the moon together with its horn... ///

body.text: 3 /// .. py aniṣedhāt* / tad evāsatītyādinā sādhayati / asati saṃbandhe śabdāpravṛtti ādiśābdād anirdiṣṭaviśayasya naño! 'prayogāt* / athavā tulyo doṣaḥ kathaṃ niṣedhāt* / asati yo niṣedhas tasya tvayaiva niṣedhād iti vyākhyeyam* / kathaṃ niṣedha ity āhāsatītyādi / asato vāsya saṃbandhasya niṣedhe tadvat saṃbandhavat* dharmiṇo .. ///
body.translated_text: [Folio 3] /// ...also because of non-negation. He establishes this very point with 'of the non-existent,' and so forth. When there is no connection, there is non-application of the word — from the word '<s>ādi</s>,' because of the non-employment of the negation particle whose object is unspecified. Or alternatively, the fault is equal: how can there be negation? Because the negation of what is non-existent is negated by you yourself — thus it should be explained. How is there negation? He says 'of the non-existent,' and so forth. When the non-existent — or this connection — is negated, like that, like one possessing connection, the property-bearer... ///

body.text: 4 /// rhi neha pradeśe ghaṭo nedānīṃ kāla ity evaṃ pratiṣedhoktau satyāṃ nānena deśena kālena vā ghaṭasya saṃbandhāstīti pratītiḥ / tathā naivaṃ nānena prakāreṇa ghaṭo 'stīty uktau naitaddharmā ghaṭa iti pratītiḥ / tathety evaṃ pratītau satyāṃ / tathāpītyādi codakaḥ nedānīm ityādināpi kathaṃ saṃbandho niṣiddho yāvad asya punsaḥ saṃbandho dharmo vā nāst. ///
body.translated_text: [Folio 4] /// ...'indeed, in this place there is no pot, nor at this time' — when the negation is stated thus, the cognition arises: this pot has no connection with this place or time. Likewise, when it is stated 'a pot does not exist in this manner,' the cognition arises: the pot does not possess this property. 'Thus' means when such cognition arises. 'Even so,' and so forth — the objector [says]: even by saying 'not now' and so forth, how is the connection negated, so long as the connection or property of this [individual] does not exist... ///

body.text: 5 /// .. rmo nāstīti matiḥ / dharmaniṣedho 'pi saṃbandhaniṣedha eva dharmadharmiṇoḥ saṃbandhaniṣedhāt* / saṃyogasamavāyalakṣaṇabhedāt tu saṃbandho dharmo veti bhedenoktam* na cāsyāḥ saṃbandho nāstīti mateḥ kathaṃcid bhāve sattāyāṃ saṃbhavaḥ / kasmāt* / abhāveṣv ityādi / tathāśabdo yathārtham ākṣipati yattador nityābhisaṃbandhāt* satsu deśādiṣu yathā nāstīti buddher abhāvaḥ / satsvabhāvabuddher virodhāt* / ta .. ///
body.translated_text: [Folio 5] /// ...the cognition 'the property does not exist.' The negation of a property is also a negation of relation, because of the negation of the relation between property (<s>dharma</s>) and property-bearer (<s>dharmin</s>). But because of the distinction of the defining characteristic of conjunction (<s>saṃyoga</s>) and inherence (<s>samavāya</s>), it is stated with a distinction that 'relation is a property.' And for this cognition 'there is no relation,' there is no possibility (of being real) even if it exists in some way. Why? With 'In absences' and so forth. The word 'thus' draws in the intended meaning — because of the invariable connection of 'that' and 'there,' in existent locations and so forth, just as the cognition 'it does not exist' is absent — because of the contradiction with the cognition of an existent nature. That... ///

body.text: 6 /// .. śān nedam ihety ādyā pratītiḥ / sā tadabhāve saṃbandhapratītyabhāve na syāt* pratītau vā tadabhāvasya saṃbandhābhāvasya yādṛśī saṃbandhābhāvapratītiḥ yathā pratīti sā vidyate yasya punsas tasya yathāpratītimataḥ / tatprabhāvāḥ saṃbandhābhāvapratibandhāḥ saṃbandhābhāvaviṣayā / kena vāryante / vikalpaviṣaya eva / saṃbandhābhāvo na śabdā .. ///
body.translated_text: [Folio 6] /// ...(in locations and so forth) the primary cognition is 'this is not here.' That, in the absence of the cognition of relation, would not exist. Or, in the cognition, whatever cognition of the absence of relation there is — whoever possesses such a cognition of the absence of relation, for that person, according to his cognition. The effects of that — the obstacles pertaining to the absence of relation, those having the absence of relation as their object — by what are they prevented? They are the object of <s>vikalpa</s> (conceptual construction) only. The absence of relation is not (the object of) words... ///

body.text: 7 /// na śabdānāṃ viṣayaḥ vikalaviṣayas tv avaśyam* śabdaviṣaya ity arthaḥ / te cet pravṛttā iti vitarkāḥ / nanu purato 'vasthite nīlādau nīlam ityādi vikalpaḥ / svalakṣaṇaviṣayo na ca svalakṣaṇam* / śābdavācyam ity ata āha / na hītyādi / avācyam artham iti svalakṣaṇaṃ vitarkādhikārād vikalpabuddhayo gṛhyante / samīhanta ity ālambante / sāmānyākārava ///
body.translated_text: [Folio 7] /// ...not the object of words; but that which is the object of conceptual construction must necessarily be the object of words — such is the meaning. 'If they have engaged' — these are the deliberations (<s>vitarka</s>). Now, when blue and so forth are present before one, the conceptual construction 'blue' and so forth — is it the object of a <s>svalakṣaṇa</s> (particular)? But a <s>svalakṣaṇa</s> is not expressible by words — therefore he says with 'For not' and so forth. The <s>svalakṣaṇa</s> is the inexpressible object — conceptual cognitions (<s>vikalpabuddhis</s>) are grasped in the domain of deliberation (<s>vitarka</s>). 'They intend' means they apprehend. Having the aspect of the universal (<s>sāmānya</s>)... ///

body.text:
8 /// . tu yaugapadyād abhimāna eṣa mandamatīnāṃ vikalpaḥ / svalakṣaṇākāra iti / vicāritaś caitat pramāṇaviniścaye śāstrakāreṇeti neha pratanyate /
v1 /// ndho vācyaḥ kathaṃ tarhy ācāryadignāgena tasyāvācyatvam uktam ity ata āha / saṃbandhasyetyādi / svena rūpeṇeti saṃbandharūpeṇeti saṃbandhanaṃ saṃbandha iti / parasparāpekṣālakṣaṇam* / bhāvamātram asatvabhūtaṃ tasya dharmaḥ / tena ca rūpeṇa tasyābhidhāykaḥ śabdo nāsti / saṃbandhaśabdo 'bhidhāyaka eṣṭavyaḥ / sa ca prayuktaḥ / kayor ity ākṣ ///
body.translated_text:
[Folio 8] /// ...but because of simultaneity, this conceit is the <s>vikalpa</s> (conceptual construction) of those of dull intellect — 'having the aspect of the <s>svalakṣaṇa</s>.' And this has been examined in the <s>Pramāṇaviniścaya</s> by the author of the treatise, so it is not elaborated here.
[Folio v1] /// ...relation is expressible — but then how has the teacher <s>Dignāga</s> stated its inexpressibility? To this he says with 'Of relation' and so forth. 'By its own form' means: in the form of relation; 'relating' (<s>saṃbandhana</s>) is relation (<s>saṃbandha</s>). Its defining characteristic is mutual dependence (<s>parasparāpekṣā</s>). Mere being (<s>bhāvamātra</s>), non-existent as a real entity — that is its property. And in that form, no word designates it. The word 'relation' should be accepted as the designator. And it is used (in that way). 'Of whom two?' — he objects... ///

body.text: 2 /// .. vyatirekasya hetuḥ saṃbandhas tadā saṃbandhirūpeṇa pratīyate / tad āhābhidhāne saṃbandhitvenetyādi / rājapuruṣayoḥ saṃbandha ity abhidhāne rājapuruṣābhyāṃ parasparānapekṣābhyāṃ niṣkṛṣṭarūpasyeva saṃbandhasya saṃbandhitvena buddhāv upasthānāt* / yathābhiprāyam apratītiḥ rājñaḥ puruṣa iti parasparāpekṣālakṣaṇaḥ saṃbandho yathā jñātum i .. ///
body.translated_text: [Folio 2] /// ...the cause of differentiation is relation; then it is cognized in the form of the relata. He states this with 'In the expression, as having relata' and so forth. In the expression 'the relation of king and servant,' because the relation — having the form as if abstracted from the king and servant who are mutually independent — presents itself to cognition as 'having relata.' The non-cognition according to intention (is this): 'The servant of the king' — how the relation, defined by mutual dependence, is to be known... ///

body.text: 3 /// t* / yathoktavidhinā saṃbandhirūpa eveti / na svarūpeṇābhidhīyate / tasmān nābhāvat saṃbandhe 'pi prasaṃga iti / abhāvo yathā buddhyā viṣayīkriyata iti / vācyaḥ prasakto naivaṃ saṃbandhe 'pi vācyatvam ity arthaḥ / abhāvo hi svena rūpeṇa buddhyā viṣayīkriyate śabdenāpi tathaivābhidhīyate / saṃbandha ///
body.translated_text: [Folio 3] /// ...in the form of the relata alone, according to the stated method — it is not expressed in its own form. Therefore, there is no overextension (<s>prasaṅga</s>) to absence (<s>abhāva</s>) either with regard to relation. Absence — how is it made an object by cognition? — is to be stated. The overextension is: just as in the case of relation, expressibility should not apply — such is the meaning. For absence (<s>abhāva</s>) is made an object by cognition in its own form, and is likewise expressed by words in its own form. Relation... ///

body.text: 4 /// py abhidhīyate / saṃbandhirūpāpannasyaiva viṣayīkaraṇāhābhinnāca / tathā cāha asatvabhūtaḥ saṃbandho rūpaṃ tasya na gṛhyate nābhidhānaṃ svarūpeṇa saṃbandhasyāsti kiñcinneti / tasmāt sthitam etad vikalpaviṣayo 'vaśyaṃ vācya iti / tataś ca yadi nāsti saṃbandha iti matis tadā tatprabhavo 'pi śabdaḥ pravartata eva tathā cābhāvaviṣayaḥ .. ///
body.translated_text: [Folio 4] /// ...is also expressed; but it is only when it has assumed the form of the relata that it is made an object — (he says) 'non-different, and...' And so he states: 'The relation, being non-existent as a real entity (<s>asatvabhūta</s>), its form is not grasped; there is no expression of relation in its own form whatsoever.' Therefore, this is established: what is an object of <s>vikalpa</s> (conceptual construction) is necessarily expressible. And therefore, if the cognition 'relation does not exist' obtains, then the word arising from it also operates, and thus the word having absence as its object... ///

body.text: 5 /// .īkaraṇaṃ neṣyate / tadā neha ghaṭa ity atra kasya niṣedho na tāvad deśādes tasya satvāt* / na saṃbandhasya tadabhāvasyāgrahaṇād iti yatkiñcid etat* / api cābhāvam abhidheyaṃ yo brūte taṃ bruvāṇaṃ praty ayam abhāvanabhidhānavādī abhāvo na vācya iti / pratividadhat* / abruvāṇaḥ kathaṃ pratividadhyāt* / na hy abhāvaśabdam anuccārayatā tasyāvācya .. ///
body.translated_text: [Folio 5] /// ...making (it) an object is not accepted; then, in 'the pot is not here,' whose negation is it? Not of location and so forth, since those exist. Nor of relation, since the non-apprehension of its absence (is what is at issue) — this is a trivial (objection). Moreover, whoever says that absence is expressible — toward that person making such a statement, this proponent of the non-expressibility of absence (argues): 'Absence is not expressible.' In making a counter-argument — how could one who does not (even) utter the word 'absence' make a counter-argument? For without uttering the word 'absence,' its inexpressibility... ///

body.text: 6 /// .. .. /// .. .. .. .. .. .. .. + + + .. .. + + .. nenaivābhāvaśabdena tasyoktaḥ .. .. .. .. syāt* / kathaṃcana syād abhāvasyaivānabhyupagamāt* / abhāvo naivāsti tenāsatvād avacanam abhāvasyeti ced āha / athābhāvam evetyādi / tenety abhāvasyāsaṃbandhena / idānīm iti abhāvasyāsatve / tad evābhāvo nāstīti vacanaṃ kathaṃ abhāvo nāstīty asyaivābhāvaśabdasya prayogo na syāt* / kathaṃcana syāt / ka .. ///
body.translated_text: [Folio 6] /// ... /// ...by this very word 'absence,' its (expressibility) has been stated... would exist. In some way, it would exist, precisely because of the non-acceptance of the very existence of absence. 'Absence does not exist at all' — therefore, because of non-existence, the non-utterance of 'absence' — if one argues thus, he says with 'But absence itself' and so forth. 'By that' means: by the non-connection of absence. 'Now' means: when absence is non-existent. That very statement 'absence does not exist' — how could the very use of the word 'absence' in 'absence does not exist' not exist? In some way it would exist... ///

body.text: 7 /// .. .. .. raparikalpitasyābhāvasya pratiṣedha iti ced iṣṭas tāvad abhāvaviṣayaḥ / śabdaḥ tasmāt kathaṃcid abhāvavyavahāraṃ pravartayatā avaśyam abhāvaviṣayā jñānaśabdā eṣṭavyā / yat punar etad uktaṃ arthaniṣedhe sati / anarthakaśabdāprayogāt kāraṇān nirviṣayasya naño 'prayoga ity atrottaraṃ vakṣyate / anādivāsanodbhūtavika ///
body.translated_text: [Folio 7] /// ...the negation of a mutually constructed absence — if one argues thus, the word having absence as its object is accepted. Therefore, whoever engages in the convention of absence in any way must necessarily accept cognitions and words having absence as their object. Now, as to what was said — 'when the object is negated, because there is no usage of a meaningless word, and because a negation-particle without an object has no usage' — the answer to that will be given here: from <s>vāsanā</s> (latent impression) without beginning, conceptual construction arising... ///

body.text:
P Pramāṇavārttikaṭīkā
r1 /// t* / svabhāvābhāvād abhāvasya rūpābhidhāyinaḥ / svabhāvābbhidhāyinaḥ śabdā nāśaṅkyā eva yatas te śabdā abhāvaviṣayāḥ vyavacchedasyānyāpohasya vācakāḥ siddhā eva / vastuni vṛttir vyāpāro yeṣāṃ śabdānāṃ teṣāṃ kiṃ rūpam abhidheyaṃ vidhirūpeṇa vastv abhidheyam āhosvid bh. ///
body.translated_text:
P. <s>Pramāṇavārttikaṭīkā</s>
[Folio r1] /// ...because of the absence of the intrinsic nature of absence, words that designate the form of absence — words that designate the intrinsic nature — are not to be suspected at all, since those words having absence as their object are already established as expressing <s>vyavaccheda</s> (exclusion), that is, <s>anyāpoha</s> (exclusion of the other). The operation — the function — pertaining to real things, of those words — what form is expressed: is a real thing expressed in the form of affirmation (<s>vidhi</s>), or is it... ///

body.text: 2 /// .. .. .. ttavyasya viṣayīkartavyasya rūpasya vastusvabhāvasya tadbhāve tasya rūpasya sattāyamm abhāvāyogāt* / tasya rūpasya bhāvas tadbhāvaḥ / sa eva lakṣaṇaṃ yasya bhāvasya sa tathoktaḥ ayam eva sa mukhyo viveko 'nyāpoho yaḥ sarvabhāvavirahaḥ / tasya vivekasya tathābhāvakhyāpina iti vivekarūpābhi .. ///
body.translated_text: [Folio 2] /// ...of the form that is the object to be cognized — of the nature of a real thing — when that form exists, absence is impossible. The existence of that form is 'its being' (<s>tadbhāva</s>). That which has this very (existence) as its defining characteristic — of that entity so characterized: this alone is the primary discrimination — <s>anyāpoha</s> (exclusion of the other) — which is the absence of all (other) entities. The words that proclaim the form of that discrimination... ///

body.text: 3 /// ..ṃbandhaḥ / te śabdā vikalpāś ca ekaṃ vyāvṛttisamāśrayabhūtaṃ vastupratisaraṇam adhiṣṭhānaṃ yeṣāṃ śabdānāṃ vikalpānāñ ca te tathoktāḥ / tathā hy akṛtakavyavacchedena yad eva vastu kṛtakaśabdasya vikalpasya vādhiṣṭhānaṃ / tad evānityānātmādiśābdānāṃ vikalpānāñ ca / te tathābhūtā api bhinnaviṣayā eveti saṃbandhaḥ / kasmād yathāsvam ityādi / yā vyāvṛttir yato .. .. ///
body.translated_text: [Folio 3] /// ...this is the connection. Those words and conceptual constructions (<s>vikalpas</s>) — the one real thing that is the basis of exclusion (<s>vyāvṛttisamāśraya</s>), the substrate (<s>adhiṣṭhāna</s>) of those words and conceptual constructions — they are so designated. For indeed, by the exclusion of the non-produced, whatever real thing is the substrate of the word and conceptual construction 'produced' — that very same (thing) is (the substrate) of the words and conceptual constructions 'impermanent,' 'non-self,' and so forth. Those, even though of such a nature, are objects of distinct (exclusions) — such is the connection. Why? With 'according to each' and so forth. Whatever exclusion, from whatever... ///

body.text: 4 /// tyatvalakṣaṇasya vyavacchedasya nitya ityādi / teṣāṃ yathāsvaṃ avadhīnāṃ bhedās tair bhedair upakalpitā nacitā anityatvādīnāṃ vivekānāṃ bhedāḥ parasparaṃ viśeṣās tair bhedaiḥ bhinneṣv iva vivekeṣu vikalpabuddhau pratibhātsu / pratibhāsamāneṣu teṣāṃ śabdānāṃ vikalpānāṃ copalayanāt* / yathākramaṃ vācakatvena grāhakatvena copaśleṣāt* / .. ///
body.translated_text: [Folio 4] /// ...of the exclusion characterized by impermanence and so forth, 'permanent' and so forth. Of those — according to their respective limits — the differences, established by those differences, the distinctions among the discriminations of impermanence and so forth — their mutual distinctions — by those differences, when the discriminations appear as if distinct in conceptual cognition — when they appear, of those words and conceptual constructions, the apprehension. In due order, through their being expressors and apprehenders respectively, the connection... ///

body.text: 5 /// syaiva sādhyasādhanabhāve 'pi na sādhyasādhanayoḥ saṃsarga ekatvaṃ tataś ca yad uktaṃ svabhāve sādhye pratijñārthaikadeśo hetuḥ syād iti sa doṣo nāstīty āha / taṃ netyādi / tad iti tasmāt* / sa cāyaṃ svabhāva iti saṃbandhaḥ / hetutvenāpadiśyamāna ucyamāna upādhibhedāpekṣo viśeṣaṇabhedāpekṣa ucyate / kevalo vety upādhyana .. ///
body.translated_text: [Folio 5] /// ...even when there is the relation of <s>sādhya</s> (probandum) and <s>sādhana</s> (probans) of the same intrinsic nature, there is no conflation — no identity — of <s>sādhya</s> and <s>sādhana</s>. Therefore, what was said — 'when the intrinsic nature is the <s>sādhya</s>, the <s>hetu</s> (reason) would be a part of the thesis (<s>pratijñārthaikadeśa</s>)' — that fault does not exist; he says with 'That, no' and so forth. 'That' means: therefore. 'And this intrinsic nature' — such is the connection. That which is being indicated as the <s>hetu</s> (reason), when it is stated, is said with reference to the difference of qualifiers (<s>upādhi</s>), with reference to the difference of qualifications. 'Merely (<s>kevala</s>), or' — without the qualifier... ///

body.text: 6 /// anityatve sādhye kṛtakatvam upādhibhedāpekṣam* tadanapekṣaṃ tu satvaṃ / apekṣitetyādinopādhibhedāpekṣitvaṃ kṛtakatvasyāha / vastubhūtāyāḥ asiddheḥ parasya hetvabhimatasya jananaśaktir eva paravyāpāraḥ / anvayavyatirekānuvidhānam eva cāpekṣā / svabhāvaniṣpattau svabhāvaniṣpattinimittam apekṣitaḥ / paravyāpāro yena bhāve .. .. ///
body.translated_text: [Folio 6] /// ...when impermanence is the <s>sādhya</s> (probandum), 'being produced' (<s>kṛtakatva</s>) depends on the difference of qualifiers; but 'existence' (<s>satva</s>) does not depend on that. With 'Depending on' and so forth, he states the dependence of 'being produced' on the difference of qualifiers. Of the ultimately established (<s>vastubhūtā</s>) <s>asiddhi</s> (unestablishment) — the capacity to produce an effect (<s>jananaśakti</s>) of the other that is claimed as a <s>hetu</s> (reason) — that alone is the operation of the other (<s>paravyāpāra</s>). And the conformity with positive and negative concomitance (<s>anvayavyatirekānuvidhāna</s>) is itself the dependence. When the intrinsic nature is accomplished, that which is the cause of the accomplishment of the intrinsic nature is depended upon — the operation of the other, by which the entity... ///

body.text: 7 /// ḥ / svabhāvābhidhāyiny api satī paropādhir ity anyaviśeṣaṇam enaṃ svabhāvam āksipati / eteneti kṛtakatvasyopādhibhedāpekṣapratipādanena / pratyayānāṃ kārāṇāṃ bhedaḥ pratyayabhedas tena bhettuṃ śīlaṃ yasya sa tathā / tadbhāvaḥ pratyayabhedabheditvaṃ / sthānaprayatnādikāraṇabhedena hi bhidyate śabdaḥ / ādiśabdāt prayatnānantarīyakatvādayo vyākhyātāḥ / ete 'pi hetu .. ///
body.translated_text: [7] /// ... Even though it designates the <s>svabhāva</s> (intrinsic nature), the qualifier 'other' indicates that it is an <s>upādhi</s> (adventitious condition) belonging to another, and thus it draws in this intrinsic nature. 'By this' means through the demonstration that <s>kṛtakatva</s> (being produced) depends on differentiation of <s>upādhis</s>. The differentiation of <s>pratyayas</s> (conditions), i.e., causes, is <s>pratyayabheda</s> (differentiation of conditions); that which has the character of being differentiated by it is so called. Its state is the property of being differentiated by the differentiation of conditions. For sound is differentiated by the differentiation of causes such as place of articulation, effort, and so forth. By the word 'etc.,' immediate succession of effort and the like are explained. These too are reasons... ///

body.text:
8 /// iti / evam ityādinopasaṃhāraḥ / kvacid iti prayoge / upādhibheda .. .. .. pekṣaṃ / ata eva sāmānyena hetuphalabhāvena padadvayaṃ anitya eva sādhye yathā satvaṃ / svabhāvabhūtaś cāsau dharmaviśeṣaś ceti vigrahaḥ / tasya parigraheṇa kvacit svabhāvo hetur ucyate iti prakṛtaṃ / yathā tatraiveti anityatve sādhye
9 /// ḥ / svabhāvabhūto 'pi dharmaviśeṣatvena pratīyate / prādurbhāvasya dharmaviśeṣatvena pratīteḥ / na tu sattāvac chuddhasya svabhāvamātrasya pratītiḥ /
v1 /// .. bhāvabhūto 'pi dharmaviśeṣatvena pratīyate / prādurbhāvasya dharmaviseṣatvena pratīteḥ / na tu sattāvac chuddasya svabhāvamātrasya pratītiḥ / ayam apy upādhyapekṣa eva svabhāvo draṣṭavyaḥ / kṛtakatvādau parabhūta upādhir iha tv ātmabhū eva dharmaviśeṣa ity etāvān bhedaḥ / anayā diśeti / upādhyapekṣahetupravibhāgadisā / dharmī sāmānyena siddho viśeṣeṇa /
2 /// sādhyeti nyāyaḥ tatra yadi sattākhyaḥ svabhāvaḥ sattāsvabhāvaḥ / satvam i .i + .. .. kṛtakatvādiko 'pi svabhāvas tannivṛtyarthaṃ / sattāgrahaṇaṃ vyatiriktāpi sattā kaiścid iṣṭeti svabhāvagrahaṇaṃ / ātmabhūtā sattety arthaḥ / sattāsvabhāvaś cet* hetuḥ na sattā sādhyate / kathaṃ sādhyāpi syāt* / atha mataṃ sattāsāmānye sādhye siddhasādhyatā syād ataḥ sattāviśeṣaḥ sādhyas tasmiṃś ca sādhye ///
body.translated_text:
[8] /// ... thus. The conclusion is by means of 'evam' etc. 'Kvacit' refers to a particular usage. The differentiation of <s>upādhis</s> ... dependence. Therefore, by the general cause-and-effect relationship, the two terms [apply]: in the <s>sādhya</s> (probandum) of impermanence alone, as for example <s>satva</s> (existence). The analysis is: it is both intrinsic to the nature and a specific property (<s>dharmaviśeṣa</s>). By the inclusion of that, sometimes <s>svabhāva</s> (intrinsic nature) is called the <s>hetu</s> (reason)—this is the topic at hand. 'As in that very case' means when impermanence is the <s>sādhya</s>.
[9] /// ... Even though intrinsic to the nature, it is cognized as a specific property (<s>dharmaviśeṣa</s>), because <s>prādurbhāva</s> (manifestation) is cognized as a specific property. But there is no cognition of the pure intrinsic nature alone, as with <s>sattā</s> (existence).
[v1] /// ... Even though intrinsic to the nature, it is cognized as a specific property, because manifestation is cognized as a specific property. But there is no cognition of the pure intrinsic nature alone, as with <s>sattā</s>. This <s>svabhāva</s> too should be understood as dependent on an <s>upādhi</s>. In the case of <s>kṛtakatva</s> (being produced) etc., the <s>upādhi</s> is extrinsic, but here the specific property is intrinsic itself—this is the only difference. 'In this direction' means in the direction of the classification of reasons dependent on <s>upādhis</s>. The <s>dharmin</s> (property-possessor) is established generally, but by a specific property
[2] /// ... the <s>sādhya</s> is [established]—this is the principle. In that case, if the <s>svabhāva</s> called <s>sattā</s> (existence) is the <s>sattāsvabhāva</s> (existence-nature), existence is ... <s>kṛtakatva</s> etc. are also <s>svabhāvas</s>; to prevent that [misunderstanding], the term '<s>sattā</s>' is used. Since some accept <s>sattā</s> as distinct [from things], the term '<s>svabhāva</s>' is used. The meaning is: <s>sattā</s> is intrinsic. If the <s>sattāsvabhāva</s> is the <s>hetu</s> (reason), then <s>sattā</s> is not being proved. How then could it also be the <s>sādhya</s>? If one thinks that when <s>sattā</s> in general is the <s>sādhya</s>, there would be the fault of proving what is already established, and therefore a particular of <s>sattā</s> is the <s>sādhya</s>—then in that <s>sādhya</s> ///

body.text: 3 /// .. .. dṛṣṭāntaḥ / syād ato na sattā sādhyate / tadā hetāv api satve viśeṣasyānanvayāt sādhanaśūnyo dṛṣṭāntaḥ syāt* tad āhānanvayo hītyādi / bhedānāṃ viśeṣāṇāṃ vyāhato duṣṭaḥ / hetusādhayor iti saptamīdvivacanaṃ / hetau sādhye cety arthaḥ / anyatra cānātmādau / tad iti satvaṃ / kilaśabdo 'nabhimatadyotakaḥ evaṃ prasādhyamānam iti asti pradhānam ityādinā pradhānādi ///
body.translated_text: [3] /// ... the example [would be deficient]. Therefore, <s>sattā</s> (existence) is not what is being proved. In that case, since there is no concomitance of the particular in the <s>hetu</s> (reason) as well—namely in <s>satva</s> (existence)—the example would lack the <s>sādhana</s> (probans). He states this with 'for there is no concomitance' and so forth. The specific differences are contradicted, i.e., faulty. 'In the <s>hetu</s> and the <s>sādhya</s>'—this is a locative dual; the meaning is: in the reason and in the probandum. 'Elsewhere' means in [the proof of] non-self and so forth. 'That' refers to <s>satva</s> (existence). The particle 'kila' indicates what is not accepted [by the author]. 'What is thus being established'—by [the argument] 'there exists a <s>pradhāna</s> (primal matter)' and so forth, the <s>pradhāna</s> etc. ///

body.text: 4 /// sādhayituṃ śakyate / kasmāt tasya viśeṣasyānanvayāt* / yathāhety ācāryadiṅnāgaḥ / asti pradhānaṃ ity annena pradhāna{m ity anena pradhā} svalakṣaṇam eva sādhyata iti yat sāṃkhyenoktaṃ tat pramāṇasyānumānasya viṣayājñānāt* / sāmānyaviṣayaṃ hy anumānaṃ na svalakṣaṇa[yogena} viṣayaṃ / vyāhanyate duṣyati kiṃ tarhi hetāv api / tulyadoṣatvāt* / tad evāha na hetur ityādi / .. .. ///
body.translated_text: [4] /// ... can be proved. Why? Because of the non-concomitance of that particular. 'As he says'—this refers to master <s>Dignāga</s>. 'There exists a <s>pradhāna</s>'—by this [statement], what the <s>Sāṃkhya</s> claimed, namely that only the <s>svalakṣaṇa</s> (particular) of <s>pradhāna</s> is being proved—that is [refuted] because of ignorance regarding the object of the <s>pramāṇa</s> (means of valid cognition), namely inference. For inference has <s>sāmānya</s> (universals) as its object, not <s>svalakṣaṇas</s> (particulars) as its object. It is contradicted, i.e., faulty. What then? In the <s>hetu</s> as well, because of the same fault. He states precisely this with 'it is not a <s>hetu</s>' and so forth ... ///

body.text: 5 /// .. .ity āha tata ityādi / tato 'sādhāraṇād dhetoḥ / bhāvaḥ sattā sā upādānaṃ viśeṣaṇaṃ yasya dharmiṇaḥ sa tathā / mātraśabdo 'vadhāraṇe / sattāviśeṣaṇamātra ityaḥ / evaṃbhūte sādhye sāmānyadharmiṇi sāṃkhyasya na kaścid arthaḥ siddhaḥ syāt* / traiguṇyādilakṣaṇasyāsiddheḥ tad evaṃ sva .. kṣyāsiddhyā sādhanaṃ vaiphalyam uktaṃ / parasyāpī .. ///
body.translated_text: [5] /// ... He says 'tataḥ' and so forth. 'From that uncommon <s>hetu</s> (reason).' <s>Bhāva</s> means <s>sattā</s> (existence); that which has it as a qualifier of the <s>dharmin</s> (property-possessor) is so called. The word 'mātra' is used in the sense of restriction. The meaning of '<s>sattāviśeṣaṇamātra</s>' is: [the <s>dharmin</s>] qualified merely by existence. When the <s>sādhya</s> (probandum) is of this kind—i.e., the <s>dharmin</s> is a universal [subject]—nothing would be established for the <s>Sāṃkhya</s>, because the characteristic of having three <s>guṇas</s> (qualities) etc. is not established. Thus, the futility of the proof due to the non-establishment of the intrinsic nature ... has been stated. For the opponent too ... ///

body.text: 6 /// .. m iti sāmānyamātraṃ / anena siddhasādhyatoktā / atha vā na kaścid arthaḥ siddhaḥ syāt* / aniṣiddhaṃ ca tādṛśaṃ hyarthe caśabdaḥ yasmāt tādṛśam aniṣiddham ataḥ siddhasādhyatādoṣān na kaścid arthaḥ siddhaḥ / syād iti / na sarvathetyādinā vyācaṣṭe / sattāsādhana iti sāttāsiddhau / bhāvamātraviśeṣaṇa iti sattāmātraviśeṣaṇaḥ / anirdiṣṭaḥ viśeṣo yasy. ///
body.translated_text: [6] /// ... is merely a universal. By this, the fault of proving what is already established (<s>siddhasādhyatā</s>) is stated. Alternatively, nothing would be established. And such [a result] is not refuted, and the particle 'ca' [indicates] because such [a probandum] is not refuted; therefore, due to the fault of proving what is already established, nothing would be established—this is the meaning. He explains with 'not in every way' and so forth. 'In the proof of <s>sattā</s>' means in the establishment of existence. '<s>Bhāvamātraviśeṣaṇa</s>' means one whose qualifier is mere existence. '[One] whose specific property is not specified' ... ///

body.text: 7 /// .. / kiṃ tu sa vādī tathā sāmānyena nāsti kaścid iti / kañcanāsya dharmiṇo bhedaṃ viśeṣam aparāmṛṣyānupādāya aneneti vādinā upāttabheda ity apāttaviśeṣaḥ triguṇātmako nitya ityādinā upāttabhede sādhye 'smin pradhānādike dharmiṇi / bhaved dhetur ananvayaḥ / nāsya sādhyaviśeṣeṇa dṣṛṭānte 'nvayo 'stīty ananvayaḥ / sādhyaśūnyo dṛṣṭānta iti ///
body.translated_text: [7] /// ... But that disputant, in that general way, [maintains] 'there is nothing whatsoever.' Without considering or taking up any particular difference of this <s>dharmin</s> (property-possessor)—'by this' means by the disputant—when the difference has been taken up, i.e., when the specific property has been taken up [as the <s>sādhya</s>], such as 'having three <s>guṇas</s> as its nature, eternal' etc., then regarding this <s>dharmin</s> such as <s>pradhāna</s> etc. with a <s>sādhya</s> whose difference has been taken up, the <s>hetu</s> would have non-concomitance—that is, 'there is no concomitance of this [<s>hetu</s>] with the specific <s>sādhya</s> in the example,' hence non-concomitance; the example would be devoid of the <s>sādhya</s> ///

body.text:
8 /// .. .. .. ka iti sukhaduḥkhamohātmakaḥ / tathābhūto 'py eko 'navayavaḥ / pareṇeṣyate anyo veti kartṛtvādiyuktaḥ yathākathaṃcid apīti yathoktair dharmaiḥ samastair vyastair vā viśeṣitaḥ tatsvabhāva iti yathoktaviśeṣaṇaviśiṣṭasvabhāvaḥ / sa ca dharmī tathe
9 /// .. .. ti sattāmātre vivādābhāvāt* /
body.translated_text:
[8] /// ... having the nature of pleasure, pain, and delusion. Even though of such a nature, [<s>pradhāna</s> is maintained to be] one and without parts. Whether it is accepted by the opponent as such, or as another [entity] endowed with agency etc.—'in whatever way' means qualified by the stated properties, all together or separately—'<s>tatsvabhāva</s>' means having the nature characterized by the stated qualifications. And that <s>dharmin</s>, being of such [nature]
[9] /// ... because there is no dispute regarding mere <s>sattā</s> (existence).

body.text:
Q Pramāṇavārttikaṭīkā
r1 /// vikalpena sattāyām uktaḥ / tathā hi ādhāraviseṣeṇa kenacid aviśeṣitam agnyādisattāmātram* sādhyam ādhāraviśiṣṭaṃ vā / ādye pakṣe siddhasādhyatā / yad āha tatrāpītyādi / yatrāpīty agnyādike sādhye / dvitīye pakṣe sādhyaśūnyo dṛṣṭāntaḥ syād āha viśiṣṭetyādi / viśiṣṭa ādhāro yatrāgnyādikaṃ sā .. ///
body.translated_text:
[K] <s>Pramāṇavārttikaṭīkā</s>
[r1] /// ... by <s>vikalpa</s> (conceptual construction), it is stated regarding <s>sattā</s> (existence). For consider: is what is being proved mere <s>sattā</s> of fire etc. without qualification by any particular substrate, or is it <s>sattā</s> qualified by a [particular] substrate? In the first alternative, there is the fault of proving what is already established (<s>siddhasādhyatā</s>). He states this with 'even there' etc. 'Where' means when fire etc. are the <s>sādhya</s>. In the second alternative, the example would be devoid of the <s>sādhya</s>. He states this with 'when qualified' etc. That substrate where fire etc. [are present] ... ///

body.text: 2 /// .. bhimatasya sapakṣe 'nanvayād asiddhiḥ na hy ādhārāntarasaṃbandho 'gnir ādhārāntare vartate / netyādy ācāryaḥ na vai sa ādhāraḥ sādhyadharmitvenābhimatas tam agnyādikaṃ viśeṣīkaroti yatra dhūmas tatrāgnisāmānyam asti cātra dhūmas tasmāyatrāpy agnysāmānyam ity evaṃ sāmānyasyaiva pratīteḥ yady ādhāreṇa na viśeṣīkriyate / kathaṃ tarhi pakṣasya dharma ity evaṃ viśe .. ///
body.translated_text: [2] /// ... because of non-concomitance in the <s>sapakṣa</s> (similar instance) of what is intended, there is non-establishment. For fire that is connected with one substrate does not exist in another substrate. 'Not' etc.—the master [<s>Dharmakīrti</s>]: that substrate is not intended as the <s>dharmin</s> possessing the <s>sādhya</s>; it does not particularize fire and the like. Where there is smoke, there is fire-in-general, and here too there is smoke, therefore there too is fire-in-general—thus, because only the universal is cognized. If it is not particularized by the substrate, then how is it a property of the <s>pakṣa</s> (thesis)? Thus [one might object regarding] the specification ... ///

body.text: 3 /// .. .. .. stasya vyavacchedena viśeṣaṇāt* pakṣasya dharma eveti na tu pakṣasyaiva dharmety uktaṃ prāk* pakṣadharmas tadaṅśena vyāpta ity asya ślokasya vivaraṇe vakṣyate ca caturthe paricchede / tasmād ity upasaṃhāraḥ / tatreti pradeśādau / tadayogavyavaccheneti tasmin pradeśādau dharmiṇi sādhyadharmasyāyogavyavacchedena / tataś ca sāmānyasya sādhanān nā ///
body.translated_text: [3] /// ... by the exclusion of what is established, i.e., by qualification, it is indeed a property of the <s>pakṣa</s> (thesis)—but it is not stated as a property of the <s>pakṣa</s> alone. This was stated earlier. 'The property of the thesis is pervaded by its aspect'—this will be explained in the commentary on this verse in the fourth chapter. 'Therefore' is a conclusion. 'There' means in a particular location etc. 'By the exclusion of its non-connection' means by the exclusion of the non-connection of the <s>sādhya</s> property with that <s>dharmin</s>, i.e., in that particular location etc. And therefore, since it is a universal that is being proved, there is no ... ///

body.text: 4 /// .. vaḥ / pradhānādike 'pi dharmiṇi ayogavyavacchedena sattāmātraṃ sādhyam iti ced āha na tathehāpīti / kvacid iti pradhānādike dharmiṇi kasmāt pradhānādiśabdavācyasyaivārthasya traiguṇyādilakṣaṇasyābhāvāt* / nirviśeṣaṇaiva sā sattā / viśeṣaṇabhūtasyādhārasyābhāvāt* / katham ityādi paraḥ / satvajñeyatvādayo bahavo dha .. ///
body.translated_text: [4] /// ... [fault]. If [one objects that] even regarding a <s>dharmin</s> such as <s>pradhāna</s> etc., mere <s>sattā</s> (existence) is the <s>sādhya</s> through the exclusion of non-connection—he says 'not so, here too' etc. 'Somewhere' means regarding a <s>dharmin</s> such as <s>pradhāna</s> etc. Why? Because the very object denoted by the words '<s>pradhāna</s>' etc., characterized by having three <s>guṇas</s> etc., does not exist. That <s>sattā</s> is without any qualifier, because the substrate that would serve as the qualifier does not exist. 'How?' etc.—the opponent [asks]. Many properties such as <s>satva</s> (existence), <s>jñeyatva</s> (knowability), etc. ... ///

body.text: 5 /// dharmatveneṣṭaiḥ so 'pi pradhānādiḥ siddha eva tasmin sattāsāmānyaṃ sādhyate / atrāpi jñeyādirūpeṇa dharmī kalpyamāno na tāvat sukhādyātmakaḥ eko nityatvādibhir viśeṣaiḥ siddhaḥ śakyate kalpayitum* / tasyaivaṃ viśeṣasya sādhyatvāt* / tasmād anena kiñcij jñeyam astīti sādhyaṃ ta .. ///
body.translated_text: [5] /// ... that <s>pradhāna</s> etc. is already established through properties accepted as such; and regarding it, <s>sattā</s> in general is being proved. [Reply:] Even here, the <s>dharmin</s> being constructed in the form of knowability etc. cannot first be constructed as having the nature of pleasure etc., as a single [entity], with the specific properties of eternality etc., because precisely that specific property is the <s>sādhya</s> (what is to be proved). Therefore, by this, what is being proved is only that 'something knowable exists'—that ... ///

body.text: 6 /// nirviśeṣaṇam astīty asminn arthe siddhe 'pi sati pradhānādeḥ siddhir astu naiveti yāvat* / na hi jñeyasattāmātre vivādas tad evāha tathāpīti naivābhimataṃ / kiñcit siddhaṃ syād ity arthaḥ / anyatreti agnir atra dhūmād ityādike prayoge ta ///
body.translated_text: [6] /// ... even when this meaning, that [something] exists without any qualifier, is established, the establishment of <s>pradhāna</s> etc. may or may not follow—that is the import. For there is no dispute regarding mere existence as knowable. He states precisely this with 'even so' etc. Nothing that is intended [by the <s>Sāṃkhya</s>] would be established—this is the meaning. 'Elsewhere' means in a usage such as 'fire exists here, because of smoke' etc. ///

body.text: v1 /// .. virahiṇeti tena pradeśenāyogas tena virahaḥ pradeśenāyoga ity arthaḥ / so 'sti yasya sāmānyasya tat tathoktaṃ viśiṣṭapradeśasaṃbandhineti yāvat* / anvayo na siddha eva viśiṣṭapradeśasaṃbandhinaḥ / sāmānyasyānyatrāvṛtteḥ netyādinā pariharati / na vai kaści ///
body.translated_text: [v1] /// ... 'lacking connection'—the meaning is: lack of connection with that location, i.e., non-connection with that [particular] location. That universal which possesses this [non-connection] is so called; the meaning is: connected with a specific location. The concomitance is not established at all for that which is connected with a specific location, because the universal does not fail to occur elsewhere. He resolves this with 'not indeed any' etc. Not indeed any ... ///

body.text: 2 /// .. .. .. .. .. .. .. .. .. .. .. .. .. .. .. + + .. nāntarīyakāgnyavinābhāvī darśanīyaḥ kīdṛśena vākyenety āha yatretyādi / yatra kvacid dhūmas tatrāgnir iti / sa dhūmas tatheti sarvopasaṃhāravyāptidarśanena / agnimātreṇa vyāptaḥ siddho yatraiva pradeśe dharmiṇi svayaṃ svena dhūmarūpeṇa nirākṛtabhrāntikāraṇena dṛśyate tatraiva pra ///
body.translated_text: [2] ...inseparable from fire, is to be demonstrated. By what kind of statement? He says 'yatra' etc.: 'wherever there is smoke, there is fire.' That smoke, 'thus'—by the observation of <s>vyāpti</s> (pervasion) through universal correlation, is established as pervaded by fire alone. In the very location where the <s>dharmin</s> (subject) is seen by itself in its own form as smoke, with the cause of error excluded, there precisely...

body.text: 3 /// .. numeyapratītau sādhyanirdeśena na kiñcit prayojanaṃ / tena vināpi sādhyasiddheḥ tad evāha tatretyādi / tatra sāmānyadharmiṇi liṅgasya darśanaṃ tasyākhyānamātrāt sādhyadharmiṇaṃ liṅgasya yaḥ saṃbandho 'nvayavyatirekalakṣaṇas tasya cākhyānamātrāt* / iṣṭasya sādhyasya siddheḥ yataś ca sādhyadharmiṇo na nirdeśas tadā tadanirdeśe ca kathaṃ tadviśiṣṭena dharmavi .. ///
body.translated_text: [3] ...in the cognition of the object to be inferred, the statement of the <s>sādhya</s> (probandum) serves no purpose, since the <s>sādhya</s> is established even without it. He says precisely this with 'tatra' etc.: the observation of the <s>liṅga</s> (inferential mark) in the general <s>dharmin</s>, and from the mere mention of the relation of the <s>liṅga</s> to the <s>sādhya-dharmin</s>—that relation characterized by <s>anvaya</s> (positive concomitance) and <s>vyatireka</s> (negative concomitance)—and from its mere mention, the <s>sādhya</s> that is desired is established. And since the <s>sādhya-dharmin</s> is not stated, then without its statement, how can the relation to a particular property...

body.text: 4 /// .ād ayaṃ dhūmo 'gninā sādhyadharmeṇāvinābhāvī siddho yatra pradeśe dṛśyate tatrārthād evāgnis tena pradeśenāyogaṃ vyavacchinatti / agnimantaṃ pradeśaṃ sādhayatīti yāvat* / iti hetoḥ sa pradeśas tathety agnimatvena sādhya ucyate / pramāṇavyāpārapṛṣṭabhāvitayā / na punas tathopanyāsapūrvakaḥ viśiṣṭapradeśasaṃbandhyagni .. .. .. ///
body.translated_text: [4] ...this smoke, established as inseparable from fire, the <s>sādhya-dharma</s> (property to be proved)—wherever it is observed in a location, there fire is implied; it excludes the non-connection of that location [with fire]. That is, it establishes the location as possessing fire. Therefore, by the <s>hetu</s> (reason), that location is called 'thus,' i.e., the <s>sādhya</s> (probandum), as possessing fire. [This is established] as being posterior to the operation of <s>pramāṇa</s> (means of valid cognition), not however through a prior statement of a qualified location in connection with fire...

body.text: 5 /// .. .. .. .. .. .. t* / atha punaḥ pakṣopanyāsapūrvaka evānvayas tatpūrvakatve vā pākṣopanyāsapūrvakatve vānvayasya nyāyaprāpte kaḥ pratijñāṃ sādhanād apākaroti / pakṣanirdeśasyāpi tadānīṃ sādhanatvāt* / na caivaṃ tasmāt sthitam etat* / pakṣam anupadarśayaiva sādhayadharmasāmānyena liṅgasya vyāptiḥ / kathanī .. .. .. .. cāryadiṅnāgasy. ///
body.translated_text: [5] ...now, if the <s>anvaya</s> (positive concomitance) is necessarily preceded by the statement of the <s>pakṣa</s> (thesis), or if, when it is reasonable that the <s>anvaya</s> be preceded by the statement of the thesis—who then separates the <s>pratijñā</s> (proposition) from the <s>sādhana</s> (proof)? Since the statement of the <s>pakṣa</s> too is at that time [part of] the proof. But this is not so; therefore this is established: the <s>vyāpti</s> (pervasion) of the <s>liṅga</s> (mark) with the general <s>dharma</s> (property) establishes the <s>pakṣa</s> without separately demonstrating it. How this is to be explained...the master <s>Dignāga</s>...

body.text: 6 /// ty āha / tathā cetyādi / liṅgasya dhūmāder avyabhicāras tu sādhyadharmeṇa / anyatreti viśiṣṭadharmisaṃbandhatyāgenānyasminn aparāmṛṣṭādhāraviśeṣe dharmimātre / anye tu sādhyadharmiṇo 'nyatra dṛṣṭāntadharmiṇīti vyācakṣate / ta ///
body.translated_text: [6] ...he says 'tathā ca' etc. The non-deviation of the <s>liṅga</s> (inferential mark), such as smoke, from the <s>sādhya-dharma</s> (property to be proved). 'Anyatra'—in another [locus], by abandoning the connection with a qualified <s>dharmin</s>, in a mere <s>dharmin</s> (subject) whose specific substratum is not considered. Others, however, explain: 'elsewhere' means in the <s>dṛṣṭānta-dharmin</s> (example-subject), other than the <s>sādhya-dharmin</s>...

body.text:
R Pramāṇavārttikaṭīkā
r1 /// .. na darśitaṃ liṅgaṃ tatra vivādāśraye dharmiṇi / prasiddhaṃ niścitaṃ tadyuktaṃ tena vyāpakena dharmeṇa yuktaṃ sādhyadharmiṇaṃ gamayiṣyatīti / tasmād ityādinopasaṃhāraḥ / yat tūktaṃ yathā sattāyāṃ sādhyāyāṃ ananvayo doṣaḥ / tathā hetāv apīti tatrottaraṃ aparāmṛṣṭetyādi / aparāmṛ .. ///
body.translated_text:
[R] <s>Pramāṇavārttikaṭīkā</s>
[r1] ...the <s>liṅga</s> (inferential mark) is shown there in the <s>dharmin</s> that is the locus of dispute. [When it is] well-established and ascertained, [then] 'tadyuktam'—connected with that pervading property, it will indicate the <s>sādhya-dharmin</s>. With 'tasmāt' etc. he summarizes. As for what was said—that in the case of <s>sattā</s> (existence) being the <s>sādhya</s>, the absence of <s>anvaya</s> (positive concomitance) is a defect...

body.text: 2 /// sattāmātrasya hetor anvayo dṛṣṭyāntadharmiṇi vṛttir na vihanyate / kiṃbhūtasya sādhyasya vastumātre sādhane kriyamāṇe ity āha tanmātravyāpinaḥ sattāmātravyāpinaḥ sādhanetyādinā vyācaṣṭe / vastumātravyāpini sādhyadharme svabhāvaviśeṣāparigraheṇa sādhane punaḥ satve kriyamāṇe nānvayavyāghātaḥ na sādhanaśūnyo dṛṣṭā ///
body.translated_text: [2] ...the <s>anvaya</s> of the mere <s>hetu</s> (reason), namely <s>sattā</s> (existence), is not obstructed by its occurrence in the <s>dṛṣṭānta-dharmin</s> (example-subject). Of what kind of <s>sādhya</s>? When mere reality is being proved—he says 'tanmātra-vyāpinaḥ' and explains with 'sattāmātra-vyāpinaḥ sādhana' etc. When the <s>sādhya-dharma</s> pervades mere reality, without adopting any particular essential nature...

body.text: 3 /// .. tvamātrasya hetutvenāśrayaṇe 'pīty arthaḥ / na punaḥ sādhyatve sattāyā viśeṣānāśrayaḥ kasmāt sattāmātre sādhye sādhanavaiphalyāt* / sattāyāṃ sādhyamukhena doṣam uktvā sādhanamukhenāha / api cetyādi / sattāyāṃ sādhyāyāṃ hetur bhāvadharmo vā upādīyeta / bhāvābhāvadharmo vā ekāntenaiva dhar. .. .. tatrāsiddhe pradhānā .. ///
body.translated_text: [3] ...even when mere existence is not taken as the <s>hetu</s>—this is the meaning. Moreover, the non-resort to particulars when <s>sattā</s> (existence) is the <s>sādhya</s>—for what reason? Because when mere existence is the <s>sādhya</s>, the <s>sādhana</s> (proof) would be futile. Having stated the defect from the side of the <s>sādhya</s> when <s>sattā</s> is the probandum, he states [the defect] from the side of the <s>sādhana</s> with 'api ca' etc. When <s>sattā</s> is the <s>sādhya</s>, the <s>hetu</s> is either a positive property of existence or...

body.text: 4 /// .. sya sa satve sādhye vyabhicārī anaikāntikaḥ / yo 'py abhāvasya dharmaḥ sa satve sādhye viruddho satvasyaiva sādhanāt* / yasyāś ca sattāyāṃ sādhyāyām asiddhādidoṣād dhetur eva nāsti sā sattā sādhyate kathaṃ taddhetur iti sattāsādhanahetuḥ traya avayavā yasyā doṣajāter doṣaprakṛteḥ sā trayi tāṃ yathāsaṃbhavaṃ nāti ///
body.translated_text: [4] ...that, when existence is the <s>sādhya</s>, is a deviating [reason], i.e., <s>anaikāntika</s> (inconclusive). And a property of absence, when existence is the <s>sādhya</s>, is <s>viruddha</s> (contradictory), since it proves the very opposite of existence. And that <s>sattā</s> for which, when it is the <s>sādhya</s>, there is no <s>hetu</s> at all due to defects such as non-establishment—how is that <s>sattā</s> to be proved? Therefore the <s>hetu</s> for proving <s>sattā</s>...

body.text: 5 /// .. dinaitad eva vibhajate / bhāvadharmo hi hetur upādīyamānas tatkāryātmako vā syāt tatsvabhāvabhūto vā na tāvad ādyaḥ pakṣaḥ kāryakāraṇabhāvasyaivāsiddheḥ / kāraṇaviśeṣeṇa hi kāryakāraṇabhāvaḥ pratyakṣānupalaṃbhasādhanaḥ sa ca pradhāne nāsti kāryavyatirekalakṣaṇo 'pi kāryakāraṇabhāvaḥ kāraṇam. ///
body.translated_text: [5] ...he analyzes precisely this. For a positive property of existence taken as a <s>hetu</s> (reason) would be either of the nature of its effect or of the nature of its essence. The first option does not hold, because the <s>kāryakāraṇabhāva</s> (cause-effect relation) itself is unestablished. For the cause-effect relation, which is proved by direct perception and non-apprehension, depends on a specific cause—and that does not exist in <s>pradhāna</s> (primal matter)...

body.text: 6 /// .. svabhāvatayā bhāvadharmo hetur ucyate / sa katham asidhasattāke pradhānādau syāt* / yasmād yo hi vādī bhāvadharmaṃ hetuṃ tatra pradhānādāv icchati sa kathaṃ pradhānādikaṃ bhāvaṃ necchet* / bhāvasvabhāvasyaiva taddharmatvāt* / kathaṃ tarhi svabhāvasyāyaṃ dharma iti vyatirekeṇa kathyata iti ced āha / svabhāva eva hītyādi / kayā ///
body.translated_text: [6] ...a positive property of existence is called a <s>hetu</s> by virtue of essential nature. How could that obtain in something like <s>pradhāna</s> whose existence is unestablished? For the proponent who accepts a positive property as the <s>hetu</s> in <s>pradhāna</s> etc.—how could he not accept <s>pradhāna</s> etc. as existing? Since it is a property precisely of the nature of existence. How then can one's own...

body.text: 7 /// .. kṣiptabhedāntaratvena dharmiṇaṃ vyavasthāpya punas tam eva pratikṣiptabhedāntaratayā dharmatvena vyvasthāpya tathākṛtasaṃketena śabdena vyatirekīva bhinnarūpa iva dharmiṇaḥ / sakāśāt* jñātṛvāñcheturodhena nirdiśyate / etac ca prāg eva niññītam ity āha / na hītyādi / uktam etad bhedāntarapratikṣepāpratikṣepau tayor dvayor ityādinā ///
body.translated_text: [7] ...having established the <s>dharmin</s> (subject) as something whose other distinctions are rejected, and then again establishing that very same [entity] as the <s>dharma</s> (property) by virtue of having its other distinctions rejected, [the proponent], through a word with a convention thus constructed, designates [it] as if it were different in form from the <s>dharmin</s>, through the restriction of the direction of the knower's desire. And this was already settled earlier...

body.text:
8 /// 'py abhāvadharmaḥ sy. + + .. .. bhayadharmo hetuḥ syād ity āha / anāśritetyādi / etad āha / yadi vidhinā bhāvātmakaṃ dharmam aṅgīkṛtyābhāvasyocyeta / ekapratiṣedhena vā tadviparītavastubhāgātmakaṃ
v1 /// d virodhas tac ca nāsti yato vyati + + + .. .yārthapratiṣedhamātrasya dharmatvena kalpitasyābhāve 'py avirodhāt* / tatra vyatirekagrahaṇena vidhimukhopāttaṃ dharmam apanayati mātragrahaṇena pratiṣedhopāyalabhyaṃ vastubhāgātmakaṃ / vyatirekamātram eva kasmād bhavatīty āha / aparyudāseneti pratiṣedhopasarjano hi vidhiḥ paryudā ///
body.translated_text:
[8] ...even an absence-property...a property of fear might be the <s>hetu</s>—he says 'anāśrita' etc. He says this: if, by a positive statement, having accepted a property that is of the nature of existence, and then [the property] of absence is stated through a single negation, or a reality-portion that is the opposite of that...
[v1] ...there would be contradiction; but that is not the case, because the <s>vyatireka</s> (negative concomitance)...

body.text: 2 /// nāśritavastuna iti yatrānyāvyavacchedena + stv āśrīyate sa paryudāsasya viṣayo na ceha vastu kiñcid āśritaṃ tad eva vyavacchedamātram āha netyādi / na bhavati mūrta ity amūrtatvaṃ mūrtapratiṣedhalakṣaṇam abhāve 'pi syān nirupākhyasyetyādi / ayaṃ bhāvaḥ pratiṣedho hi nivṛttiḥ / sā ca kriyā na ca kriyāśrayam antareṇa kriyā yujyate / tasmād abhāvo na prati ///
body.translated_text: [2] ...of a thing not resorted to—where something is resorted to through the exclusion of others, that is the domain of <s>paryudāsa</s> (implicative negation); but here no real thing is resorted to. That very mere exclusion he states with 'na' etc.: 'it is not corporeal'—incorporeality, defined as the negation of corporeality, would apply even to absence, to what is unnameable—and so forth. This...

body.text: 3 /// .. ty abhiprāyaḥ / nanu santy abhāve 'pi śabdā ity atrāntare nirupākhyasyāpi pratiṣedhaviṣayatvaṃ pratipāditam eva satyaṃ kiṃtu nirviṣayasya naño 'prayogād ity anena pūrvapakṣeṇoktam idaṃ tu kriyākārakasaṃbandhadvāreṇeti viśeṣaḥ / yadi na pratiṣedhaviṣayatā nirupākhyasya tat kim idānīṃ nirupākhyaṃ vidhiviṣayo 'stu ta .. ///
body.translated_text: [3] ...is the intent. [Objection:] 'But there are words even regarding absence'—in that context, it has already been demonstrated that even what is unnameable can be the object of negation. True, but since a negation without an object has no application—this was stated as the prior position. However, the distinction here is 'through the relation of action and agent.' If there is no object of negation...

body.text: 4 /// ṣayaḥ pratiṣedhaviṣaya eva / kasmād vidhītyādi / vidher yā nivṛttiḥ sa eva pratiṣedho vidhipratiṣedhābhyām aparasyābhāvāt* na ca nivṛttir nāma kācid vastubhūtā kriyāsti yenābhāveṣu na syāt* / tad etad anantaroktaṃ vyavacchedamātraṃ dvayor api bhāvābhāvayoḥ saṃbhavat satve sādhye gamakatvaṃ katham ātmasāt kuryāt* yasmād vi .. ///
body.translated_text: [4] ...the object of negation is precisely the object of negation. For what reason? 'Vidhi' etc.—the cessation of <s>vidhi</s> (positive injunction) is itself <s>pratiṣedha</s> (prohibition); since apart from positive injunction and prohibition there is nothing else, and cessation is not some real action that would prevent [its application] to absences. This, just stated, is mere exclusion, for both...

body.text: 5 /// tra śaṃkā tasyā vyavacchedena satve ca sādhye vipakṣo 'satvaṃ na cobhayadharmasya hetor vipakṣād asato vyāvṛttir asti sa ca vādī svavācā svavacanena sattāsādhanasya hetor ubhayadharmatāṃ bruvāṇaḥ / sato 'nyatrāpi asaty apy ubhayadharmasya hetor vṛttiṃ bhāṣate / evaṃ hy asyobhayadharmatvaṃ syād yadi sati cāsati + varteta / sattāyā .. ///
body.translated_text: [5] ...here is a doubt; by its exclusion: when existence is the <s>sādhya</s>, the <s>vipakṣa</s> (counter-example) is non-existence. And there is no exclusion of the <s>hetu</s>, which is a property of both [thesis and counter-example], from the non-existent <s>vipakṣa</s>. And the proponent, by his own words, asserting the property-of-both-sides nature of the <s>hetu</s> that proves existence—even in [the domain] other than the existent, i.e., in the non-existent too, the <s>hetu</s> being a property of both sides...

body.text: 6 /// .. .. .. ..ṃ .. .. tuṃ sattāyāṃ vadato 'sya vādino viruddho hetuḥ syāt* / satvaviparītasyāsatvasya sādhanāt* kaḥ punar abhāvasyaiva dharmo bhavatīty āha / bhāvamātretyādi / yo hi vastumātravyāpī arthakriyākāritvakṛtakatvādilakṣaṇo 'rthaḥ / tasya vyavacchedo niyamenābhāvasyaiva dharmaḥ / sarvabhāvaniṣedhasyābhāva eva bhā .. ///
body.translated_text: 6 /// ...when speaking of existence (<s>sattā</s>), this disputant would have a contradictory reason (<s>hetu</s>), because it would prove non-existence, the opposite of existence. What then is the property of non-existence alone? — he says 'mere existence of things' and so forth. The object that pervades mere real things — characterized by causal efficacy, being produced, and the like — its exclusion is necessarily a property of non-existence alone. The negation of all existents is precisely non-existence ///

body.text: 7 /// .. .. .. / abhāva evetyādinā vipakṣa eva satvam+ / tad iti tasmāt* ayaṃ yathāvibhaktas triprakāro 'pi hetuḥ sattāsādhane sattāsiddhau yathāvibhaktād dhetutrayān na dānyā gatir asti / sādhanatve liṅgatve / asyāḥ sattāyāḥ sāmānyenānupāttaviśeṣatvena siddhasattāke pakṣe dharmiṇi .. ///
body.translated_text: 7 /// ...by 'non-existence alone' and so forth, existence is [shown to be] in the counter-thesis alone. 'That' means 'therefore.' This three-fold reason as analyzed, in proving existence, in establishing existence — from the three-fold reason as analyzed, there is no other course. In being a proof, in being an inferential mark. Of this existence, in the thesis-subject in which existence is established through universality and without specific qualification ///

body.text:
S Pramāṇavārttikaṭīkā
r1 /// .. .. .. .. tenāsiddhatādoṣaḥ parihṛtaḥ / viruddhatvaṃ anikāntikatvaṃ ca pariharan āha / tena cetyādi / tena sādhyādharmeṇa liṅgasya vyāptiḥ / kathañcid ity anvayamukhena vyatirekamukhena vā yadi niścīyate na virodhavyabhicārau / na viruddham anaikāntikatvaṃ vā / nāyaṃ prasaṃgaḥ sattā ///
body.translated_text:
S <s>Pramāṇavārttikaṭīkā</s>
r1 /// ...thereby the fault of non-establishment is removed. Removing the faults of contradiction and inconclusiveness, he says 'by that' and so forth. The pervasion of the inferential mark by that property [that is] not the property to be proved — if ascertained in some way, whether through the method of positive concomitance or through the method of negative concomitance — [there is] neither contradiction nor deviation. It is neither contradictory nor inconclusive. This consequence does not apply to existence ///

body.text: 2 /// .. .. .. .. .. .. .. .. .. .. .. samāśraye vā pakṣadharmatve vā aniścite sati / tatsvabhāvatayā niścitavyāptidharmisamāśrayasvabhāvatayā yo gamako 'bhimato na sa kaścid gamakaḥ / ata eva hetoḥ / svadharmeṇa svena sādhyadharmeṇa vyāpto hetuḥ / pakṣadharmiṇi siddhasvabhāvo vācyaḥ / niścitatrairūpy. vācya ity arthaḥ ///
body.translated_text: 2 /// ...or when the relation to the substrate, or the property-of-the-thesis-subject status, is not ascertained — what is intended as an indicator, [merely] by having the nature of ascertained pervasion and relation to the substrate — that is not any [real] indicator. For precisely this reason: the <s>hetu</s> (reason), pervaded by its own property — the property to be proved — must be stated as having its own nature established in the thesis-subject. Meaning: it must be stated as having ascertained triple characteristic (<s>trairūpya</s>) ///

body.text: 3 /// .. .. .. .. .. .. .. .. ..* upalaṃbhayan* pradīpaḥ sa evaṃbhūtaḥ kadācid ghaṭādyudarāntarvartī tadrūpāpratipattau / satyāṃ svām arthakriyāṃ stambhādiprakāśanalakṣaṇaṃ na hi karoti yādṛśo gamakaḥ svabhāvas tathoktaṃ gamyas tarhi kīdṛśa ity āha / vyāpakas tasyetyādi / yo 'sau gamako vyāpyaḥ svabhāvas tasya vyāpako niścito vy. ///
body.translated_text: 3 /// ...illuminating — a lamp; such [a lamp], when sometimes situated inside a pot and the like, when there is non-apprehension of that form, though possessing [the capacity for] its own causal efficacy — characterized by illuminating pillars and the like — does not perform it. What kind of indicator has such a nature? Having stated this, he says what the indicated is like: 'the pervader of that' and so forth. That which is the indicated — the pervaded nature — its pervader, ascertained ///

body.text: 4 /// dharmo gamyaḥ / kīdṛśas tasya gamakatvenābhimatasya vyāpakatvena niścitaḥ kathaṃ punar vyāpakatvena niścito bhavatīty āha / taddharmaniścayād eveti / tasya dharmasya gamakadharmatayā svabhāvatayā niścayaḥ / taddharmaniścayaḥ sādhyasya sādhanasvabhāvatayā niścayād evety arthaḥ / iyatānuvartyānuvarttakabhāva uktaḥ / nirvar.. ///
body.translated_text: 4 /// ...the indicated property. What kind? Ascertained as the pervader of what is intended as the indicator. How then is it ascertained as the pervader? — he says 'from the ascertainment of that property alone.' The ascertainment of that property as having the nature of the indicator-property — the ascertainment of the property to be proved as having the nature of the proof — this is the meaning. Thus the relationship of the concomitant and that which follows has been stated. The establishment ///
