body.text: 5 /// ḥ svayannivṛttau satyāṃ tasya vyāpyasya nivarttakaḥ tasyetyādinā vyācaṣṭe / ayaṃ vyāpako dharmaḥ svayaṃ nivarttamānaḥ tasya vyāpyasya nivarttaka iti saṃbandhaḥ / kiṃ kāraṇaṃ yasmād evaṃ hy asyāyaṃ sādhyo dharmo vyāpakaḥ siddho bhavati / yady asya vyāpakasyābhāve tyāpyo na bhavet* / tad iti vākyopanyāse / anenety anantaroktenānuvartyānuva .. ///
body.translated_text: 5 /// ...when it itself ceases, [it is] the remover of that pervaded [entity] — he explains with 'of that' and so forth. This pervading property, itself ceasing, is the remover of that pervaded — this is the connection. What is the reason? Because this property to be proved — the pervader — is established for it. If in the absence of this pervader, the pervaded would not exist — 'that' introduces the statement. 'By this' means: by what was stated immediately before, the concomitant and that which follows ///

body.text: 6 /// pīti sādharmyavato vaidharmyavataś ca sādhanaprayogasya yathākramaṃ gamakalakṣaṇaṃ sādhyasādhakatvalakṣaṇam uktaṃ veditavyam* / tad eva prayogadvaividhyam āha / dvividho hītyādi / yathāhur eka iti naiyāyikāḥ sādharmyavān eva hi prayogo 'nvayī vaidharmyavāṃś ca vyatirekī / nanu cānyathānvayavyatirekiṇo vyavasthāpito yasya vipakṣābhāvāṃ nāsti vyatirekaḥ kevalaṃ sapakṣa eva satvaṃ so 'nyayī yasya tu vipakṣād ekāntena vyav. ..ḥ sapakṣābhāvā .. .. .. .. /// .. nvayasyāyogāt* anvayam antareṇa vyatire ///
body.translated_text: 6 /// ...thus it should be understood that the definition of the indicator — the definition of being proof and being the property to be proved — has been stated respectively for the proof-application that has similarity and the proof-application that has dissimilarity. He states that very twofold proof: 'twofold indeed' and so forth. As the <s>Naiyāyikas</s> say, 'it is one' — indeed the proof based on similarity alone is positive (<s>anvayī</s>), and the one based on dissimilarity is negative (<s>vyatirekī</s>). But the positive-negative [reason] has been established otherwise: one whose absence from the counter-thesis-class does not exist has no negative [concomitance] — it has existence only in the thesis-similar class, and is positive; one that is exclusively excluded from the counter-thesis, with absence from the thesis-similar class... /// ...because of the impossibility of positive concomitance without positive [concomitance], negative [concomitance] apart from positive ///

body.text: 7 /// .. gabhedād anvayī vyatirekī ceti kathyate / iti / vastubalāt tair apy aṅgīkartavyaṃ / etad eva sādhayann āha nānayor ityādi / anayor ity anvayavyatirekiṇor hetvo vastutaḥ svarūpato na kaścid bhedo dvayor apy anvayavyatirekavatvāt* anyatra prayogabhedād iti / tāv evānvayavyatirekau kadācid anvayavatā prayogena pratipā ///
body.translated_text: 7 /// ...because of the difference of application, it is called positive and negative. Thus: by the force of reality, even they must accept [this]. Establishing this very point, he says 'not of these two' and so forth. 'Of these two' — of the positive and negative reasons — in reality, in their own nature, there is no difference between the two, since both possess positive and negative concomitance. 'Otherwise, because of the difference in application' — those very positive and negative concomitances are sometimes understood through an application possessing positive [concomitance] ///

body.text:
8 /// vati prayoge sādharmyam eva pratīyate vaidharmyavati ca vaidharmyam eva tato .. .. .. .. .. dāpy astīti cet tan na yasmāt sādharmyeṇāpi hi prayoge 'rthāt sāmarthyāt sādhyavipakṣād dhetor vyāvṛttir vaidharmyaṃ tasya gatis tad eva sāmarthyam āhāsatītyādi / tasminn iti vaidharmye evaṃ hi sādhyena hetur vyāptaḥ syād yadi sādhyavipakṣā
9 /// .. .. yogo vaidharmyaśabdenoktas tasminn anvayagatiḥ katham ity āhāsatītyādi /
v1 /// .y. .. .. tur vyāptaḥ syād evaṃ tannivṛtyā nivarteta / etac ca vyatirekihetucintāyāṃ vistareṇa vakṣyāmaḥ / anityatve yathā kāryam iti anitya eva kṛtakatvam ity arthaḥ / etac cānvayina udāharaṇaṃ / akāryaṃ vināśinīti / kṛtakatvābhāvo kāryaṃ vināśyabhāvaś cāvināśī tenāyam artho bhavati avināśi vināśābhāve sati akāryaṃ kṛta .. ///
body.translated_text:
8 /// ...in the proof that has [similarity], only similarity is cognized; in [the proof] that has dissimilarity, only dissimilarity — therefore... even so, it exists. If [one says] this — [the reply is] no, because even in a proof through similarity, by implication, by force of meaning, the exclusion of the reason from the counter-thesis of the property to be proved — that is the dissimilarity, its course — he states that very force: 'in the absence of' and so forth. 'In that' means: in dissimilarity. For the reason would be pervaded by the property to be proved in this way: if from the counter-thesis of the property to be proved —
9 /// ...the application stated by the word 'dissimilarity' — how is there the cognition of positive concomitance in that? — he says 'in the absence of' and so forth.
v1 /// ...the reason would be pervaded thus — and by its cessation, it would cease. And we shall explain this at length in the examination of the negative reason. 'As being produced in impermanence' — meaning: being produced exists only in what is impermanent. And this is an example of the positive [reason]. 'What is not an effect is imperishable' — the absence of being produced is [being] an effect; the absence of what perishes is imperishable. Thus the meaning is: what is imperishable, in the absence of perishing, is not an effect, not produced ///

body.text: 2 /// tyādi / anayor ity anvayivyatirekiṇoḥ / yatkiṃcid iti sarvopa + + + + vyāptikathanaṃ tataś cārthān nityād vyāvṛtiḥ kṛtakatvasyeti vyatirekagatiḥ / evaṃ hi sarvaṃ kṛtakam anityaṃ syād yadi na kiṃcin nityaṃ bhavet* yasya nityam eva nāsti tasya kathaṃ tato vyatireka iti cet* tadā saṃdeha eva nāsti tadabhāvāt tatrāvṛtteḥ .. .. ///
body.translated_text: 2 /// ...and so forth. 'Of these two' — of the positive and the negative. 'Whatsoever' — the statement of pervasion with all... and from that, the exclusion of being produced from what is permanent — this is the cognition of negative concomitance. For thus everything produced would be impermanent, if nothing whatsoever were permanent. [If one asks:] for one who has absolutely no permanent thing, how can there be negative concomitance from that? — [the reply is:] then there is simply no doubt, because of its absence, because of the non-occurrence in that ///

body.text: 3 /// .. .. śaṃkyāha kṛtakatvasyetyādi śabdasya ca / kṛtakatve kathita iti anityatvena vyāptaṃ kṛtakatvaṃ yadā śabde kathitaṃ tatra niyamena svaṃ vyāpakaṃ sannidhāpayatīti sāmarthyād evānityaḥ śabda iti bhavati / tasmān nāvaśyam ityādi / avaśyaṃ na nirdeśa iti saṃbandhaḥ / iheti sādharmyaprayoge / avidharmyavantaṃ prayogam āha / vyatireky apī ///
body.translated_text: 3 /// ...he says apprehending doubt: 'of being produced' and so forth, and of sound. When being produced is stated as pervaded by impermanence, when it is stated in sound, it necessarily brings its own pervader into proximity — thus by force of implication, 'sound is impermanent' follows. Therefore 'not necessarily' and so forth — the connection is: the explicit statement is not necessary. 'Here' means: in the proof by similarity. He states the proof without dissimilarity. 'The negative also' ///

body.text: 4 /// .. ..ṃ .. .i .. .inīty asya vivaraṇaṃ / kṛtakaś ca śabda iti pakṣadharmakathanaṃ / ihāpi na pratijñāvacanaṃ / yasmāt siddhatatsvabhāvatayā siddhānityasvabhāvatayā karaṇabhūtayā tadabhāva iti anityatvābhāve sati na bhavataḥ kṛtakatvasya śabde ca bhāvakhyātau satvaprakāśane kṛtakaś ca śabda ity evaṃ kṛte tadātmanaḥ sata ///
body.translated_text: 4 /// ...this is the explanation of that. 'And sound is produced' — this is the statement of the thesis-property. Here too it is not a proposition-statement. Because, by having the nature of established impermanence as an instrument, 'in the absence of that' — in the absence of impermanence — being produced does not exist in sound; and in the manifestation of existence, the revelation of existence, when 'sound is produced' is thus stated — of that having such a nature, being existent ///

body.text: 5 /// .. .. .. .. tyaḥ śabda iti siddheḥ pūrvavad iti sādharmyaprayogāt* / nanv anityatvābhāve kṛtakatvaṃ na bhavatīti prayoge vaidharmyamātram uktam anvayo nokta ity āhānvayas tv ityādi / anvayam antareṇa vaidharmyasyānupapattir arthāpattiḥ tām eva na hītyādināha / atadātmaniyatasyeti anityasvabhā ///
body.translated_text: 5 /// ...sound is impermanent — thus it is established, as before, from the proof by similarity. But [if one objects:] in the proof 'in the absence of impermanence, being produced does not exist,' only dissimilarity has been stated, positive concomitance has not been stated — he says 'but the positive concomitance' and so forth. The impossibility of dissimilarity without positive concomitance is <s>arthāpatti</s> (implication) — he states that very [point] with 'for not' and so forth. 'Of what is restricted to that nature' — of what has the nature of impermanence ///

body.text: 6 /// .. .. .. .. niyatasyaiva tannivṛttau nivṛttir iti yāvat* / yata evaṃ tasmān niyamaṃ tādātmyalakṣaṇaṃ pratibandhaṃ / pramāṇena prasādhya sādhyanivṛttyā hetor nivṛttir vaktavyā / nanu sādhyanivṛttyā nivṛttiḥ kathyate niyamasyaiva prasādhanāya pramāṇāntareṇa cen niyamaḥ prasādhitaḥ kiṃ niṣphalena nivṛttivaca .. ///
body.translated_text: 6 /// ...only of what is restricted [to that nature], cessation occurs upon the cessation of that — this is the import. Since this is so, therefore, having established the restriction — the connection characterized by identity of nature (<s>tādātmya</s>) — by a means of valid cognition, the cessation of the reason upon the cessation of the property to be proved is to be stated. But [if one objects:] the cessation upon the cessation of the property to be proved is stated for the very purpose of establishing the restriction; and if the restriction has been established by another means of valid cognition, what is the use of the fruitless statement of cessation? ///

body.text: 7 /// .. prasādhya paścān nivṛttir abhidhīyeta / atraiko bruvato yat tāvad ucyate niyamapradarśanāya nivṛttivacanam iti tan na yato nivṛttivacanaṃ vipakṣapracārāśaṃkānivṛttyarthaṃ na tu tena saṃbandhaḥ kathyate / sādhyābhāve hetvabhāvasya śabdāt pratīteḥ / anyad eva tādātmyam anyad vipakṣāsatvaṃ asti kaścid avidva ///
body.translated_text: 7 /// ...having established, then cessation is stated. Herein, one [commentator] says: as for what is said — that the statement of cessation is for demonstrating the restriction — that is not [correct], because the statement of cessation is for the purpose of removing the apprehension of occurrence in the counter-thesis, not for stating the connection. [This is] because the absence of the reason in the absence of the property to be proved is understood from the words [themselves]. Identity of nature (<s>tādātmya</s>) is one thing; absence from the counter-thesis is another. There is some ignorant one ///

body.text: 8 /// .. .. .i .. .. .. .. .. ..ḥ pramāṇena siddhaḥ tasmāt tannivṛttyā nivartata iti sā cet sidhyatīti niyamam ity uttarakālabhāvinīti vṛttiḥ tadātmaniyamaṃ .. .. .. .. .. .. tvam ity arthaḥ /
body.translated_text: [8] /// ...established by a <s>pramāṇa</s> (means of valid cognition); therefore, by the cessation of that, [it] ceases—if that is established, then the restriction (<s>niyama</s>)—'arising subsequently' is the commentary (<s>vṛtti</s>). The restriction to that nature (<s>tadātmaniyama</s>) /// ...this is the meaning.

body.text:
T Pramāṇavārttikaṭīkā
r1 /// nye .. nyathā vyācakṣate sādhya eva sādhanasya bhāve niyamaḥ / prasādhya śabdaś cārthād ākṣepavacanas tenāyam arthas tasmān niyamaṃ prasādhya / niyamam arthād ākṣipya nivṛttir vaktavyeti tathābhūtena vacanena nivṛttir vaktavyā yā sāmarthyān niyamam ākṣipatīti atat evāha sā ce .. ///
body.translated_text: <s>Pramāṇavārttikaṭīkā</s> /// ...others explain otherwise: the restriction (<s>niyama</s>) is that the means of proof (<s>sādhana</s>) exists only in the <s>sādhya</s> (probandum). And the word '<s>prasādhya</s>' implies [something] from the meaning; thus the meaning is: therefore, having established the restriction, having implied the restriction from the meaning, the cessation must be stated—by such a statement, the cessation that implies the restriction through [its] capacity is to be stated. That itself he states with 'sā cet' /// ...

body.text: 2 /// .. tena vacanena prakāśyate / tadātmaniyamaṃ sādhyātmaniyamam arthād uktisāmarthyād ākṣipati iti hetoḥ siddho 'nvayaḥ / katham ityādi / paro hi kṛtakaṃ vināśaniyatam icchaty eva kālāntarasthāpinaṃ tu tenāyaṃ praśnārthaḥ / kṛtaka utpādānantaravināśitvenāvaśyam anitya iti / katham avagantavyaṃ kālāntaraṃ ///
body.translated_text: [2] /// ...is illuminated by that statement. 'Restriction to that nature' means the restriction to the nature of the <s>sādhya</s> (probandum)—it implies from the meaning, from the capacity of the statement—thus the positive concomitance (<s>anvaya</s>) of the <s>hetu</s> (reason) is established. Regarding 'katham' ('how?') and so forth: the opponent indeed accepts that what is produced (<s>kṛtaka</s>) is determined to perish (<s>vināśa</s>), but [holds that it] persists for some time; hence the meaning of the question is: how is it to be understood that what is produced (<s>kṛtaka</s>) is necessarily impermanent (<s>anitya</s>) by virtue of perishing immediately after arising? How [should one understand] a later time /// ...

body.text: 3 /// ..ḥ kṛtaka utpādānantaravināśīty ucyate ca sidhyatu nāma kṛtakatvād anityatvaṃ kṣaṇikatvaṃ na sidhyatīti uttaram āha yasmād ityādi / svabhāvād iti svasya kṛtakarūpasya bhāvād utpādād evānubandhitā kṛtakasvabhāvaniṣpattāv evānityatāsvabhāvaniṣpatter ity arthaḥ / tadbhāva ity anityatvabhā .. ///
body.translated_text: [3] /// ...it is said that what is produced (<s>kṛtaka</s>) perishes immediately after arising. And [if one says] 'let <s>anityatva</s> (impermanence) be established from <s>kṛtakatva</s> (being produced), but <s>kṣaṇikatva</s> (momentariness) is not established'—he gives the reply with 'yasmāt' ('because') and so forth. 'From its own nature (<s>svabhāva</s>)' means: from the existence, i.e., the arising, of its own produced form—the connection [follows]; the meaning is that the accomplishment of the nature of impermanence (<s>anityatā</s>) occurs precisely upon the accomplishment of the nature of being produced (<s>kṛtakasvabhāva</s>). 'Tadbhāva' means the state of impermanence /// ...

body.text: 4 /// .. .. tor vinaśvarāṇām anityasvabhāvānāṃ bhāvād utpādāt* etac ca svabhāvād anubandhitety asya vivaraṇaṃ yata evaṃ tasmād ityādi / prakṛtyaivety svabhāvenaiva yadi tu sahetuko vināśaḥ tato 'vaśyaṃ bhāvī na syāt* tad eva darśayann āha sāpekṣāṇām ityādi / tasmān nirapekṣo bhāvo vināśe caśabdo 'vadhāraṇ. ///
body.translated_text: [4] /// ...from the arising, i.e., the coming into being, of perishable things having an impermanent nature. And this is the elaboration of 'connected from [its own] nature.' Since this is so, 'therefore' and so forth. 'By nature itself' means by [its] intrinsic nature alone. But if destruction (<s>vināśa</s>) requires a cause, then it would not necessarily occur. Showing precisely that, he states 'of those that are dependent' and so forth. Therefore, the entity is independent with respect to destruction, and the word 'ca' has the force of restriction /// ...

body.text: 5 /// .. tyatā syā .. ṣāṃ vināśakāraṇam asannihitam* bāhulyād vināśakāraṇānāṃ na kvacid asannidhānam iti ced āha yenetyādi / yeneti yasmāt* / taddhetor iti vināśahetoḥ / teṣām api vināśakāraṇānāṃ nāvaśyaṃ sannidhānam iti saṃbandhaḥ / kasmāt svapratyayādhīnasannidhitvāt* svakāraṇāya tu sannidhānatvāt* na ca vinā .. ///
body.translated_text: [5] /// ...there would be impermanence... the cause of destruction (<s>vināśakāraṇa</s>) is not proximate. [If one objects:] 'Because causes of destruction are numerous, there is nowhere that they are not proximate'—to this he replies with 'yena' and so forth. 'Yena' means 'because.' '<s>Taddhetoḥ</s>' means 'of the cause of destruction.' Even of those causes of destruction, proximity is not necessarily [present]—this is the connection. Why? Because their proximity depends on their own conditions (<s>svapratyaya</s>); proximity is [only] for their own cause; and without /// ...

body.text:
6 /// .. vināśahetor asannidhānāt kaścin na vinaśyed api / sa .. .. hetusannidhānena niyato vināśo yato na hy avaśyaṃ hetavaḥ phalavantaḥ vināśākhyakāryavantaḥ / kasmād vaikalyetyādi sahakārisannidhānavaikalyaṃ / viruddhopanipātaḥ pratibandhaḥ / eteneti sāpekṣasya nāvaśyaṃbhāvitve
In margin (line 8) /// nāśahetūnāṃ nāśasya liṅgatvena ye he .. .. + + + + + + nte teṣāṃ / kasmāt kāryāvyavasthiteḥ nāśahetor nāśasvabhāvakāryotpattiniyamābhāvāt* / keṣāṃ punar vādinām ayaṃ prasaṃga ity āha heyuma .. tyādi / hetumantaṃ
7 /// .. / tad ityādinopasaṃhāraḥ / tad iti tasmāt* / + + + + + .i .. śasyāyaṃ bhāvaḥ / kṛtako 'napekṣas tadbhāvaṃ prati / vināśabhāvaṃ prati /
v1 /// .ināśabhāvaniyataḥ / anena sādhanaphalaṃ / asaṃbhava + + + + + .. .. antyāyāḥ sāmagryāḥ sā tathoktā / kā punar saṃbhavatpratibandhety āha sakaleti / sahakāripratyayena santānapariṇāmena ca paripūraṇety arthaḥ / anena dṛṣṭānta uktaḥ / prayogas tu / ye yadbhāvaṃ praty anapekṣās te tadbhāvaniyatās tadyathāsaṃbhavatpratibandhākāraṇa .. ///
body.translated_text:
[6] /// ...due to the non-proximity of the cause of destruction, some things would never perish. That... destruction determined by the proximity of a cause—since causes do not necessarily have results, i.e., do not necessarily produce the effect called destruction. Why? 'Due to deficiency' and so forth—deficiency in the proximity of cooperating conditions (<s>sahakāri</s>). 'Encounter with an opposing [factor]' means obstruction. 'By this' [refers to] the causes of destruction being the mark (<s>liṅga</s>) of destruction /// ... Why? Because of the non-fixity of the effect—because there is no necessity in the production of the effect whose nature is destruction from the cause of destruction. For which disputants is this consequence [relevant]? He states with 'heyuma...' and so forth. 'Having a cause' (<s>hetumantam</s>)—
[7] /// ...'tad' ('therefore') and so forth is the conclusion. 'Tad' means 'therefore.' /// ...this is the meaning: what is produced (<s>kṛtaka</s>) is independent with respect to that state—with respect to the state of destruction (<s>vināśabhāva</s>). /// ...determined by the state of destruction. By this [is stated] the result of the proof. Impossibility /// ...of the final aggregate—that is so called. What then is the possible obstruction? He replies with 'sakala' ('complete'). Completion by cooperating conditions (<s>sahakāripratyaya</s>) and by the transformation of the continuum (<s>santānapariṇāma</s>)—this is the meaning. By this, an example (<s>dṛṣṭānta</s>) is stated. The formal argument (<s>prayoga</s>) is: those which are independent with respect to the arising of a given [state] are determined to [attain] that state, just as [in the case of] the non-obstruction of what can possibly occur /// ...

body.text: 2 /// vo vināśa iti svabhāvahetuḥ / nanv ityādinānekāntam āśaṃkate / kvacit kārye 'napekṣāṇām api keṣāṃcit kāraṇānāṃ nāvaśyaṃ tadbhāva iti yatrānapekṣās tadbhāvaniyamo nāstīty arthaḥ / kva punar etad ity āha bhūmītyādi / sā hi kāryajanane 'napekṣā tathābhūtāyāṃ satyām api kadācit pratibandhakāle 'ṅkurānutpatteḥ / etac ca santāna ///
body.translated_text: [2] /// ...destruction is [by] a <s>svabhāvahetu</s> (nature-based reason). With 'nanu' ('but') and so forth, [the opponent] raises the objection of inconclusiveness (<s>anekānta</s>). Even for some causes that are independent with respect to a certain effect, that state does not necessarily [follow]—the meaning is that where [causes] are independent, the determination of that state does not exist. Where then does this [occur]? He states with 'bhūmi' ('earth') and so forth. For earth (<s>bhūmi</s>) is independent in producing an effect, yet even when [earth] is present in that condition, sometimes during the period of obstruction a sprout does not arise. And this [relates to] the continuum /// ...

body.text: 3 /// .. nekāntas ta .. yathoktāyāṃ sāmagryā santānapariṇāmo 'pekṣatvāt kāryotpādanasya tato 'napekṣatvād ity asya hetos tatrāvṛttiḥ kṛtakasyāpy asti vināśaṃ prati kālāntarapratīkṣā tato hetur asiddha ity āha naivam ityādi kṛtakasya bhāvasya nāśe kācit kālāntarāpekṣā / yadi hi syāt svabhāvasyāviśeṣāt prāgvat paścād pi na .i ///
body.translated_text: [3] /// ...inconclusiveness... because the production of an effect from the aggregate as described requires the transformation of the continuum (<s>santānapariṇāma</s>), and therefore, because of the non-occurrence of this reason [viz.] 'because of independence' in that case—even of what is produced (<s>kṛtaka</s>), there is the expectation of a later time with respect to destruction, hence the reason is unestablished (<s>asiddha</s>)—he replies with 'na evam' ('not so') and so forth. Of a produced entity, there is no dependence on a later time for [its] destruction. For if there were, then due to the non-difference of [its] intrinsic nature (<s>svabhāva</s>), just as before, afterwards too it would not /// ...

body.text: 4 /// ṇāmāpekṣatvam ato vyabhicāra eva hetor ity āha tatrāpītyādi / na bhūmibījādaya ekasvabhāvāḥ paścād iva prāg api kāryotpādaprasaṃgāt* kiṃtūttarottarapariṇāmena bhinnāḥ / tatreti tasyāṃ santānapariṇāmena bhinnāyāṃ sāmagryām* / ante bhāvā antyā paścād utpannā sāmagrī yā kāryotpādane kṣa ///
body.translated_text: [4] /// ...dependence. Therefore there is indeed deviation (<s>vyabhicāra</s>) of the reason—he states with 'tatrāpi' ('even there') and so forth. Earth, seeds, and the rest do not have a single nature—because there would be the absurd consequence of producing the effect before just as after. Rather, they are differentiated by successive transformations. 'Tatra' means in that aggregate differentiated by the transformation of the continuum. The final [members of the aggregate]—the aggregate produced afterwards—which in the production of the effect /// ...

body.text: 5 /// .. anantaroktā sāmagrī pariṇāmeṣu madhye / pūrvas tarhi pariṇāmaḥ kimarthaḥ kathaṃ vā kāraṇam ity ucyata ity āha anyas tv ityādi / tasmāj janakābhimatād antyāt pariṇāmād anyaḥ tato 'nyaḥ paro 'py astīty āha / pūrva iti tadartha iti samarthakṣaṇārthaḥ / ataś ca kāraṇakāraṇatvād upacāreṇa kāraṇavyapadeśa i .. ///
body.translated_text: [5] /// ...the aggregate just mentioned [is] among the [stages of] transformation. Then what is the purpose of the prior transformation, and how is it a cause?—to this he replies with 'anyas tu' ('but another') and so forth. Another, i.e., one different from the final transformation considered to be the producer, also exists—he states with 'pūrva' ('prior'). 'For that purpose' means for the purpose of [producing] the capable moment. And therefore, because of being a cause of the cause, the designation as 'cause' is applied by figurative usage (<s>upacāra</s>) /// ...

body.text: 6 /// dṛṣṭānta ity āha na cetyādi / tām ity antyāṃ sāmagrīm* / tatreti kārye janye ekatra bhāva iti kāraṇabhūte 'ntye kṣaṇe vikārasyotpattau vā tasyāntyasya kṣaṇasya ekatvahāneḥ pūrvasya pracyuter vikārākhyasya ca dvitīyasyotpatteḥ / tataś ca nāsāv antyaḥ syāt* atha mā bhūd eṣa doṣa iti ta .. ///
body.translated_text: [6] /// ...as an example, he states with 'na ca' ('and not') and so forth. 'Tām' means the final aggregate. 'Tatra' means [when] in the effect to be produced, 'unity of state' means at the final moment which is the cause—upon the arising of a modification (<s>vikāra</s>), or [rather] because the unity of that final moment is lost—because the prior [moment] has departed and because a second [moment] called 'modification' has arisen. And therefore, that would not be the final [moment]. Or, [if one says] 'let this fault not arise,' then /// ...

body.text: 7 /// .. .. .. .. .āraṇ. .. .. kṣaṇasaṃgṛhītasya tadutpādanaṃ kāryotpādanaṃ prati vaiguṇyam akurvāṇasya
body.translated_text: [7] /// ...of that which is included in the [final] moment—the production of that, i.e., the production of the effect, not causing any deficiency in

body.text:
U Pramāṇavārttikaṭīkā
r1 /// .. .kārye śālyaṅkure janye / kasmāt tadutpattipratyayānāṃ bhūmyudakādīnāṃ kadācit tatrāpi yavabījādau sannidhānāt* / te nirapekṣā api na śālyaṅkuraṃ janayanti / tatas tadavastho 'nekānta iti / katham iti siddhāntavādī / sāpekṣā evety arthaḥ eṣām iti ///
body.translated_text: <s>Pramāṇavārttikaṭīkā</s> /// ...in the effect, the rice sprout to be produced—why? Because among the conditions for its production, such as earth, water, and the rest, sometimes even there, i.e., even in barley seeds and the like, there is proximity [of those conditions]. Yet they, though independent, do not produce a rice sprout. Therefore, the same inconclusiveness (<s>anekānta</s>) [applies]—[asks the opponent]. 'How?'—[asks] the proponent (<s>siddhāntavādī</s>). 'They are indeed dependent (<s>sāpekṣa</s>)'—this is the meaning. 'Of these' /// ...

body.text: 2 /// .. t. saṃbandhaḥ / tatsvabhāvāpekṣā iti śālyaṅkurotpādanasvabhāvāpekṣāḥ / tathā ca na hetos tatra vṛttir iti nānekāntaḥ / evaṃ tarhīti paraḥ / upādhyapekṣaṃ śuddhaṃ ca hetudvayam apy adhikṛtyāha kṛtakānāṃ keṣāṃcit satāṃ veti tatrāpi keṣāṃcid iti saṃbandhaḥ / sa eva svabhāvo nāsti yo naśvaraḥ / pratikṣa ///
body.translated_text: [2] /// ...this is the connection. 'Dependent on that nature' means dependent on the nature of producing a rice sprout. And thus the reason does not apply there, so there is no inconclusiveness (<s>anekānta</s>). 'If so, then'—[says] the opponent. Addressing both types of reason—one with a qualifying condition (<s>upādhi</s>) and one that is pure—he states: 'Of some produced things (<s>kṛtaka</s>) that exist'—'even there, of some' is the connection. That very nature does not exist which is perishable. The expectation /// ...

body.text: 3 /// .. śvarasvabhāvāpekṣatvāt* na vinaśvarāḥ / anenānapekṣatvād ity etasya hetor asiddhatām āha / śālibījetyādinā pariharati ādiśabdād yavabījādīnāṃ sa svabhāva iti abhimatetarakāryajananājananasvabhāvaḥ / svahetor iti kṛtvā yo yavabījādir na taddhetuḥ sa śālibījahetur yasya hetur na bhavatīty . ///
body.translated_text: [3] /// ...because of dependence on a perishable nature, [they] are not perishable. By this, he states the unestablishedness (<s>asiddhatā</s>) of the reason 'because of independence.' He refutes with 'śālibīja' ('rice seed') and so forth. By the word 'ādi' ('etc.'), barley seeds and the like [are included]. 'That nature' means the nature of producing or not producing the intended alternative effect. 'From its own cause'—because of being produced [by its own cause]; that which, like barley seed and the rest, is not the cause of that—the cause of rice seed, of which it is not the cause /// ...

body.text: 4 /// katven. v. .. vād dhetupravibhāga eva nāstīti yo manyate taṃ praty āha niyataśaktiś cetyādi / niyatā pravibhaktā śaktir ātmātiśayalakṣaṇā yasya sa niyataśaktiḥ / sa hetur iti śāliyavabījajananaḥ / na hi bhūtabhautikatvaṃ nāma kiṃcid ekaṃ rūpam iṣyate pratyakṣapratītaś ca hetupravibhāga ity āha .. .. ///
body.translated_text: [4] /// ...because of being produced... there is no differentiation of causes at all—to one who thinks thus, he replies with 'niyataśaktiḥ ca' ('and [that which has] a determinate power') and so forth. 'One whose power is determinate' means one who has a determinate, i.e., differentiated, power characterized by an inherent distinction (<s>ātmātiśaya</s>). 'That is the cause'—namely, the production of rice and barley seeds [respectively]. For the state of being composed of elements (<s>bhūtabhautikatva</s>) is not accepted as some single form; and the differentiation of causes is apprehended by direct perception (<s>pratyakṣa</s>)—he states /// ...

body.text: 5 /// nenā .i .i .. ta ity āha na cetyādi arthānāṃ padārthānāṃ svabhāvaniyama iti pravibhaktasvabhāvatvam* / ākasmika ity ahetukaḥ kasmān na yukta ity āha / anapekṣasyetyādi / hetunirapekṣasya kvacid eva deśe na sarvatra kvacit kāle na sarvadā kvacid dravye yavabhījādau na sarvatreti / yo 'yaṃ .. ///
body.translated_text: [5] /// ...he states with 'na ca' ('and not') and so forth. The determination of the intrinsic nature (<s>svabhāvaniyama</s>) of things (<s>padārtha</s>) means having a differentiated intrinsic nature. 'Causeless' (<s>ākasmika</s>) means without a cause (<s>ahetuka</s>). Why is [that] not tenable? He states with 'anapekṣasya' ('of that which is independent') and so forth. Of that which is independent of a cause (<s>hetu</s>)—only in a certain place, not everywhere; at a certain time, not always; in a certain substance, such as barley seed and the rest, not in all [substances]—that which /// ...

body.text: 6 /// .ād deśā .. ..m apekṣya bhavan* hetumān iti gamyate / etāvanmātranibandhanatvād dhetumatvavyavahārasyeti svabhāvahetuḥ / yathā śalibījādīnāṃ hetubhedāt svabhāvaniyamaḥ tathātrātrāpi kṛtakeṣu satsu vā niyamahetur vaktavyo yato niyāmakād dhetor ime kṛtakāḥ santo vā kecin naśvarātmano jātā nānye ///
body.translated_text: [6] ///...with respect to place...it is understood as 'possessing a cause' (<s>hetumān</s>). Since the conventional usage of 'possessing a cause' is based on just this much alone, it is a <s>svabhāvahetu</s> (nature-based reason). Just as in the case of rice-seeds and the like, there is a restriction of nature (<s>svabhāvaniyama</s>) due to the difference of causes, so too here as well, a cause of restriction must be stated for produced things (<s>kṛtaka</s>) or existent things, such that from a restricting cause, these produced or existent things—some are born with a perishable nature (<s>naśvarātman</s>) and not others. ///

body.text: 7 /// .. yeṣāṃ te sarvajanmānaḥ / kāraṇamātrād utpanna .. .. viśeṣeṇa nāśasiddher ity arthaḥ / etac ca parapratītam eva kālāntaravināśaṃ gṛhītvoktam iti pratyetavyam* / na tu pratikṣaṇavināśaṃ tasyaiva sādhayituṃ prastutatvāt* kālāntareṇāpi tu vināśe siddhe / tasya naśvarātmā sidhyati anyathā prāgvat paścād api ///
body.translated_text: [7] ///...those whose [births] are such—they are born of all [types of] birth. From a mere cause, having been produced...the meaning is that destruction is established through a particular [cause]. And this should be understood as having been stated by adopting destruction at another time, which is already accepted by the opponent. It is not [meant to establish] momentary destruction (<s>pratikṣaṇavināśa</s>), since that itself is what is being proven. But when destruction even at another time is established, its perishable nature (<s>naśvarātman</s>) is proven; otherwise, just as before, afterward too... ///

body.text:
8 /// bhāvāt* tasmād anaśvarātmānaṃ hetuṃ janayatītīcchatā sarvakālasthāpinaṃ janayatīty aṅgīkartavyam* / tathābhūtaṃ ca kṛtakaṃ vastu nāsti sarvasya kālāntareṇa
v1 /// vad buddhīndriyadehāḥ pravāhacchedi .. upalabhyante .. .. ś. .. vṛkṣādayaḥ parvatādayo 'pi tadāśritavṛkṣādivināśād vinaśyanty evānyathāśritavināśābhāvāt* / tajjātīyatayānye 'pi antaśo vijñānakāryasyāpi kadācid anutpādād vajrāder api vināśaḥ siddhaḥ / na hetukṛto naśvarānaśvarvibhāgaḥ .. .. .. .. ///
body.translated_text:
[8] ///...because of [its] existence. Therefore, one who wishes [to maintain] that [a cause] produces something of imperishable nature (<s>anaśvarātman</s>) must accept that it produces something that persists for all time. But such a produced (<s>kṛtaka</s>) thing does not exist, since everything [is destroyed] at another time.
[v1] ///...like the intellect (<s>buddhi</s>), sense organs (<s>indriya</s>), and body (<s>deha</s>), which are observed as having breaks in their continuum (<s>pravāha</s>)...trees and the like, and even mountains are destroyed through the destruction of the trees etc. dependent on them; otherwise there would be no destruction of their supports. By being of the same kind, others too—even down to the effect of consciousness (<s>vijñāna</s>)—since even it sometimes does not arise, the destruction of even a diamond (<s>vajra</s>) and the like is established. The division into perishable and imperishable is not caused by the cause... ///

body.text: 2 /// .. janmisvabhāvaḥ sa eva nāstīti naśvaraḥ / etad uktaṃ bhavati ja .. eva kasyacit tādṛśaṃ yena kaścin naśvaro bhavati aparo neti na vai janma nāśisvabhāvasya hetuḥ / na hi janma nāma kiṃcid vyatiriktam asti yena nāśisvabhāvaṃ kaṃcit kuryāt* svabhāva eva hi padārthānāṃ janma tasyaiva hetupravibhāgo nirūpyate .. .. ///
body.translated_text: [2] ///...the nature of being born—that very [thing] does not exist, hence it is perishable (<s>naśvara</s>). This is what is stated: birth...of something is such that by it someone becomes perishable and another does not—that is not so, for birth is not the cause of a nature that is [inherently] destructible. For there is no birth as something separate that could make something have a destructible nature; indeed, birth is nothing but the intrinsic nature (<s>svabhāva</s>) of entities, and the classification of causes is determined with respect to that very [nature]... ///

body.text: 3 /// .. .. .. + .āśasiddhiḥ nāpi janma nāśisvabhāvasya hetus tasmān nātra kṛtakeṣu satsu vā hetor vinaśvarāvinaśvarajanakatvena svabhāvavibhāgaḥ tadabhāvād dhetupravibhāgābhāvāt phalasya kṛtakasya sato vā naśvarānaśvaratvena vibhāgo nāstīti asamānaṃ yavabījādinā / kṛtakatvāpekṣa .. .. ///
body.translated_text: [3] ///...the establishment of destruction. Nor is birth the cause of a destructible nature. Therefore, here among produced things (<s>kṛtaka</s>) or existent things, there is no division of nature (<s>svabhāvavibhāga</s>) in terms of the cause producing perishable versus imperishable things. Because that [division] does not exist, and because there is no classification of causes, there is no division of the effect—whether produced or existent—into perishable and imperishable. Thus it is dissimilar to barley-seeds and the like. With regard to being produced (<s>kṛtakatva</s>)... ///

body.text: 4 /// .. .. .. .. .. .. .. .. tasyābhyupagatatvāt* naitad asty akṛtakasya satvāyogāt* sarvaṃ hi satvaṃ deśakālavastupratiniyataṃ ahetutve tanniyamāyogāt* paramāṇūnām aṇumanasaś ca mūrtimatvād deśaniyamaḥ pareṇāṅgīkṛtaḥ tatkṛtopakārābhāve 'smin deśe paramāṇur nānyasmin* tathā .. ///
body.translated_text: [4] ///...because that is accepted. This is not so, since something unproduced (<s>akṛtaka</s>) cannot be existent, for all existence is restricted to a particular place, time, and thing; without a cause, such restriction would be impossible. The restriction of place for atoms (<s>paramāṇu</s>) and the atomic mind (<s>aṇumanas</s>) is accepted by the opponent due to their having material form (<s>mūrtimatva</s>). In the absence of benefit produced by that [cause], an atom is in this place and not in another; likewise... ///

body.text: 5 /// .. .. .. .. .. .. tasmād ityādinā ye yadbhāvaṃ praty anapekṣā ityādeḥ prayogasyārtham upasaṃharati seyaṃ vināśasya nirapekṣatā kvacid vastuni kadācit kāle vināśasya yo bhāvas tena virodhinī kiṃ karoti / tadabhāvaṃ tasya kecit kadācic ca vināśabhāvasyābhāvaṃ svabhāvena sattayā sādhayati ///
body.translated_text: [5] ///...therefore, by 'tasmāt' etc., he summarizes the meaning of the formulation 'those which are independent with respect to the existence of something' etc. This independence of destruction—the existence of destruction of some entity at some time—what does [an objection] that contradicts this accomplish? It establishes the absence of that—that is, the absence of destruction [occurring] for certain [things] at certain times—through intrinsic nature (<s>svabhāva</s>), through [their mere] existence (<s>sattā</s>). ///

body.text: 6 /// .. ṇa .. .. .. + + + + + + + t. yasmin kāle bhavati yatra vā dravye taṃ kālaṃ dravyaṃ cāpekṣata iti nirapekṣa eva na syād ity uktaṃ prāk* / sa tarhīti paraḥ / nety acāryaḥ / sattāyā yo hetubhāvas tasmād eva tathotpatteḥ naśvarasvabhāvotpatteḥ / etad eva spaṣṭayann āha sato hītyādi / .. ///
body.translated_text: [6] ///...at whatever time it exists, or in whatever substance, it depends on that time and substance—thus it would not be independent at all, as was stated previously. 'If so'—says the opponent. 'No'—says the master (<s>ācārya</s>). Because of the causal nature (<s>hetubhāva</s>) of existence (<s>sattā</s>), from that very [existence], there is production in that manner—production of a thing with perishable nature (<s>naśvarasvabhāva</s>). Clarifying this very point, he says 'of the existent, indeed' etc. ///

body.text: 7 /// ścit kāraṇād bhāva utpāda iti cet* ayam abhiprāyo na sarvasya sataḥ kāraṇāyattatā / kecid dhi santaḥ kūṭasthanityā eva dikkālaparamāṇvādayaḥ tataś ca satvād ity asya hetos tair evānekānta iti / ākasmikīty ahetukā .. ///
body.translated_text: [7] ///...if [one objects that] an entity, an arising, [comes] from some particular cause—the intention is this: not everything existent is dependent on a cause, for some existent things are eternally immutable (<s>kūṭasthanitya</s>), such as spatial direction (<s>dik</s>), time (<s>kāla</s>), atoms (<s>paramāṇu</s>), and the like. And therefore, the reason 'because of being existent' is subject to the fallacy of <s>anaikāntika</s> (inconclusiveness) by those very [counter-examples]. 'Spontaneous' (<s>ākasmikī</s>) means without a cause... ///

body.text:
V Pramāṇavārttikaṭīkā
r1 /// .. .. .. .. .. .. kasmād vyavasāyaphalatvān niścayaphalatvāt praṃāṇānāṃ pratyakṣam api hi pramāṇaṃ sarvākāragrahaṇe 'pi yeṣv evākāreṣu niścayam ā .. .. .. .. .. .. .. .. .. .. .. .. .. + + + n. cey. .. .. .. .. .. .. .. .. .. ///
body.translated_text:
[V] <s>Pramāṇavārttikaṭīkā</s>
[r1] ///...why? Because <s>pramāṇas</s> (means of valid cognition) have ascertainment (<s>vyavasāya</s>) as their result, because they have definite cognition (<s>niścaya</s>) as their result. For even perception (<s>pratyakṣa</s>), which is a <s>pramāṇa</s>, though it apprehends all aspects, with respect to precisely those aspects in which it produces certainty... ///

body.text: 2 /// paricchedo yasya cetasa iti vigrahaḥ / saṃśaye saty avaśyaṃ na pravartitavyam ity evaṃ niścitaṃ ceto na karotīty arthaḥ / saṃśayād api kvacil lokasya kṛṣīvalādeḥ pravṛtteḥ kathaṃ tarhy apravṛttiphalatvenāsyāḥ prāmāṇyam uktam ity ata āha / tathātve tad i + + + .. .. .. ///
body.translated_text: [2] ///...'that whose mind has discrimination'—this is the analysis of the compound. When there is doubt (<s>saṃśaya</s>), one necessarily should not act—the meaning is that a mind so determined does not produce [action]. Since even from doubt there is activity in the world for some people such as farmers (<s>kṛṣīvala</s>) and the like, how then is its authority (<s>prāmāṇya</s>) stated in terms of having non-activity as its result? To this he says 'tathātve tad' etc. ///

body.text: 3 /// .. .y. .. .. .r. .. seyam adṛśyaviṣayānupalabdhir apravṛttiphalāproktā / liṅgātiśayabhāvinīti liṅgam anupalabdhis tasyātiśayo viśeṣa upalabdhilakṣaṇaprāptasyeti / tasya bhāvaḥ satvam* / tad yasyām asti sā tathoktā / liṅgaviśeṣaṇavatīty arthaḥ / upalabdhilakṣaṇa + + + + + + + yāvat* / ///
body.translated_text: [3] ///...this non-apprehension (<s>anupalabdhi</s>) of an invisible object (<s>adṛśyaviṣaya</s>) is stated as having non-activity as its result. 'Having the character of an extraordinary mark' (<s>liṅgātiśayabhāvinī</s>)—the mark (<s>liṅga</s>) is non-apprehension; its excellence (<s>atiśaya</s>) or distinction is 'of that which has obtained the conditions of perception' (<s>upalabdhilakṣaṇaprāpta</s>). Its existence (<s>bhāva</s>) means its being present (<s>satva</s>). That which has this is so called. The meaning is: that which possesses the qualification of the mark. The conditions of perception (<s>upalabdhilakṣaṇa</s>)...up to [this point]. ///

body.text: 4 /// prāptasyety asmād viśeṣaṇād utpadyate / atretyādinā vyācaṣṭe / atety asadvyavahāre / yathodāhṛtā prāg iti / asajjñānaphalā kācid dhetubhedavyapekṣayetyādinā / yat punar uktam apramāṇam anupalabdhir iti / nāviśeṣeṇa boddhavyaṃ kiṃtu svabhāvetyādi / deśādiviprakarṣa .. bhāvaḥ jñāpakaṃ liṅgaṃ tayo ///
body.translated_text: [4] ///...arises from the qualifier 'of that which has obtained [the conditions of perception]'. He explains with 'atra' ('here') etc. 'Ata'—in the context of non-existence (<s>asadvyavahāra</s>). 'As previously illustrated'—with the statement 'some cognition of the non-existent, dependent on a difference in reasons' etc. As for the statement 'non-apprehension (<s>anupalabdhi</s>) is not a <s>pramāṇa</s> (means of valid cognition)'—this should not be understood without qualification, but rather [with the qualification] 'of the intrinsic nature' (<s>svabhāva</s>) etc. The remoteness of place etc....the indicator (<s>jñāpaka</s>) is the mark (<s>liṅga</s>); of those two... ///

body.text: 5 /// sādhye nasti prāmāṇyam iti svabhāvājñānaṃ pratyakṣanivṛttiḥ / jñāpakājñānam anumānanivṛttiḥ / adṛśyaviṣayāyāḥ pratyakṣānumānanivṛtter ayaṃ nyāya udāhṛta iti samudāyārthaḥ / yasyetyādinā vyācaṣṭe / yasya kasyacid arthasya viprakṛṣṭasya svabhāvaḥ pratyakṣeṇa nopalabhyate deśādiviprakarṣāt* kāraṇāt* sa svabhāvaḥ / tad anu ///
body.translated_text: [5] ///...there is no authority (<s>prāmāṇya</s>) with respect to the object to be proven (<s>sādhya</s>)—thus ignorance of intrinsic nature (<s>svabhāvājñāna</s>) is the cessation of perception (<s>pratyakṣa</s>). Ignorance of the indicator (<s>jñāpaka</s>) is the cessation of inference (<s>anumāna</s>). This principle has been illustrated for the non-apprehension (<s>anupalabdhi</s>) that has an invisible object—such is the meaning of the whole passage. He explains with 'of which' etc.: of whichever remote object, the intrinsic nature (<s>svabhāva</s>) is not apprehended by perception (<s>pratyakṣa</s>) due to the cause of remoteness in place etc.—that intrinsic nature, following that... ///

body.text: 6 /// .. tyakṣanivṛttimātreṇāsan nāma yathoktaṃ prāg iti na ca tathā viprakṣṛṭeṣu svasāmarthyopādānāj jñānotpādanaśaktir astītyādinā svabhāvājñānasyety etad vyākhyāya / jñāpakājñānasyety etad vyākhyātukāma āha yo 'pītyādi / jñāpakasyety asya vivaraṇaṃ liṅgasyeti / atīndriyaḥ pratikṣipyate 'rthaḥ / sarvathaiva yathā nāsti viraktaṃ ///
body.translated_text: [6] ///...merely through the cessation of perception, [something] is called non-existent, as was stated before. And it is not the case that with respect to remote things, there is the power to produce cognition through one's own capacity of apprehension—thus having explained 'ignorance of intrinsic nature' (<s>svabhāvājñāna</s>), wishing to explain 'ignorance of the indicator' (<s>jñāpakājñāna</s>), he says 'yo 'pi' etc. The gloss of 'of the indicator' (<s>jñāpakasya</s>) is 'of the mark' (<s>liṅgasya</s>). The meaning of 'beyond the senses' (<s>atīndriya</s>) is rejected. In every way, just as [something] does not exist, [so too what is] devoid [of indicators]... ///

body.text: 7 /// .. vā pratikṣipyate / atra viśeṣaḥ pratikṣipyate na dharmisattāmātraṃ yathā nāsti dānetyādi / dānaṃ ca hiṃsāviratiś ceti dvandvaḥ / tadviṣayāś cetanās tathoktā dānacetanānāṃ hiṃsāviraticetanāṃ cety arthaḥ / abhyudayahetutā viśiṣṭānāgataphalahetutā / atra cetanānāṃ na svarūpaṃ pratikṣipyate tā .. .. .. ///
body.translated_text: [7] ///...or is rejected. Here a particular [attribute] is rejected, not the mere existence of the property-bearer (<s>dharmin</s>). As in 'giving does not exist' etc.—'giving' (<s>dāna</s>) and 'abstinence from violence' (<s>hiṃsāvirati</s>) is a <s>dvandva</s> (copulative compound). The volitions (<s>cetanā</s>) directed toward those are so called—meaning the volitions of giving and the volitions of abstinence from violence. Being a cause of prosperity (<s>abhyudaya</s>) means being the cause of a distinguished future result. Here, the intrinsic form of those volitions is not rejected; they... ///

body.text:
8 /// .. cetanānāṃ pratyakṣatvād abhyudayahetutā / tadātmabhūtā pratyakṣaiva tat kuta iyaṃ bhrāntir ity āha / pratyakṣe 'py artha ityādi / pratyakṣe 'py arthe viparyasta ity anena saṃbandhaḥ / apavadetāpi pratikṣiped api /
v1 /// .t. ity āhātatphaletyādi / atatphalā anabhyudayaphalā ye dṛṣṭās cetanāviśeṣāḥ / avyākṛtāḥ / taiḥ sādharmyāt* sādharmyam eva katham iti ced āha / phalasyānantaryābhāvād iti yā anyā atatphalāś cetanāḥ yāś ca tatphalāḥ / ubhayatra tatphalasyānantaryaṃ na dṛśyate / na tāvateti phalasyānantaryada ///
body.translated_text:
[8] ///...because of the perceptibility of those volitions (<s>cetanā</s>), being a cause of prosperity (<s>abhyudayahetutā</s>)—that which has that nature is perceptible itself. Then whence this error? He says 'pratyakṣe 'py arthe' ('even in a perceptible object') etc. 'Even in a perceptible object, erroneous'—this is the connection. 'Would deny' means 'would also reject.'
[v1] ///...thus he says 'atatphala' etc. Those that have non-prosperity as their result (<s>atatphalā</s>), those special volitions (<s>cetanāviśeṣa</s>) that are observed as not having prosperity as their result—are ethically indeterminate (<s>avyākṛta</s>). By similarity with those—if asked how there can be similarity—he says: 'because of the absence of immediate succession of the result' (<s>phalasyānantaryābhāva</s>). Those other volitions that do not have that result and those that do have that result—in both cases, the immediate succession of that result is not observed. 'Not so'—the immediate succession of the result... ///

body.text: 2 /// .. t kālāntareṇottarottarāvasthāpariṇāmalakṣaṇena vyavahitānāṃ phalānāṃ darśanāt* mūṣikā cālarkaś ceti dvandvaḥ / alarka unmattaḥ śvā / mūṣikālarkayor daṃśakṛtaṃ yadviṣaṃ tasmāt pūrvam adṛṣṭvā vikārāt kālāntareṇa mūrcchādilakṣaṇasya vikārasya darśanāt* mūṣikāviṣādau paścād vikāradarśanād yuktaṃ tatphalasāmarthyānumān. ///
body.translated_text: [2] ///...because results that are separated by the transformation characterized by successive stages at another time are observed. 'Mouse and mad dog' (<s>mūṣikā ca ālarkaś ca</s>)—this is a <s>dvandva</s> compound. <s>Alarka</s> means a rabid dog. From the poison caused by the bite of a mouse or a rabid dog, without having seen [symptoms] before the alteration, through seeing the alteration characterized by fainting etc. at another time—because of observing the alteration afterward from mouse-poison and the like, the inference of the capacity of that result is justified... ///

body.text: 3 /// satvam eva nyāyyam ity āha / tad ityādi / tatra danādicetanābhya āyatyāṃ phalabhāve virodhābhāvād bādhakapramāṇābhāvāt* atra phaladānasāmarthyābhāve sādhye 'nupalabdhimātram apramāṇaṃ yadi bādhakaṃ pramāṇaṃ nāstīty apratikṣepo bhāve 'stitve kiṃ pramāṇaṃ naivāsti pramāṇaṃ ataḥ sattāniścayo 'pi na yukta iti satyam ata eva bādhakasā ///
body.translated_text: 3 /// ...existence alone is justified — he says: 'tad' and so forth. There, since there is no contradiction to the future fruition of results from <s>cetanās</s> (intentions) such as <s>dāna</s> (giving), etc., there is no defeating <s>pramāṇa</s> (<s>bādhaka</s>). Here, when the incapacity to grant results is to be proven, mere non-apprehension is not a <s>pramāṇa</s> (means of valid cognition). If there is no defeating <s>pramāṇa</s>, there is non-rejection. As for existence — what is the <s>pramāṇa</s>? There is indeed no <s>pramāṇa</s>. Therefore, even the ascertainment of existence is not justified — this is true. For this very reason, the defeating... ///

body.text: 4 /// .. .. .. iti viraktacittasarvajñatve bhaved vā pramāṇam ity apratikṣepaḥ / tac ca saṃbhavat pramāṇaṃ dvitīye paricchede 'bhidhāyiṣyate / syād etad yadi hiṃsāviraticetanānām abhyudayahetutālakṣaṇaḥ svabhāvo 'sti tadā tāsu gṛhyamāṇāsu so 'pi gṛhyeta na ca gṛhyate / na ca yasmin gṛhyamāṇe ya .. gṛhyate / sa tasya svabhāv. ///
body.translated_text: 4 /// ... ...thus, there may be a <s>pramāṇa</s> (means of valid cognition) for the <s>sarvajñatva</s> (omniscience) of one whose mind is dispassionate — this is the non-rejection. And that possible <s>pramāṇa</s> will be set forth in the second chapter (<s>pariccheda</s>). One might object: if the <s>svabhāva</s> (intrinsic nature) characterized as being the cause of <s>abhyudaya</s> (worldly prosperity) exists in the <s>cetanās</s> (intentions) of <s>hiṃsā</s>-abstention (<s>virati</s>), then when those are apprehended, that [nature] too should be apprehended — but it is not apprehended. And that which is not apprehended when something is being apprehended... is its <s>svabhāva</s>... ///

body.text: 5 /// dṛśyate tato 'rthakriyāyā akaraṇād asatvam ity etad bādhakaṃ bhaviṣyatīty āha tad atretyādi / tad iti vākyopanyāse / atreti nirdhāraṇe eṣu prakrānteṣu viprakṛṣṭeṣu artheṣu madhye keṣāṃcid arthānāṃ svabhāvānāṃ veti .. .. .i .. .. .. ..ḥ / tathāpi .. ///
body.translated_text: 5 /// ...is seen; therefore, from the failure to produce <s>arthakriyā</s> (causal efficacy), non-existence — this would be the defeating [cognition]. He says: 'tad atra' and so forth. 'Tad' introduces the statement. 'Atra' is for specification — among these matters that have been introduced, which are remote, among certain objects, [whether] of <s>svabhāvas</s> (intrinsic natures)... ... ...even so... ///

body.text: 6 /// .. tavābhāvāt tadviṣayasyānubhavasya yathāgṛhītasvarūpaniścayotpādanasāmarthyābhāvāt* keṣāṃcid arthānāṃ svabhāvādiviprakṛṣṭānāṃ kāryaṃ jñāpakaṃ tasyābhāvād bhavej jñāpakāsiddhiḥ / kāryasyaiva kasmād abhāva ity āha / kāraṇānām ityādi / na hi kāra .. + + + + mātma .. ///
body.translated_text: 6 /// ...due to the absence of that, because of the incapacity of the experience pertaining to that domain to produce ascertainment of the nature as apprehended; for certain objects that are remote in terms of <s>svabhāva</s> (intrinsic nature) and so forth, the indicator is the effect (<s>kārya</s>), and due to the absence of that, there would be the non-establishment of the indicator. Why is there absence of the effect itself? He says: 'kāraṇānām' and so forth. For indeed, the cause... + + + + self... ///

body.text: 7 /// arvāgdarśanāviṣayabhūtāyāḥ kāraṇāt* / neyateti yathoktajñāpakābhāvamātreṇa / tadabhāva ity atīndriyānāṃ devatāviśeṣādīnāṃ svabhāvaviśeṣāṇāṃ .. .. .. .. .. .. .. .. .. bhāvaḥ / pratyakṣānumānani .. .i .. .. .. ///
body.translated_text: 7 /// ...because of the cause that is beyond the scope of ordinary perception. 'Na iyata' means: merely through the absence of the aforesaid indicator. 'Tadabhāva' means: of the <s>atīndriya</s> (supersensory) — of the particular <s>svabhāvas</s> (intrinsic natures) of specific deities (<s>devatā</s>) and such... ... ... ...existence. <s>Pratyakṣa</s> (perception) and <s>anumāna</s> (inference)... ... ///

body.text: 8 /// .. .. .. .i kvacid darśanamāndyā dṛṣṭaḥ svabhāvo na niścīyate ///
body.translated_text: 8 /// ... ...in some cases, due to dullness of vision, the perceived <s>svabhāva</s> (intrinsic nature) is not ascertained. ///

body.text:
W Pramāṇavārttikaṭīkā
r1 /// .. yathā viṣādidravyaṃ abhyāsād evaṃ dānādicetanāsv api āvirbhūtaprakāśānāṃ yogināṃ yoginām abhivvyaktiḥ saṃbhāvyatāṃ yogisiddhau ca saṃbhavat pramāṇaṃ vakṣyāmaḥ / tathā keṣāṃcid anārabdhakāryāṇāṃ bījādīnāṃ kālāntareṇa kāryābhinirvṛttir dṛśyate / evaṃ atīndriyeṣv api saṃbhāvyatāṃ / tathā hi piśācādayaḥ keṣu .. ///
body.translated_text:
[W] <s>Pramāṇavārttikaṭīkā</s>
[Folio r1] /// ...just as poisonous substances and the like, through repeated practice — so too with regard to the <s>cetanās</s> (intentions) of <s>dāna</s> (giving) and the like, the manifestation of <s>yogins</s> whose illumination has become manifest should be considered possible. And we shall state the possible <s>pramāṇa</s> (means of valid cognition) in establishing the <s>yogin</s>. Similarly, for certain things like seeds whose effects have not yet begun, the production of effects is seen after a lapse of time. Thus, with regard to <s>atīndriya</s> (supersensory) things too, this should be considered possible. For example, <s>piśācas</s> (spirits) and the like, to some... ///

body.text: 2 /// .. nāsattāsādhanaṃ nāpi kāryānupalaṃbhaḥ / kāraṇānupalambhas tu tatrāpy abhāvasādhanam ity āha / kārye tv ityādi / kārye tu svabhāvādiviprakarṣiṇy api kārakājñānaṃ kāraṇānupalabdhir abhāvasya sādhanam eva svabhāvetyādinā vyācaṣṭe / viprakṛṣṭaviṣayasya svabhāvasyābhāve sādhye svabhāvānupalambha evāpramāṇ. ///
body.translated_text: 2 /// ...is not a proof of non-existence, nor is there non-apprehension of the effect. However, non-apprehension of the cause is indeed a proof of absence even there — he says: 'kārye tu' and so forth. With regard to the effect, even though it is remote from <s>svabhāva</s> (intrinsic nature) and so forth, ignorance of the agent — non-apprehension of the cause — is indeed a proof of absence. He explains with '<s>svabhāva</s>' and so forth. When the absence of a <s>svabhāva</s> pertaining to a remote domain is to be proven, mere non-apprehension of the <s>svabhāva</s> is not a <s>pramāṇa</s>... ///

body.text: 3 /// .. palambha eva niścetum aśakyaḥ / svabhāvādivirakarṣiṇāṃ kenacit saha kāryakāraṇabhāvasyaivāniścayāt* satyam etat kiṃtu sanuddiṣṭaviṣayasyābhāvamātrasya praptipattau śakyate / etāvad vaktuṃ kāraṇam antareṇa kāryaṃ svabhāvādiviprakṣṛṭam apy avaśyaṃ na bhavatīti / iyatā leśenāsyopanyāsaḥ / ata eva sā ///
body.translated_text: 3 /// ...apprehension alone cannot be ascertained, because there is no certainty whatsoever of a cause-effect relationship between things remote in <s>svabhāva</s> (intrinsic nature) and so forth with anything. This is true, but when the mere absence of a specifically indicated object is to be established, this much can be said: without a cause, an effect, even one remote in <s>svabhāva</s> and so forth, certainly does not come into being. By this much indication, the presentation [of the argument] is made. For this very reason, that... ///

body.text: 4 /// .. nuddiṣṭaviṣayo 'pi śakyate vyavasthāpayituṃ / nanv ityādi paraḥ / agner vināśe 'pi vāsagṛhādau dhūmasya darśanāt* tathā cāsaty api kāraṇe kāryaṃ dṛṣṭam iti vyabhicāraḥ / asati kāraṇe kāryaṃ na syād ity anena vākyena kāraṇasthitikālabhāvikāryaṃ / yāvat kāraṇasattā tāvat kāryasattety arthaḥ / evaṃ na brūmo yena kā ///
body.translated_text: 4 /// ...even that which has a specifically indicated object can be established. 'Nanu' and so forth — [this is] the opponent. Even when fire has perished, smoke is observed in a dwelling and so forth. And thus, an effect is observed even when the cause does not exist — this is the deviation (<s>vyabhicāra</s>). [Reply:] 'When the cause does not exist, the effect would not exist' — by this statement, [what is meant is] the effect that exists contemporaneously with the cause. As long as the cause exists, so long the effect exists — this is the meaning. We do not say it in such a way that... ///

body.text: 5 /// saṃgaḥ syāt* / kāraṇāt sakṛdutpannasya kāryasya kāraṇanāśe 'pi kālāntaram avsthānāt* / kiṃ tarhy anena vākyenocyata ity āha heturahitetyādi / yady apy ayaṃ granthena ca tathetyādi granthena vyavahitaḥ tathāpy artha .. ///
body.translated_text: 5 /// ...there would be a connection. Because an effect, once produced from a cause, persists for some time even after the destruction of the cause. What then is stated by this statement? He says: '<s>heturahita</s>' (devoid of cause) and so forth. Although this [passage] is separated by the text 'tathā' and so forth in the manuscript, nevertheless in meaning... ///

body.text: v1 /// ḥ kāraṇe naṣṭe kāryasya sthānam eva nāstīti kuto vyabhicārāśaṃkā / tathā hi yo 'gnijanyo dhūmakṣaṇas tasyāgnau vinaṣṭe nāstyavasthānaṃ / yato yasmin kṣaṇe dvitīye agnijanyasya dhūmakṣaṇasya sattā tasminn eva kāraṇabhūto 'gnikṣaṇo vinaṣṭas tadanantaraṃ ca tṛtīye kṣaṇe dhūmakṣaṇo 'pi vinaṣṭa iti ku ///
body.translated_text: [Folio v1] /// ...when the cause has perished, there is simply no persistence of the effect — so whence the suspicion of deviation? For indeed, the moment of smoke that is born from fire — when the fire has perished, there is no persistence of that. Because in the very second moment when the moment of smoke born from fire exists, the moment of fire that is its cause has already perished, and immediately thereafter, in the third moment, the moment of smoke too has perished — so whence... ///

body.text: 2 /// gnihetukas tad eva darśayann āha na ca tathetyādi / tathā sthāyīti naṣṭe 'py ādye kāraṇe kālāntarasthāyī tadupādānaḥ pūrvaniruddhahetūpādānaḥ kathaṃ tarhi pascāt yo 'pi dhūmo 'gnihetuka ity ucyata ity āha / pāraṃparyetyādi / ādyaṃ tāvad dhūmakṣaṇaṃ vahnir eva janayati sa dhūmakṣaṇo 'paraṃ so 'py apara .. ///
body.translated_text: 2 /// ...caused by fire. Demonstrating precisely that, he says: 'na ca tathā' and so forth. 'Tathā sthāyī' means: persisting for a further duration even when the first cause has perished; 'tadupādāna' means: having as its material cause [something] whose prior cause has ceased. How then is the subsequent smoke also said to be caused by fire? He says: '<s>pāramparyeṇa</s>' (through succession) and so forth. First, fire itself generates the first moment of smoke; that moment of smoke [generates] another; and that too another... ///

body.text: 3 /// .. .. .. .. mato jananāt* / tatkāryavyapadeśaḥ / tasyādyasya kāraṇasya paścātyam api kāryam ity evaṃ vyapadeśaḥ / yady asya hetoḥ kathaṃcit pramāṇenābhāvaḥ sidhyet* tadā tatphalaṃ tasya pratiṣedhyamānasya hetoḥ phalaṃ nāstīti niściyate / tadabhāvaḥ pratīyeta hetunā yadi kenacid ity asyaiva vakṣyamānasya .. ///
body.translated_text: 3 /// ... ... ...because of being generated from that. 'Tatkāryavyapadeśa' means: the designation as an effect of that — that the subsequent too is an effect of the original cause — such is the designation. If the absence of this cause could somehow be established by a <s>pramāṇa</s> (means of valid cognition), then it would be ascertained that the result (<s>phala</s>) of that — the result of the cause being negated — does not exist. 'Its absence would be cognized if by some reason' — this is an elaboration of what will be stated... ///

body.text: 4 /// .y. .. anuddiṣṭaviṣaye tu naivam apekṣyate / yadi kāraṇaṃ na bhavet kāryam apy avaśyaṃ na bhaved dheturahitāyā bhāvotpatter asaṃbhāvād ity etāvanmātrasya pratipādanāt tac cānantaraṃ evoktam iti svabhāvetyādi / arthasyeti vyāpakasya svabhāve liṅginy asatvena sādhye svabhāvānupalambhaś ca vyāpakānupalambha ///
body.translated_text: 4 /// ...but with regard to what has not been specifically indicated, such [investigation] is not required. If the cause does not exist, the effect too certainly would not exist, because the arising of an existent from something devoid of a cause (<s>heturahita</s>) is impossible — since only this much is being demonstrated, and this has been stated immediately [before]. '<s>Svabhāva</s>' and so forth: when the non-existence of the <s>svabhāva</s> (intrinsic nature) of an object — the pervader — is to be proven as the logical mark (<s>liṅgin</s>), the non-apprehension of <s>svabhāva</s> is also a non-apprehension of the pervader... ///

body.text: 5 /// svabhāva evetyādinā vyācaṣṭe / kiṃcid iti vyāpakānupalambhaḥ / yadi anupalabhyamāno vyāpakaḥ svabhāvo 'sya niṣedhyābhimatasya vyāpyasya siddhaḥ syāt* tadā bhavet pramāṇaṃ yathā vṛkṣatvaṃ vyāpakaṃ si .. ///
body.translated_text: 5 /// ...he explains with '<s>svabhāva</s> eva' and so forth. 'Kiṃcid' refers to the non-apprehension of the pervader (<s>vyāpaka</s>). If the pervading <s>svabhāva</s> (intrinsic nature) that is not apprehended were established as belonging to that which is intended to be negated — the pervaded (<s>vyāpya</s>) — then it would be a <s>pramāṇa</s> (means of valid cognition). Just as <s>vṛkṣatva</s> (tree-ness) is the pervader, being established... ///

body.text:
X Pramāṇavārttikaṭīkā
r1 /// .. vaḥ pratīyeta hetunā kenacit svabhāvānupalaṃbhākhyena yadītyādinārtham āha yady asya kārakasyābhāvaḥ sidhyed iti saṃbandhaḥ / vyāpakasya ca svabhāvasyābhāvaḥ kutaścid gamakād dhetor iti upalabdhilakṣaṇaprāptānupalambhāt* sa eva hi pratiṣedhe ga .. .. .. .. .. .. .. .. .. ///
body.translated_text:
[X] <s>Pramāṇavārttikaṭīkā</s>
[Folio r1] /// ...its absence would be cognized through some reason — through a reason called the non-apprehension of <s>svabhāva</s> (intrinsic nature). He explains the meaning with 'yadi' and so forth: 'If the absence of the agent could be established' — this is the connection. And the absence of the <s>svabhāva</s> that is the pervader [is established] from some indicative reason (<s>hetu</s>) — that is, from the non-apprehension of what has fulfilled the conditions of apprehension (<s>upalabdhilakṣaṇaprāpta</s>). For that alone is indicative in negation... ... ... ... ///

body.text: 2 /// .. .. .. .. .. .. .. ddh. kārakavyāpakayor abhāvāsiddhau nivartye 'pi kārye vyāpye ca saṃśayāt* / etac coddiṣṭaviṣayasyābhāvasya sādhane draṣṭavyaṃ yathoktaṃ prāk* / yadi svabhāvābhāve sādhye tadanupalambha evāpramāṇām ucyate katham idānīṃ bhāvasya ghaṭādeḥ svayam anupalabdher abhāvasiddhiḥ / uttaram āha dṛśyasye .. ///
body.translated_text: 2 /// ... ... ... ...since the absence of the agent and the pervader is not established, there is doubt even regarding the effect to be negated and the pervaded. This is to be understood with regard to proving the absence of a specifically indicated object, as stated earlier. If, when the absence of <s>svabhāva</s> (intrinsic nature) is to be proven, mere non-apprehension of that is said to be not a <s>pramāṇa</s>, then how now is the absence of an existent thing like a pot established through its own non-apprehension? He gives the answer: '<s>dṛśyasya</s>' (of the perceptible)... ///

body.text:
In margin (line 7) /// na svabhāvāviprakarṣam āha / tasyaivaṃvidhasya bhāvasyānupalabdhasya sataḥ bhāvābhāvaḥ sattāyā abhāvaḥ pratītyate / kadā darśanābhāvakāraṇāsaṃbhave sati darśanābhāvasya kāranaṃ kāraṇāntarāṇāṃ
3 /// tasyāsaṃbhave sati upalambhapratyayāntarasākalye satīty arthaḥ / bhāvo hītyādinā vyācaṣṭe / ātmānaṃ bhāvayati bodhayatīti bhāvaḥ / svabhāvādyaviprakṛṣṭaḥ svabhāvaviśeṣaḥ / sa yadi bhaved yathāsvaṃ grāhakeṇa kāraṇena yasya yad grāhakam indriyaṃ tenopalabhya eva bhavet* etena dṛśyasyety etad vyākhyātaṃ sa yathokto ///
body.translated_text:
[Marginal note, line 7] /// ...he states the non-remoteness of <s>svabhāva</s>. The absence of existence — absence of being — of such a thing that is not apprehended is cognized. When? When the absence-of-perception has no [other] cause — when the cause for the absence of perception is impossible. The cause of absence of perception is other causes...
3 /// ...when that is impossible — when the other conditions of apprehension are complete — this is the meaning. He explains with '<s>bhāvo hi</s>' and so forth. '<s>Bhāva</s>' means: that which makes itself known, that which illuminates — this is [the meaning of] <s>bhāva</s>. 'Not remote from <s>svabhāva</s> and so forth' means: a particular <s>svabhāva</s>. If that were to exist, it would exist only as apprehended by its own appropriate apprehending instrument — the sense faculty (<s>indriya</s>) that is its apprehender. By this, '<s>dṛśyasya</s>' (of the perceptible) is explained. That which is as described... ///

body.text: 4 /// ṣu vyavadhānādiṣv ādiśabdād vaikalyapratibandhādiṣu asatsūpalambhapratyayeṣu satsv iti yāvat* / upalabhyata eva nānyathā / tathābhūto 'nupalabdhas tv asann iti niścīyate kiṃ kāraṇaṃ tādṛśaḥ sataḥ upalabdhilakṣaṇaprāptasya sataḥ / upalambhāvyabhicārāt* ya evāyaṃ svabhāvasyābhāvaṃ niścaye dṛśyasya darśanetyādinokto 'yam eva hetur ve ///
body.translated_text: 4 /// ...in obstructions such as intervening barriers and the like — the word 'ādi' includes deficiency, impediment, and so forth — when the conditions of apprehension are absent, [yet] present, 'is apprehended only, not otherwise.' One that is of such a nature, when not apprehended, is ascertained as non-existent. What is the reason? Because such a thing, being one that has fulfilled the conditions of apprehension (<s>upalabdhilakṣaṇaprāpta</s>), does not deviate from apprehension. This very reason that was stated with '<s>dṛśyasya darśanena</s>' (by the perception of the perceptible) and so forth for ascertaining the absence of <s>svabhāva</s> — this very <s>hetu</s> (reason)... ///

body.text: 5 /// .. dhye viruddhasya cetyādi caśabdo bhinnakramaḥ tadviruddhopalabdhau ceti draṣṭavyaḥ yasyābhāvaḥ sādhyas tena yo viruddhas tena yo viruddhas tasyopalabdhau ca syād asattāyāḥ pratiṣedhyābhāvasya niścayaḥ kiṃ kāranaṃ viruddhasya bhāvasya bhāve sattāyāṃ tadbhāvabādhanāt* / tasya niṣedhyābhimatasya sattābādhanāt* dravyoḥ sahānavasthānād iti yāvat* / yo hītyādinā / vyācaṣṭe / yo hi bhāvo yena .. .. ///
body.translated_text: [5] ///...regarding 'viruddhasya ca' and so forth—the particle 'ca' is in a different order; it should be understood as 'tadviruddhopalabdhau ca' (and upon the apprehension of what is contradictory to that). When the <s>abhāva</s> (absence) of something is what is to be proved (<s>sādhya</s>), and upon the apprehension of what is contradictory to it, there would be ascertainment of the non-existence of the absence that is to be negated. For what reason? Because when the contradictory entity exists—i.e., when it has existence—there is the sublation of its existence (<s>tadbhāvabādhanāt</s>). Because there is sublation of the existence of what is considered to be the thing to be negated—that is, because two [contradictory] substances cannot coexist together. With 'yo hi' and so forth, he explains: 'For whatever entity by whatever'... ///

body.text: 6 /// .. .. .. .. .. .. .. .. .i .. .. ity āha tadupādānayor ityādi tayor viruddhayor ya upādāne tayor anyonyaṃ parasparaṃ / dvaiguṇyaṃ tasyāśrayatvena śītopādānam uṣṇopādānavaiguṇyasyāśraya itarac cetarasyety arthaḥ / tena kāraṇena viruddhayoḥ śītoṣṇakāryayor ekatra yugapadārambhavirodhāt* / tayor anantaroktena prakāre ///
body.translated_text: [6] ///............he says 'tadupādānayoḥ' and so forth. Of those two contradictories, their substrates (<s>upādāna</s>)—of each other, mutually—the deficiency (<s>vaiguṇya</s>): the substrate of cold is the substrate of the deficiency of heat, and vice versa—this is the meaning. For that reason, since the effects of the contradictories, namely cold and heat, are opposed to arising simultaneously in a single locus (<s>ekatra yugapadārambhavirodhāt</s>). Of those two, in the manner just stated... ///

body.text: v1 /// bdhiprabhede / na śītaḥ sparśo 'trāgner ityādi / yady apy atrānupalabdhir iti na śrutis tathāpīdaṃ svabhāvaviruddhākhyaṃ liṅgam anupalabdheḥ sakāśān na pṛthag ucyate / kiṃ kāraṇaṃ tata evānupalambhād virodhagateḥ virodhāc cābhāvasādhanāt* viruddho hi kathaṃ niścīyeta / yadi tadupalaṃbhe pratiyogino 'nupala ///
body.translated_text: [v1] ///...in the sub-division of apprehension. 'There is no cold touch here, of fire' and so forth. Although the word '<s>anupalabdhi</s>' (non-apprehension) is not explicitly heard here, nevertheless this <s>liṅga</s> (logical mark), called <s>svabhāvaviruddha</s> (contradictory in nature), is not stated separately from <s>anupalabdhi</s> (non-apprehension). For what reason? Because the cognition of contradiction arises from that very non-apprehension, and because absence is established through contradiction. For how would the contradictory be ascertained? If, upon the apprehension of that, the counter-correlate's non-apprehension... ///

body.text: 2 /// palabdher abhāvāsiddher ity arthād viruddhavi .. ne 'nupalabdhir eva prayu .. .. .. .iti / bhavatu nāmaivaṃvidhāyāyā dṛśyaviṣayā anupalabdheḥ sakāśād abhāvagatir ataś ceyaṃ pramāṇaṃ sā punaḥ katham anumānaṃ kiṃtu pramāṇāntaram eveti bhāvaḥ / kathaṃ vā na syād ity ācāryaḥ / dṛṣṭāntānapekṣaṇād iti paraḥ / dṛṣṭāntāpekṣaṃ hy anumānam anvayavyatirekava .. ///
body.translated_text: [2] ///...because absence is established through non-apprehension—the meaning is that in the case of the contradictory..., <s>anupalabdhi</s> (non-apprehension) alone is to be employed. Granted, let it be that from such <s>anupalabdhi</s>, which has a perceptible object, there arises cognition of absence; and hence this is a <s>pramāṇa</s> (means of valid cognition). But how then is it <s>anumāna</s> (inference)? Rather, it is simply a separate <s>pramāṇa</s> altogether—this is the intent. 'How could it not be [inference]?'—says the <s>Ācārya</s> (Master, i.e., <s>Dharmakīrti</s>). 'Because it does not depend on a <s>dṛṣṭānta</s> (example)'—says the opponent. For <s>anumāna</s> depends on a <s>dṛṣṭānta</s>, through <s>anvaya</s> (positive concomitance) and <s>vyatireka</s> (negative concomitance)... ///

body.text: 3 /// .. .. .. .. mānaṃ dṛṣṭāntānapekṣatām edva na hītyādinā prāha / asyām ity anupalabdhau kiṃ na nirupākhyam ityādi ācāryaḥ dṛṣṭānta evety arthaḥ / tad asad ityādi paraḥ / tad vyomakusumādi asad iti kathaṃ kena pramāṇenāvagantavyaṃ yenaivaṃ syāt* / anupalaabdher liṅgād abhāve sādhye dṛṣṭāntaḥ syād ity arthaḥ / anupalabdher eva liṅgād vyomakusumā ///
body.translated_text: [3] ///...<s>anumāna</s> (inference) does not depend on a <s>dṛṣṭānta</s> (example)—he states this with 'na hi' and so forth. 'In this'—i.e., in <s>anupalabdhi</s> (non-apprehension)—'is it not something unnameable (<s>nirupākhya</s>)?' and so forth—says the <s>Ācārya</s>; the meaning is: it is the <s>dṛṣṭānta</s> (example) itself. 'That is non-existent' and so forth—says the opponent. That [entity] such as a sky-flower (<s>vyomakusuma</s>) etc. is non-existent—how and by what <s>pramāṇa</s> (means of valid cognition) is this to be ascertained, such that it could be so? The meaning is: from the <s>liṅga</s> (logical mark) of <s>anupalabdhi</s> (non-apprehension), when absence is the <s>sādhya</s> (what is to be proved), there should be a <s>dṛṣṭānta</s> (example). From the <s>liṅga</s> of <s>anupalabdhi</s> alone, the sky-flower... ///

body.text: 4 /// .idyate dṛṣṭānto yasyā asattāsiddher iti vigrahaḥ / athātrāpy aparo dṛṣṭāntas tasyā vyomakusumādyasattāsiddheḥ sadṛṣṭāntatve vānavasthāprasaṃgaḥ / tatrāpy aparo dṛṣṭāntas tatrāpy aparo 'pīti kṛtvā / tathā cānavasthāyāṃ satyāṃ ekasyāpi siddhāv apratipattiḥ / sarvatra tasmād anavasthādoṣaparihārārthaṃ nirupākhya ///
body.translated_text: [4] ///...is ascertained as a <s>dṛṣṭānta</s> (example) for which the non-existence is established—this is the analysis. Now, if in this case too there is another <s>dṛṣṭānta</s> for establishing the non-existence of that sky-flower etc., and if that [example] also requires a [further] <s>dṛṣṭānta</s>, then there would be the fault of infinite regress (<s>anavasthā</s>)—in that case too another <s>dṛṣṭānta</s>, and in that case too yet another—and so on. And thus, when there is an infinite regress, there would be failure to establish even a single [case]; [this applies] everywhere. Therefore, in order to avoid the fault of infinite regress, the unnameable (<s>nirupākhya</s>)... ///

body.text: 5 /// .. labdhilakṣaṇaprāptasya anupalabdher ityādāv api prayoge dṛṣṭāntānapekṣaṇād ananumānam anupalabdhiḥ / śṛṇvann apīty ācāryaḥ / sakṛd uktaṃ yathā svabhāvānupalabdhau nābhāvaḥ sādhyate kiṃtu abhāvavyavahāra iti tacchṛṇvann api / mūrkhasya trīṇi nāmāni devo divyaḥ prajayatir ity ato devānāṃ mūrkhāṇāṃ pri .. ///
body.translated_text: [5] ///...of that which has attained the characteristic of non-apprehension—even in the application beginning with '<s>anupalabdhi</s>' etc., because it does not depend on a <s>dṛṣṭānta</s> (example), <s>anupalabdhi</s> (non-apprehension) is not <s>anumāna</s> (inference). 'Even hearing this'—says the <s>Ācārya</s>. It has been stated with reason: just as in <s>svabhāvānupalabdhi</s> (non-apprehension of the intrinsic nature), it is not absence that is established but rather the conventional practice of absence (<s>abhāvavyavahāra</s>)—even hearing that. 'A fool has three names: <s>deva</s> (god), <s>divya</s> (divine), <s>prajayati</s>'—therefore, of the gods, of fools, the dear... ///

body.text: 6 /// ..m evāsadvyavahāraṃ sādhyaṃ darśayann āha / nimittaṃ hītyādi / dṛśyasyānupalabdhir upalabhyānupalabdhiḥ / sā nimittaṃ kāraṇaṃ sadvyavahārāṇāṃ sānupalabdhiḥ svasannidhānād ātmanā sannidhānāt* / svanimittān* svam anupalabdhirūpa .. ///
body.translated_text: [6] ///...showing that precisely the conventional practice of non-existence (<s>asadvyavahāra</s>) is what is to be proved (<s>sādhya</s>), he says 'nimittaṃ hi' and so forth. The non-apprehension of the perceptible (<s>dṛśyasyānupalabdhi</s>) is <s>upalabhyānupalabdhi</s> (non-apprehension of the apprehensible). That is the cause (<s>nimitta</s>), the reason, for the conventional practices of existence—that non-apprehension, from its own proximity, by itself, from [its own] presence. From its own causes, its own form being that of non-apprehension... ///
